News.title: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
News.content:
A soldier in the US Army has been arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia, British counter-terror police have said.

The 41-year-old senior serviceman was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday.

Counter Terrorism Policing London said the man had been arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023.

Section one of the Act relates to obtaining or disclosing protected information, while section three relates to assisting a foreign intelligence service.

As part of the investigation, officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire.

The BBC understands the soldier was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire. The barracks serve as the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), a strategic operational base for the alliance.

Counter Terrorism Policing said it was not linked to any other ongoing investigations.

FBI director Kash Patel said in a statement: "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies."

He added: "While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message â this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners."

News.title: David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct after losing injunction bid
News.content:
One of the women who alleged Walliams "groomed" her as a teenager told BBC Newsnight she was "angry" at his behaviour.

Lilly Creightmore - who Walliams contacted when she was 18 - waived her right to anonymity.

Creightmore told Newsnight that a month after they first met, Walliams told her she "could move in with him and basically that I could be his flatmate".

She said that after she arrived to stay at his house she "felt instantly pressured to share a bed with him".

"In the evenings, he would sort of come and sit with me and stroke my leg, and one night I think he put his head in my lap and sort of be like, 'are you sure you don't want to come and sleep in my bed with me?' I had an inner strength like, 'no I'm not attracted to you in that way'... I felt I was being manipulated," she added.

She told Newsnight: "I am angry, I'm suppressing it well, but just that this culture of older men in positions of power needs to go, needs to stop. They're abusing their positions, using young people and abusing young people, and people of any age of course. There were too many men in power still, that are doing this and they need to go."

Walliams's lawyers told the ITV News and Guardian investigation that he denied grooming Creightmore or acting inappropriately. They added he did not "target" her because she was "vulnerable" or "young".

Walliams said he believed his friendship with Lilly was a "special one" and felt "devastated" by her account. He denied the offers of help or gifts were attempts to groom, manipulate or coerce her into sleeping with him.

Two women, given pseudonyms of Alex and Jade in the investigation, have alleged that they first had contact with Walliams when they were 15 years old.

Alex alleged that she met Walliams in 2004 at a fan event when she was 15. She claimed that she and Walliams stayed in touch over the next two years and they had consensual sex for the first time when she was 17, the report alleged.

News.title: Why Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed
News.content:
David Walliams' unprecedented legal battle not to be named in relation to allegations against him went downhill as he tried to secure a permanent injunction.

He was named by the Guardian and ITN because he had no sound legal reason to prevent the news organisations' investigation from being published. In response to the allegations included, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

The 55-year-old's bid for an injunction had been an open secret from the start after what would have normally been an anonymised application briefly appeared under his own name on a court cases register.

His exceptionally unusual attempt to gag the media - forever - became clear at the full trial last month - but that's when his bid to remain anonymous got worse.

In court, his lawyers did not claim that the investigation would be disclosing legally confidential or private information the journalists were not entitled to - two avenues often trod to silence reporters.

Instead lawyers for Walliams argued that such was the threat to his life from publication that the court itself would be breaching his human rights, were it to allow the story to go ahead.

This was, the court ultimately concluded, unheard of.

Under Article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights, the British state has a duty to take reasonable steps to try to protect life where they can do so and, importantly, where a particular body has an actual responsibility to do so.

There's no expectation that a state agency can save all lives in all circumstances - but it must show it has done its best if it is clear it had a responsibility to act.

The most obvious example of this law in practice is that the police must try to act on credible intelligence of a threat to life, even if the intended victim is a gangster.

But that duty, and how it should be applied in the real world, is also why Walliams lost: he was expecting the wrong public body to be doing the protecting.

The High Court's Mr Justice Nicklin said that the responsibility to try to protect the comedian and author's life was on clinicians and the hospital he had already been taken to. He had been detained for his own protection, meaning the state was already trying to meet its obligation to protect him from harm.

The court could not do that protecting because it had not taken responsibility for Walliams' psychiatric treatment or safety. Its role was to decide the legal dispute between Walliams and the news organisations.

Walliams' lawyers had suggested that there might be a right to private family life issue in the case but the judge said there had been no evidence to detail that, and he had to take into account the media's right to freedom of speech to publish what was described in court as a detailed investigation in the public interest.

If the media were wrong about their claims, Walliams could later sue for defamation - the way that any wrong party seeks redress against journalists.

News.title: Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up
News.content:
The dangers in Slovyansk are clear from the start.

"If I say run, you run," Tetiana tells us. She and her colleague Yasha are escorting us into a city now under constant bombardment from Russian drones, missiles and glide bombs.

It is raining and cloudy as we enter the city, and our military escorts call this "good" weather, meaning it is bad for drones.

But the threat is still there, and Yasha keeps his eyes peeled on the skies, while 21-year-old Tetiana scours her phone for the latest military intelligence on likely threats from the air.

They are members of a drone unit who call themselves Peaky Blinders and their distinctive emblem is a flat cap of the type made popular by the cult BBC TV series, although theirs are camouflaged.

Slovyansk is one of four cities that make up Ukraine's "fortress belt" - a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the parts of eastern region of Donetsk still under its control.

Russia wants Kyiv to give up the fortress cities and they are central to talks on a possible peace deal that have resumed after nine months between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi.

Ukrainians worry that doing so would make it much easier for Russia to advance further west, including to the capital Kyiv.

News.title: Train attack driver's '10 seconds' to change line
News.content:
The driver of a high-speed train where a mass stabbing took place said he had "probably about 10 seconds" to decide to switch to the slow line before making an unscheduled stop.

Andrew Johnson was driving the London-bound LNER service on 1 November last year when the train stopped at Huntingdon in Cambridgeshire.

Giving evidence, Johnson told jurors at Cambridge Crown Court he heard someone on the intercom "screaming 'there's a knifeman stabbing people'".

Anthony Williams, 33, of Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder on the train.

He is also charged with four other attempted murders following earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

News.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
News.content:
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.

One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.

Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.

A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother, Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.

Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.

Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.

In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.

"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."

The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.

"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.

"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."

The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.

"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."

The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line.

News.title: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
News.content:
Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affair between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.

Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation". The FBI is also conducting its own probe.

The company's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (Â£375bn) wiped of its stock market value since Friday.

Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, given it is the sole manufacturer of a computer chip used in AI tools.

It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials who are keen to win the AI race.

Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.

Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked.

Nvidia has also maintained that the US government did not inform it that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern.

News.title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP
News.content:
The next census should include more ethnicity options to allow people to define themselves as black English or Asian English, according to a group of MPs.

Liberal Democrat MP Josh Babarinde told the BBC that "most people" in the country believe "you don't have to be white to be English", as he called for the categories to be updated in a similar way to changes in Wales and Scotland.

At the 2021 census, the ethnic group section saw English offered only within the white category.

Babarinde's proposal, dubbed the "St George's Bill", aims to broaden the options and its supporters include Labour's David Lammy and Conservative Sir James Cleverly. It was tabled in the House of Commons on Tuesday.

In his speech to introduce his private member's bill (PMB), Babarinde told MPs he is a "proud Englishman" and has "proud Nigerian heritage".

He said: "But my parents and I were born in England, we grew up in England, our home is in England, yet some voices attempt to reduce Englishness to a skin colour and to a bloodline.

"Well, if we're going to go down that path, my mum's side of the family has been English for as far back as we have traced."

The Eastbourne MP said he had received "death threats for daring to say that you don't have to be white to be English".

He added "English ethnicity is real" before arguing it is a "matter of historical fact that it has never been one bloodline" and "even our Royal Family has German roots".

"Is the King not English either, I ask."

Addressing the ethnicity section of the census, Babarinde said the "only box that says English sits under the white category".

He added: "If you are black, the form offers you black British, if you are Asian, it offers you Asian British, but not English.

"Now, the same question in the Welsh census offers a black Welsh category. In Scotland, the census offers Scottish Asian, for example.

"Yet the best that England offers in our census is a miscellaneous write-in box that may as well be the margin."

Lammy, a former deputy prime minister, said in a statement: "It is quite absurd that neither I or my mixed heritage children can describe themselves as black or mixed race and English on our census form.

"I have long campaigned for us to change to the position enjoyed by others in Wales and Scotland. We have to end this backward racial gatekeeping."

News.title: Met Police investigating more 'potential criminal allegations' about Brand
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police have said several people contacted them during the trial and following the conviction and sentencing of the disgraced comedian Russell Brand, "to provide information or report a potential criminal allegation".

A Met spokesperson said: "Detectives are assessing this information as part of their ongoing enquiries."

Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Det Supt Andy Furphy, who led the Brand investigation, said officers were "looking at exactly what we've got" and "whether they're information that points to behaviour or whether they could constitute a criminal offence".

Brand is already being investigated over rape allegations from two more women. He has been interviewed under caution in connection to those allegations.

News.title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
News.content:
Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.

Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.

The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.

However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.

The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.

Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.

After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.

"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.

"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.

Sales of tinned and jarred goods rose from Â£58.2m in the 10 days to 2 November 2025 to Â£79.5m over the same period in 2026.

Bottled water sales jumped from Â£13.6m to Â£22.8m compared with a year earlier and hand sanitiser sales climbed from Â£497,000 to Â£908,000.

News.title: Carrick's Man Utd future to be decided as Berrada and Wilcox retain support
News.content:
Looking back, the 48 hours before United's season-opening match at Hull were pivotal.

With Benjamin Sesko still trying to ease his way back from the shin issue that ended his previous campaign early, Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out for seven weeks. It meant Carrick was deprived of his first-choice striking alternative, with Bryan Mbeumo having to play on the right of the attack.

Carrick instead turned to Matheus Cunha, whose preference for dropping deep took him into the spaces captain Bruno Fernandes likes to occupy.

It neutralised United's attack on a day they seemed ill-prepared to meet the physical challenge of an opponent motivated by their long-awaited Premier League return.

In his role as interviewer for Nordic broadcaster Viaplay, former Norway and Middlesbrough striker Jan Aage Fjortoft later claimed United had lacked passion - something Carrick dismissed as "ridiculous".

"It's one game," Carrick told the media afterwards.

The following week, United were losing to Ipswich - another newly promoted side. Only a slip from Marcelino Nunez inside his own half allowed Cunha to tee up Fernandes for an undeserved equaliser.

The Portugal playmaker, who had just been crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26, went on to complete a hat-trick in a 5-2 win.

He has scored just once - a penalty against Villa on Sunday - in the league since.

After the Ipswich win came a trip to Everton.

Twice United led, the second occasion when Sesko struck two minutes from full-time after coming on as a substitute. Deep into stoppage time, Ainsley Maitland-Niles drove home from long range to deny the visitors.

Asked how confident he was in his side's ability to react to a disappointing start to the season, Carrick snapped back: "It's not been that bad."

What happened next, however, was.

Time and again, United's fitness was called into question. They struggled badly against a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men in the first half before their rivals benefited from an Erling Haaland goal that referees' chief Howard Webb later admitted should not have stood.

Carrick's complaints were justified - but they masked a poor performance from his team.

After taking a 2-0 lead inside 10 minutes against Brighton in the EFL Cup, United were outplayed and beaten, thanks to two goals in four second-half minutes.

The fine margins United benefited from during Carrick's interim spell were now going against them, and his coaching staff - lauded months earlier - could not find an answer.

Carrick called Cunha's injury-time equaliser against a Fulham side who started the game bottom of the table a positive to build on. But immediately after the international break, United were held to another draw - conceding in injury time to an out-of-form and 10-man Tottenham.

The whirlwind was starting to pick up strength.

Lisandro Martinez, who scored an own goal against Fulham, was at fault for Spurs' leveller, which made his post-match outburst after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid more amazing.

The Argentina defender criticised United's summer recruitment and placed the blame at the door of "the technical director" - Wilcox.

By the time of Martinez's outburst, Sesko and left-back Luke Shaw were injured. Marcus Rashford has not played since. The rotation at left-back that eventually led to Carrick starting five different players in that role was in full swing.

After conceding in the opening minute against Atletico, Como scored inside the first two in a 4-1 Champions League defeat for United. Fernandes came out afterwards and criticised Carrick's tactics.

He was dropped for the Bournemouth game, but returned as captain at Chelsea. United were beaten in both matches.

With just three wins in 15 matches in all competitions this season and United stuck in 18th in the Premier League, Carrick is set to pay the price.

News.title: More than 12 US military aircraft leave second UK base
News.content:
Retired Royal Air Force Air Marshal Greg Bagwell told BBC Verify "we need to keep an open mind" about the reasons behind the US aircraft movements.

He suggested they could be the result of an exercise, or because the weather forecast meant it was safer to move the aircraft to other bases ahead of planned deployments elsewhere.

Bagwell said the decision may also have been taken because of a hoax as part of "nuisance hybrid warfare" by countries like Iran - or it could be a genuine threat.

He said the aircraft being dispersed to several bases could indicate the US was spreading them around to keep them safe and the moves have been "triggered by something".

Bagwell added that the reason "we haven't seen an attack succeed or even happen" could be that "maybe our intelligence and our security is better than people might believe".

Monday's departures from Mildenhall follow a security incident at RAF Fairford, a US-operated airbase in Gloucestershire.

A major incident was declared after three suspicious vans were seen near that base in September. It later emerged that the US had pulled its bombers from there and returned them to America.

Two British nationals appeared in court in October in connection with an alleged Iran-linked plot.

Seven men have been arrested as part of the investigation, Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed to the BBC on Tuesday, while an eighth has been interviewed under caution and since charged under Section 3 of the National Security Act 2023.

Iran has previously said that it considered UK bases used by the US for military strikes to be "legitimate targets".

Additional reporting by Nick Johnson at RAF Mildenhall, and Rob Corp, BBC Verify.

News.title: Seven in hospital after car 'mounts pavement' in Glasgow
News.content:
Seven people have been taken to hospital after they were struck by a car in the west end of Glasgow.

Police Scotland said the driver was assessed by paramedics and treated at the scene of the incident, which happened at about 15:45 on Hyndland Road.

Unconfirmed reports suggest the vehicle mounted the pavement, hit a bus stop shelter and then struck scaffolding before coming to a halt.

A force spokesperson said: "Officers remain in attendance and inquiries are ongoing into the incident which is being treated as a road traffic collision."

News.title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest
News.content:
The coroner asked what kind of response Edkins hoped for from the school.

Edkins said: "I would have thought just being a bit more compassionate and understanding towards someone struggling with self-esteem - for Taylor to receive a bit more compassion and understanding around that time."

A lawyer for Lee's family asked principal Rachel Hutchinson if this was a missed opportunity to consider the impact of the new behaviour policy on students like him. Hutchinson agreed it was.

Hutchinson said she felt Lee's SEND needs were "competently met" by the school, adding Lee "struggled with the culture" the leadership was trying to create.

Lee's mother, Michelle Lee, raised her concerns on 6 November 2023 about the number of resets and reflections he was being given.

If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line.

Richard Brooks, a youth worker who met Lee several times in the autumn term, told the inquest he seemed "unhappy" and "apprehensive".

He said Lee told him "every day [at school] was a battle and it's exhausting".

The inquest heard that, in the month before Lee died, he broke down in tears at school on 2 October and told a member of staff he had self-harmed and was thinking about suicide.

Asked by the coroner what action the school took after this disclosure, Hutchinson said they contacted his parents and "kept a closer eye on him".

But the coroner concluded there was no evidence Lee's teachers were informed he had self-harmed or was having suicidal thoughts.

The family's counsel said Lee was "highly intelligent" and a "talented musician" who enjoyed spending time with his friends and skateboarding.

The inquest heard his parents found him unconscious in his bedroom. He died on 18 November 2023.

Longhorn concluded that, while Lee had experienced mental health issues for some time, his treatment at school and what he saw as unfair school sanctions had the most significant impact on his mood.

News.title: US pilot arrested at Heathrow admits drugs offence
News.content:
An American pilot has admitted possessing cocaine after being arrested at Heathrow Airport earlier this month.

Wayne Sigler, 64, from Louisiana, was detained by police on Sunday 1 November and appeared at Uxbridge Magistrates Court on Saturday. After pleading guilty to the possession offence he was placed into custody, the Metropolitan Police confirmed.

He has also been charged with being drunk or unfit to fly while flying or working on an aircraft - two offences that fall under the Railway and Transport Act 2003.

He is due appear for his next hearing at Isleworth Crown Court on 7 December.

Police have not specified which company the pilot was working for when he was arrested.

Heathrow Airport has declined to comment.

News.title: Stevie Wonder leaves cafe staff £1,000 tip after Manchester gig
News.content:
Staff at a Greater Manchester cafe found themselves sharing a Â£1,000 tip after a late-night visit from a musical legend.

Cafe Continental in Stalybridge found itself feeding Stevie Wonder, his band and entourage after the singer's sold-out gig performing his classic album Songs In The Key Of Life at the Co-op Live in Manchester.

Owner Ryan Robinson said Wonder, 76, was "a really nice guy, happy to chat to everybody".

Among those dining was Wonder's daughter and backing singer Aisha, about whom he wrote Isn't She Lovely? for the album.

Robinson said he had been contacted about 18 months ago by members of the band, who called in while playing in soul singer Toni Braxton's backing band.

They stayed in touch, and then on Sunday, Robinson got a call to ask if they could come back after the show.

"The band turned up at 23:00 had some food and then at about 00:30, four blacked out mini buses turned up outside, and Stevie Wonder was in one of them," he said.

The cafe staff had been forewarned that they would need to work late and put on a different menu to the usual Sunday roast.

The singer had a seaside feast with grilled sea bream, bouillabaisse and octopus.

And the staff's efforts were rewarded with the generous tip from Wonder and his band.

"That was first for everyone," Robinson said, adding: "His family, his entourage and his crew are absolutely lovely.

"You wouldn't even think they were famous and they're really enthusiastic about the restaurant."

News.title: Kennedy family members ask a judge to block Trump's Arlington memorial arch
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty asked a judge Tuesday to block President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 250-foot (76-meter) structure would cast a shadow over their relatives' gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery.

The shadow would “fundamentally alter the experience of visiting the gravesites,” the relatives argued. They filed a motion to intervene in two existing lawsuits seeking to block construction of the arch.

U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan last week prohibited the Trump administration from breaking ground on the structure for 14 days.

The nine Kennedy family members who filed suit are children and grandchildren of Robert F. Kennedy and Edward M. Kennedy, brothers of the slain U.S. president John F. Kennedy, both of whom served in the U.S. Senate. They are buried close to the eternal flame that marks JFK's gravesite, a trio of memorials that are a major draw for the millions of people who visit the Arlington cemetery each year.

Building the arch would be a “permanent denigration” of the gravesites, and the Kennedy offspring “would never again be able to appreciate both sites as they always have before, and as the Kennedy family always intended," lawyers for the relatives wrote. They are represented by veteran Washington lawyer Norm Eisen and Democracy Defenders Fund.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump's health and human services secretary who has a fractured relationship with many of his relatives, did not join the lawsuit.

The arch is one of several projects around Washington that the Republican president has undertaken as he alters the capital to his tastes — from renovating one of its storied public golf courses to threatening to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. Those projects could soon face intense scrutiny after Democrats gained control of Congress in the midterm elections this week.

The White House last week unveiled a glitzy new website to showcase the arch, which is slated to rise in a mass of gold ornamentation and stately gray granite between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

News.title: The free weekly activity that could boost children's mental health
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Regular weekly trips to the local park could support better mental health in children as they grow, new research has suggested.

In research called the Children of the 90s Study, experts from the University of Exeter examined data on 4,219 children from the ages of four to 11. T

hose experts emphasised that communities require "good quality parks that are safe, accessible and welcoming to families from all backgrounds".

Social-emotional progress was tracked using questionnaires, completed by the children's parents, across five distinct stages of their childhoods.

The study revealed that youngsters visiting parks at least once a week showed enhanced social-emotional development compared to those who went less often.

This finding was attributed to "physical activity, cognitive benefits, social interaction, parent- child interaction and bonding, and play opportunities", the team determined.

The study revealed that youngsters visiting parks at least once a week showed enhanced social-emotional development ( Getty/iStock )

Mark Ferguson, of the University of Exeter, said: “Our research suggests encouraging children to visit parks and playgrounds at least once a week could be a practical way to support their emotional wellbeing, social skills and mental health.

“But for this to work fairly, communities need good-quality parks that are safe, accessible and welcoming to families from all backgrounds.

“Parks give children space to be physically active, which is known to support mental and physical health, as well as helping adventurous and imaginative play to build confidence and independence. We believe parks could be more than places to play, but an important resource for children’s healthy development.”

Reacting to the findings, which are published in Epidemiology and Community Health, Paul Noblet, interim head of external affairs and research at the charity YoungMinds, said: “We know how important community spaces such as parks and playgrounds can be in supporting mental health, and addressing the increasing isolation and loneliness young people today feel.

“Many spaces where young people can connect and build relationships have disappeared from communities across the country. This is a trend that we need to urgently reverse.

“Free, safe and accessible spaces are vital in our communities can help young people make friends, build confidence and develop a sense of belonging, all of which supports mental health.”

News.title: Government must go 'further and faster' to ensure Britain is ready for war in 1,000 days, peers warn
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Burnham’s Government needs to move "further and faster" to prepare the UK for the possibility of war within 1,000 days, a group of peers has warned.

Industry will be unable to "move quickly enough" to safeguard Britain unless the Government alters its "buyer-seller" relationship with commercial firms and urges regulators to strip away "overly prescriptive" rules, the Lords Industry and Regulators Committee cautioned.

In a report published on Wednesday, the committee stated that investors must also be given "more certainty" regarding the timeline and nature of contracts to enable funds to flow.

Peers called for a "significant shift in the culture" at the Ministry of Defence, arguing the department has "too often focused on the comfort blanket of following process rather than delivering capability at speed."

Setting out a series of recommendations, the committee stated the ministry should become "more comfortable" with accepting risk when procuring capabilities and consider a broader range of factors when determining value for money, rather than focusing solely on low costs.

open image in gallery Wes Streeting said the satellite will enable the UK to see threats sooner (PA) ( PA Wire )

It comes after the Defence Secretary warned that Britain must be ready for war in 1,000 days as Russia ramps up its hybrid warfare against Nato.

Writing in The Telegraph last month, Mr Streeting warned Britain’s adversaries could be ready to attack the UK in 2030.

“When procuring innovative capabilities, the Government should consider funding a number of companies working on the same problem to ensure greater industrial resilience and capacity,” the report said.

“Much of the bureaucracy and process in defence procurement was intended to reduce the risk of wasting public money. This has slowed down procurement without obviously reducing waste.

“The Ministry of Defence must become more comfortable with greater flexibility and risk in its procurement of new capabilities, accepting that the finished product might not be as initially envisaged, that failure can be instructive, and that speed can be more important than cost management.”

Peers also called on the Prime Minister to reinforce promises from Defence Secretary Wes Streeting to provide cover for officials to take greater risks, with a “strategic statement on defence to ensure industry is able to provide UK defence readiness”.

“If the Government continues its arm’s-length, buyer-seller relationship with industry delivering against detailed and prescriptive technical specifications, industry will not be able to move quickly enough to exploit fast-developing technology or to protect the UK in the event of war,” the report said.

“The Ministry of Defence must improve its ability to work with the defence industry on a quicker, more informal basis to improve outcomes. It should consult earlier in process, before requirements become fixed.”

open image in gallery Chancellor John Healey committed the Government to spending 3% of economic output on defence by 2030 in his November budget ( Getty )

The committee welcomed the Government’s adoption of the 2025 strategic defence review’s recommendation of a new partnership with industry and said its recommendations focus on “where the Government must go further and faster”.

Chancellor John Healey committed the Government to spending 3% of economic output on defence by 2030 in his November budget and said next year’s spending review would plot a course to reach the target.

Baroness Hayter, chair of the Industry and Regulators Committee said: “Last year the Strategic Defence Review called for a new relationship between government and the defence industry to reflect the urgency of rebuilding the UK’s defence strength to meet the challenges and changing nature of warfare demonstrated so clearly by the war in Ukraine.

“Whilst we welcome recognition of the need for change within the Ministry of Defence, it must accelerate, embrace new technologies and enhance the role of SMEs (small and medium-sized enterprises), whilst ensuring the skilled workforce needed to deliver this change.

“With ongoing threats from Russia and other malign actors, the Government must show the necessary leadership and move at pace to achieve the Defence Secretary’s target of being ready for action within 1,000 days and use the December 1 Defence Investment Summit to provide certainty to business to drive the new partnership forward.”

A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: “This Government is delivering the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the Cold War, investing almost £300 billion to transform our Armed Forces to warfighting readiness to keep Britain safe.

“We are driving reforms to deliver capability faster, secure better value for money, and strengthen the UK defence industrial base.

“This includes increasing spending with SMEs by £2.5 billion and our Office for Small Business Growth is reducing barriers to entry, helping more SMEs win defence contracts and backing British firms.”

News.title: The UK's ‘happiest place to live’ where homes have an average price tag of £1m
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An annual survey has named Richmond upon Thames the happiest place to live in Britain – but moving there comes at a price.

While the borough offers residents glimpses at roaming deer, easy access to central London and the chance to stroll down Thames pathways, the average asking price for a home there exceeds £1 million.

More than 24,000 people responded to Rightmove’s 15th annual “happy at home index” study, which placed Harrogate in North Yorkshire second and Cirencester in Gloucestershire third.

Monmouth was the highest ranked place in Wales, while Kirkcaldy took the top spot in Scotland.

Skipton in North Yorkshire, last year's winner, ranked seventh in this year's study and remained among Britain's 10 happiest places to live.

Richmond upon Thames, famed for its links to hit TV series Ted Lasso, has returned to number one after previously winning in 2023 and finishing second last year.

The leafy London borough ranked particularly highly across several aspects of local life, including access to nature and green spaces, essential local services, shops and restaurants, employment opportunities and desirable jobs, as well as residents' pride in their area, Rightmove said.

Meanwhile, Harrogate also ranked highly for access to nature and green spaces, as well as residents' agreement with the statement: “I can be myself,” according to the research.

Richmond upon Thames, famed for its links to hit TV series Ted Lasso , has returned to number one after previously winning in 2023 and finishing second last year ( Getty/iStock )

Across Britain, four-fifths (81 per cent) of people who took part in the survey said they are happy with where they live.

Colleen Babcock, a property expert at Rightmove, said: "Richmond stands out for offering a combination many people value: easy access to nature and green spaces, without having to give up local services, places to eat and shop, or employment opportunities.

"That balance between greenery and everyday convenience runs through the wider findings.

"Even among people who would ideally choose a rural setting, access to amenities, parks and public transport remains important.

“This year’s results suggest that the places people rate most highly aren’t simply urban or rural, but often bring together some of the best elements of both.”

People participated in the study after being emailed via Rightmove's database, so the survey was self-selecting.

Mayor of Richmond upon Thames, Councillor Nancy Baldwin, said: "This recognition is especially meaningful because residents highlighted their pride in the local area, our beautiful parks and green spaces, and the local services they rely on every day.

“Above all, it is our people and communities that make Richmond special.”

Amy Reynolds, head of sales at estate agent Antony Roberts, said: "Families are drawn to Richmond for its excellent schools and green spaces, and they stay for the strong sense of community.

"With Richmond Park and the Thames on the doorstep, a thriving town centre and plenty of places to eat, shop and spend time, it offers a quality of life that's hard to match in London.

“Add in the easy journey into central London, and it’s easy to see why people are so happy to call Richmond home.”

Graham Price, director at Randall Price, said: "What makes Richmond upon Thames such a happy place to live is the balance it offers.

"There's a real sense of community, plenty going on locally, and people can enjoy the best of both worlds: a great place to call home while still feeling well connected.

“It’s the kind of area people put down roots in, and once they’re here, many don’t want to leave.”

News.title: Prince George contributes colourful drawing to Prince William's special edition of Country Life
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A drawing of a kingfisher by Prince George appears in a special edition of Country Life that has been guest edited by his father, the Prince of Wales.

The 13-year-old's colourful picture of the bird, perched on a branch, takes pride of place in this week's 300-page bumper issue of the magazine.

Prince William has spent the past six months preparing the collectors' edition, which goes on sale on Wednesday.

George is said to enjoy drawing, and created the artwork at home in the spring, when he was 12.

He appears to be following in the footsteps of his grandfather King Charles, who is a keen artist.

His mother Catherine, the Princess of Wales, studied art at A-level and history of art at university.

open image in gallery Prince George has contributed a drawing of a kingfisher for a special edition of Country Life ( Matt Porteous/Kensington Palace )

In 2025, Kate and her children released portrait sketches they drew of each other after spending time together being creative.

The four images were drawn in a variety of mediums from charcoal to ink, but no details were released about who drew each one.

Kate has also given a rare interview to the magazine, and is said to have discussed the healing power of nature.

William also talks about family walks with the Waleses' dogs Orla and Otto, and how George and his siblings, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, love to get out and explore.

He recalls growing up at the King's Gloucestershire retreat Highgrove, and having to remember not to open the curtains before getting dressed as the garden was often filled with visitors.

He also tells of his fondness for a visit to the pub for a chat and a pint of cider with ice.

open image in gallery William and George at an Aston Villa game ( Getty )

He admits his support for his “second family”, Aston Villa, has become “fanatical”.

Villa manager Unai Emery features in the magazine talking about leadership, and also discusses the importance of William's support for the club.

“It’s fantastic for us. If we can give him good news, good results or good moments in football, we are proud of it,” Emery says in a video released to mark the publication.

William, a major landowner through his Duchy of Cornwall estate, opens up about his commitment to the countryside.

In the magazine's leader column, he writes: "The places you love best are not the ones you preserve unchanged, but the ones you keep quietly improving.

“One day, George, Charlotte and Louis may ask me what I did to help communities thrive … we didn’t simply imagine a better future, we helped build it, so that someone else could build further still.”

He sets out his countryside champions, choosing wildlife rangers and curlew conservationists.

open image in gallery William says he and his family love getting out in nature ( AFP/Getty )

He also picks Groove Armada star Andy Cato, who is now a regenerative farmer, and next generation farming students who studied at Duchy College in Cornwall.

The prince also shares his weakness for chocolate biscuit cake, first served to him by his grandmother the late Queen Elizabeth.

William chose the no-bake treat as his wedding cake when he and Kate married in 2011.

The future head of the armed forces also uses the magazine to set out his drive to make sure women in the military feel safe, respected and valued.

Behind the scenes over the past year, the heir to the throne has been on a fact-finding mission, carrying out private and public meetings with servicewomen of all ranks from the Royal Navy, the RAF and the Army as a priority, to learn first hand about their experiences.

Mark Hedges, Country Life's editor-in-chief, described the prince as a “formidable, hands-on guest editor”.

William is the latest member of the royal family to edit the publication, after the King, Queen Camilla and the Princess Royal.

News.title: Ads for four brands banned over ‘misleading’ carbon neutral delivery claims
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ads for Grind Coffee, SportShoes.com, ProCook and toilet paper brand Who Gives a Crap have been banned for making “misleading” claims about their carbon neutral or carbon positive deliveries.

In all four cases, the ads made claims that the delivery of products was either “carbon neutral” or “carbon positive”.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) found that the ads failed to make clear that carbon neutral delivery relied on offsetting credits rather than actively reducing emissions.

A video about recycled toilet paper brand Who Gives a Crap’s history included text in the ad’s caption stating “carbon neutral shipping”, later explaining to the ASA that consumers could now click on a link to a page that explained the basis of the claim.

An ad for Grind, also seen in June, said “Coffee From The Grind Roastery, Delivered To Your Door Each Month. Carbon Positive Delivery.”

Banning the ad, the ASA said it had “reminded Grind to ensure that they made the basis of all environmental claims clear, including in relation to what extent any ‘Carbon Positive Delivery’ claims depended on the use of offsetting credits or the actual removal of any source of emissions”.

The banned ad for SportsShoes.com said: “Over 12,000 products on site from a wide range of brands … Carbon Neutral Deliveries” while kitchenware brand ProCook offered “Next Day Delivery Available – Carbon Neutral Delivery.”

The ASA said: “Environmental claims must be made clear and supported by evidence. If ads leave out important information, they can risk misleading people.”

Justine Grimley, investigations manager at the ASA, said: “Carbon neutral or net zero claims can mislead if it’s not clear what they actually mean or how they’ve been achieved.

“Where these claims rely on carbon offsetting, this must be made clear so that people don’t think what’s being advertised produces no or few emissions.

“We’ll continue to take action when these types of claims are misleading or lack the information people need to make informed decisions when it comes to making greener choices.”

Ted Robinson, chief of staff at Grind Coffee, said: “Since May 2020 we’ve offset the carbon from our deliveries through Shopify Planet and its precursor Shopify Offset. Both of these are schemes that use shipment weight and distance to estimate emissions, and then fund carbon removal.

“Since then, we’ve funded the carbon removal of over a million orders through the Shopify Planet scheme and we’re in the top 0.2% of all contributors to the programme.

“Previously we had referred to this as ‘carbon positive delivery’, but we felt it was a bit confusing – so more recently we call this carbon neutral delivery.

“As you’ll see in the ruling, the issue that the ASA challenged was whether the ad made the basis of the claim ‘Carbon Positive Delivery’ clear.

“The challenge was not that we weren’t able to substantiate the claim, but rather that we didn’t explain it fully in the ad. We’ve since updated our website with a clear definition of ‘carbon neutral delivery.’

News.title: Parents back to choosing toys for fun over educational value as market soars
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Parents are returning to buying toys for fun rather than educational value amid the fastest growth in the market for more than a decade, the industry has said.

Britons bought 38 million more toys in the year to September, up 17% to 257 million on the previous year, according to industry data analyst Circana.

The UK toy market grew 13% in value over the year to reach £2.64 billion, the fastest growth rate in more than 10 years.

The figures come as the DreamToys list of the predicted 15 top sellers this Christmas – selected by a panel of independent toy retailers and experts – is unveiled, ranging from the Mini Brands Really Works Vinyl Playset, a miniature record player that spins and plays music, to Mattel’s Hot Wheels Ultimate Garage, a multi-level track playset.

open image in gallery 11 toys at the Toy Retailers Association DreamToys exhibition at the House of Fine Art in Mayfair, London (Nicholas Warren/PA) ( PA Wire )

Also making the list are collectibles like squishy fidget toys NeeDoh and Clickeez Bubble Pops Keyboard, a keyboard-shaped collector’s case and toy set.

Lego’s Creator 3-in-1 Pirate Ship which allows for the building of three different models using the same set of bricks and action figure Beyblades Sneak Attack Battle Set are expected to be favourites this Christmas, while Pokémon is back with its Trading Card Game: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box, which marks three decades since the brand was first created in 1996.

Meanwhile, research suggests that fun has overtaken educational value to become the primary driver of parents’ toy purchasing decisions, according to market intelligence company The Insights Family.

The research found that children’s weekend playtime with toys and games is up 10% on last year, and one in five parents of children aged three to nine say the chance to play together as a family influences what they buy.

The Insights Family said this was reflected in the list with the furReal Gabby the Grow & Roar Tiger, an interactive plush that transforms from a cub into a larger tiger, and the Primal Hatch Megalodon, a water activated robotic shark.

Gui Gui Mega Slime Haul, a sensory slime play kit, the KPop Demon Hunters Singing Fashion Dolls and the PAW Patrol Megasaurus Dino Vehicle have made the list.

Tom Williams, chief executive at The Insights Family, said: “These findings highlight the important role toys continue to play in children’s lives and the evolving priorities of families when it comes to choosing what to buy.

“Fun is now the leading factor in parents’ toy-buying decisions, overtaking educational value, while value for money and the potential for toys to be played with repeatedly are also increasingly important.

“Parents are choosing toys that are entertaining, empowering and deliver a sense of creativity and achievement.”

Melissa Symonds, executive director of UK toys at Circana, said: “Last December, more than 1,300 toys were flying off shelves every minute during the busiest shopping week, and with sales already well ahead of last year, retailers will be hoping for another bumper festive season.”

Paul Reader, chairman of the DreamToys selection panel at the Toy Retailers Association, said: “2026 has been incredible for the UK toy market, with growth reaching levels we haven’t seen in more than a decade.

“What’s particularly encouraging is that this isn’t being driven by one product or category.

“This year’s DreamToys list celebrates the toy market’s diversity and the products we expect to be high on children’s wish lists this Christmas. From toys that spark imagination and creativity to those that bring families together, the list reflects the incredible variety of play experiences available today.”

News.title: Gaza floods are an “immediate humanitarian emergency”, warns Trump’s Board of Peace
News.content:
Donald Trump’s Board of Peace has accused Israel of an “insufficient” response to deadly floods that have hit the Gaza Strip.

In a rare statement, the US-led body, charged with ending war in Gaza and rebuilding the Strip, called on Israel “to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies”.

“The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency,” they said on Monday.

The Board has been pushing Israel for at least a month to speed up its “winterisation” policies so that residents in Gaza are better able to withstand the coldest months of the year.

The statement followed a weekend of torrential rain and winds that battered the decimated territory’s displacement camps, causing widespread flooding, landslides and several deaths.

A mother and her three young children were killed when a sand dune collapsed onto their tent in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. The children, aged four, five and eight died on Sunday. Their mother also suffocated under the sand.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

Sports.title: Hill insists Ferrari should back 'extraordinary' Hamilton over Leclerc
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 world champion Damon Hill has insisted Ferrari should back the "extraordinary" Lewis Hamilton over his team-mate Charles Leclerc if they want to have a chance of winning next year's drivers' title.

Ferrari's handling of their drivers came under increased scrutiny earlier this month following the Mexico City Grand Prix when a first-lap clash between Hamilton and Leclerc, running in first and second respectively at the time, cost the Italian team a likely one-two, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen going on to win the race.

Hamilton, who had started on pole and led on the approach to the first corner, was highly critical of Leclerc after the race for what he perceived to be an overly aggressive approach against a team-mate. Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur also expressed his displeasure at the incident.

The seven-time world champion said any issues he had with Leclerc had been "squashed" following a conversation at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, which came the weekend after the race in Mexico.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive a dramatic opening lap as Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was given a five-second penalty after overtaking Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Hill, the 1996 world champion, wrote on social media following the race in Mexico that Italian squad should make Hamilton their number one driver for the 2027 season and that "Lewis will deliver for Ferrari if they back him 100 per cent."

Appearing on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show following the triple-header of races, Hill explained his position.

"They [Ferrari] have invested all this in Lewis, they've got him on board, he is a massive name in the sport," the 1996 world champion said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show, Damon Hill says that Ferrari needs to settle a 'political problem' regarding if the team should be built around Lewis Hamilton.

"If they have a competitive car next year, they could win the Drivers' Championship and the Constructors' Championship, and I can't see how they're going to win it if they have two drivers currently behaving the way they do, if Charles is constantly racing against Lewis like that.

"So, you have to make a decision as a team principal how you're going to enter into the fray. And I think it makes sense to me to put all your eggs behind Lewis.

"You've got him there anyway. You've gone through all the pain and the investment to get him there. It would be a huge story, clearly. His eighth world title is just sitting there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton has criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari a likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix.

"Now Charles might say, well, this is totally unfair, you know, I've been here longer. But yes, you have been there longer, but look at the results.

"Lewis has got a valid point, which is he's there to make them win as a team, not just be a Ferrari driver."

'Hamilton has rebuilt himself after being crushed by 2021 title loss'

After claiming the most recent of his seven titles in 2020, Hamilton was controversially denied a record eighth triumph as he lost out to Max Verstappen at the final race of the 2021 season.

That coincided with a drop-off in performance for the Mercedes team that Hamilton had won six of his seven titles with, which ultimately played a part in the Brit deciding to make a blockbuster switch to Ferrari for the 2025 season.

Hamilton's last campaign with Mercedes and first with Ferrari suggested he was on the decline as he was outperformed by former team-mate George Russsell and then Leclerc, but he has returned to form in 2026.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the most heated clashes between Ferrari team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc this season.

With the all-new cars for this season appearing to better suit him, Hamilton claimed his first grand prix victory for Ferrari in Barcelona to reignite hope he could once more contend for the title.

Leclerc, who spent just one season at Sauber before joining Ferrari as a 21-year-old, has claimed nine grand prix wins across his eight campaigns with the Italian team.

Hill added: "I think there's a gravitas that Lewis has. I mean, don't forget what he was like last year. He was crushed.

"He's been crushed since Abu Dhabi, in effect, you know, in 2021. He's been fighting his way back. He's performed incredibly well this year, much better than I thought, considering I thought it was going to be very difficult, but he's rebuilt himself.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two,

"He is an extraordinary individual. And I think he has, and he's got pole positions and won races this year in a Ferrari. Who would have said that was possible last year?

"And I think we need to settle this in the team because there's a political problem in that team. For me, it seems like there's factions within the team that are shooting for one side or the other.

"You can't have that if you're going to be an effective competitor against the Red Bulls, McLaren and Mercedes."

Davidson: Number one status has to be earned

Sky Sports F1 pundit Anthony Davidson, appearing on The F1 Show alongside Hill, questioned whether Hamilton has earned number one status over Leclerc at Ferrari.

Hamilton is fourth in the 2026 drivers' standings, a place ahead of Leclerc with just 12 points separating the pair.

Davidson compared the situation to that of Verstappen at Red Bull, where the four-time world champion has long received preferential treatment over his team-mates.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc says he's 'settled' feud with Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton after their clash in last week's Mexico City GP.

Davidson said: "Do you think, though, with Red Bull, that it's not like they give Max better equipment? He has, without question, earned that status in the team through his dominance of lap times alone.

"And it's pretty much every time. A bit like [Michael] Schumacher did against either [Rubens] Barrichello or [Felipe] Massa or [Eddie] Irvine.

"It was just every time he is unbeatable. And you earn that. You have to earn that status.

"I'm not comfortable with the fact, thinking of Charles, the speed he had particularly last year. I wouldn't be comfortable with the fact if you just say the number one in the team is Lewis and Charles, no matter where he is, you finish behind.

"That doesn't sit easy with me. I think to a certain degree, you have to earn that status in the team."

Sports.title: Reynolds: Fearless Love can lead Packers to Super Bowl
Sports.content:
I'm well aware that we've only reached the halfway point of the 2026 season and so much can change in the NFL, especially at the back end of the year.

But I'm now starting to believe the Green Bay Packers can make a serious run and they have emerged as true contenders in the NFC.

Sunday's 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in Foxborough was a statement victory and it was a win that showed the Packers to be a complete team.

Jordan Love is playing as well as any quarterback in the NFL this season and he backed it up on Sunday on a big stage in a game being called by Tom Brady as he threw for 372 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

He could not look more comfortable right now. He's in his bag, he's playing with confidence, he's playing calmly and it looks like he has no fear.

That's what's incredible when you look at the success of Jordan Love. It's not dinking and dunking, it is attacking downfield at a more prolific rate than any other quarterback in the NFL.

And he has the guys that can make the plays on the other end. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson both went over 150 receiving yards on Sunday and they both have emerged as true game-breaking wide receivers.

Now you could say that Golden went into Week Nine leading the NFL with seven drops but then look at some of the catches he's tried to make. Again I think it goes back to that aggressive nature of the Packers.

So it wasn't that long ago we looked at the Packers with four or five wide receiver targets and said they've got a collection of players but they don't have a true number one. Well they might have something approaching two number ones now in Watson and Golden.

Defensively I felt like they've been dangerous all year and they showed it on Sunday, pouncing early for the interception of Drake Maye - who regressed on a huge stage. Of all the days for Drake Maye to have a nightmare, Tom Brady's calling the game up in the booth - a reminder of the gigantic shoes to fill in New England.

But this is what the Packers do on defense. They rush the passer really well. They harass teams into mistakes and then they are opportunistic. Four takeaways on Sunday was no fluke.

What they did in Foxborough was what they've done all season long, and they still have one of the most prolific pass rushers in the game to return providing Micah Parsons comes back at full speed.

He has taken his time coming back from the knee injury and should be targeting a Thanksgiving week (3:03) return to action.

If that boost comes at the right time then I think the Packers have all the tools to make a serious run come January and I think they're more than capable, based on what we've seen in the last couple of weeks, of extending that run all the way into February and you know what that means - the Super Bowl.
