“If it’s me, I hope they would do the same. And if it’s any other person, I would do the same. I would respect it. But you can’t call for a coalition, then disagree if you don’t follow your part,” he said.

He cautioned, however, against replacing the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration with another government that would reproduce the same governance failures.

“We don’t want to replace the APC or the present administration with someone who would take us back again,” he said.

Duke alleges obstacles to opposition campaigns

The former governor also accused the ruling APC of enjoying an overwhelming advantage in campaign visibility, alleging that opposition parties were struggling to secure advertising spaces and venues for political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said the dominance of APC billboards and posters in cities across the country reflected the difficulties opposition candidates faced in reaching voters.

“You can see what is happening to other opposition parties who have been on the campaign trail. If you go throughout the country, you hardly find their billboards and posters on the streets of the various cities across Nigeria. You only find one party, the APC,” he said.

Mr Duke alleged that advertising spaces had become prohibitively expensive in some states, with political parties reportedly required to spend as much as N1 billion to begin advertising campaigns.

He said the financial burden would be particularly significant for parties seeking national visibility across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The PRP presidential candidate also said his party had repeatedly postponed its retreat because it struggled to secure venues.

“Now, as it pertains to us in the PRP, we had to postpone this retreat several times because we were deprived of venues. Sometimes, they’ll tell you, ‘Oh, the date has been booked. Go to other venues,’” he said.

PRP rejects calls to surrender party structure

The PRP National Chairman, Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, said the party was exploring ways to strengthen opposition unity but would not dissolve its political structure into another party.

He said the party was willing to support one or two opposition candidates capable of defeating the APC but insisted that participating in a coalition did not mean abandoning its identity.

“Well, as it pertains to us in the PRP, if you ask us about the current state of our campaign, we will tell you. But we can’t collapse the structure for anybody because that time is over,” he said.

Mr Baba-Ahmed said discussions about possible political realignments remained open, adding that the party was assessing the available options.

He also rejected suggestions that the PRP was participating in the 2027 election merely to make up the numbers.

He said the party was committed to negotiations that would produce a viable opposition alliance, with an agenda addressing insecurity, economic hardship, youth participation and the protection of vulnerable communities.

“We will discuss how we will win elections without stolen fortunes. We will adopt strategies that give voices to women and the young Nigerian; courage to beleaguered communities under constant attack from all manner of killers, kidnappers and terrorists,” he said.

He added that the proposed coalition should offer Nigerians confidence in a country where religion or geographical origin would not determine citizens’ access to opportunities or expose communities to vulnerability.

“We have faith that Nigerians will choose wisely in 2027, and disappoint those who think we are cheap and disposable. We are ready to be part of the change we all need. Nigeria must survive 2027. We are not in the race for leadership in 2027 just to make up the numbers. We are in this contest to win,” he said.

Opposition coalition struggles to settle on common candidate

Mr Duke’s remarks are coming on the heels of renewed efforts by opposition parties to establish an alliance capable of challenging Mr Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that representatives of six opposition parties, including the PRP, ADC, NDC, Allied Peoples Movement, a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party and Social Democratic Party, attended an opposition summit in Abuja on 31 August.

The summit, facilitated by the G100 opposition unity initiative, agreed to establish committees and working groups to develop proposals on political cooperation, a common national reform programme and the possibility of presenting a single presidential candidate.

However, disagreements over the proposed arrangement have persisted, particularly over whether the coalition should produce a common presidential candidate or focus on electoral cooperation.

In October, the ADC said the G100 discussions were not specifically aimed at producing a single presidential candidate, but rather at exploring electoral cooperation, including strategies for protecting votes.

The PRP’s position adds another dimension to the negotiations, with its leadership signalling willingness to support a common opposition candidate while maintaining the party’s independent political structure.

World.title: INEC asks court to set aside subpoena for Tinubu’s 1999, 2023 election records
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to set aside a subpoena directing its chairman, Joash Amupitan, to produce President Bola Tinubu’s records from the 1999 Lagos State governorship election and the 2023 presidential election.

In a motion filed on Tuesday, the commission argued that the subpoena was defective, that Mr Amupitan was not personally served and that the documents requested were not in its custody in the form described.

The application came ahead of Mr Amupitan’s scheduled appearance in court on Wednesday as a subpoenaed defence witness in the criminal trial of human rights activist Omoyele Sowore.

The case, marked FHC/CR/484/2025, is before trial judge Mohammed Umar.

Mr Sowore is being prosecuted in the case by the State Security Service for calling Mr Tinubu a criminal in social .edia posts last year.

INEC, through its lawyer, Alex Izinyon, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), asked the court to set aside the subpoena issued on 26 October. The motion was received at the court registry at 3.45 p.m. on Tuesday.

The subpoena, titled Subpoena Duces Tecum, requires Mr Amupitan, a professor, to produce two sets of documents submitted by Mr Tinubu to the electoral commission.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

They are the president’s Form CF001 for the 1999 Lagos governorship election, including an affidavit relating to lost certificates, and his corresponding nomination form for the 2023 presidential election.

The court also directed the INEC chairman to testify for the defence and remain in attendance until the case is determined.

According to The Guardian newspaper, a hearing notice was served on Mr Amupitan on Monday, 9 November, directing him to appear in court on Wednesday, 11 November.

INEC’s grounds for challenging the subpoena

In its application, the commission listed four grounds for asking the court to set aside the subpoena.

It described the document as “void ab initio, ungrantable, inconsistent and contradictory”.

INEC also argued that Mr Amupitan was not personally served with the subpoena, as required by law.

On the documents sought by the defence, the commission said there was no form known as INEC CF01 for either the 1999 Lagos governorship election or the 2023 presidential election.

It maintained that the forms, as described in the subpoena, were unknown to it and were not in the custody of its chairman.

The commission further accused Mr Sowore’s defence team of bringing the application in bad faith, describing it as irrelevant, speculative and intended to embarrass the electoral body.

In an affidavit supporting the motion, Mendie Akpan, a litigation secretary in Mr Izinyon’s law firm, explained how the subpoena was received at INEC’s headquarters.

Ms Akpan said the document was served on the commission’s Litigation and Prosecution Department at about 12.30 p.m. on 6 November.

She said the information was obtained during a telephone conference with Mr Izinyon at his Abuja office on 10 November, following information received from the INEC chairman.

According to the affidavit, Mr Amupitan was not personally served with the subpoena on 6 November or at any other time.

Ms Akpan also stated that the chairman was not a party to the criminal proceedings between the Federal Republic of Nigeria and Mr Sowore.

She added that Mr Amupitan was not the maker of the documents and could not give evidence about them.

Other defence witnesses

The subpoena followed an application by Mr Sowore’s defence team, led by Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika, also a SAN, seeking to compel relevant individuals to appear in court and produce documents considered necessary for his defence.

Apart from Mr Amupitan, the court approved a subpoena against Joe Igbokwe, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, as a proposed defence witness.

However, Mr Umar set aside an earlier subpoena issued against the State Security Service (SSS) lead prosecuting lawyer, Akinlolu Kehinde, also a SAN, ruling that the lawyer should not be compelled to testify in the case.

The court adjourned the proceedings until 11 November for further hearing.

Sowore reacts

Mr Sowore disclosed INEC’s move in a Facebook post on Tuesday, accusing the commission of trying to avoid producing the president’s electoral records.

“Instead of producing the documents, @inecnigeria has rushed to court, asking that the subpoena be set aside!” he wrote.

He questioned why the commission was challenging a court order for documents he said should be in its custody.

“Why is INEC fighting a court order demanding records that should be in its custody? What exactly is the electoral commission afraid of producing?” he asked.

The activist insisted that the records must be produced on Wednesday.

Mr Sowore is being prosecuted by the SSS over social media publications in which he described President Tinubu as a criminal. He has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

INEC’s application seeks to prevent its chairman from being compelled to produce the documents and testify in the trial. The Federal High Court is yet to rule on the application.

World.title: How AI is helping Nigerian farmers tackle crop diseases, improve farm decisions
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Cynthia Alo

With many Nigerian farmers still relying on traditional knowledge to identify crop diseases and determine appropriate treatments, delayed access to agricultural advice often means problems are left unresolved until they affect yields.



In some cases, farmers have to wait days for agronomists to visit their farms and recommend solutions.



CropCura, a digital agricultural innovation co-founded by Victor Onyekachukwu, is seeking to change this practice by bringing crop diagnosis and farm advisory services directly to farmers through technology.



Onyekachukwu said the application allows farmers to take pictures of affected crops and receive an AI-powered analysis and recommendations on possible solutions in less than a minute.



Apart from crop diagnosis, the platform provides weather information, an AI advisory service and digital farm mapping which allow farmers to access information needed to make decisions about their farms.



He said the innovation also addresses another longstanding challenge in Nigerian agriculture which is farmers’ difficulty accessing formal credit because of inadequate records.



Through digital farm profiles containing information about farmers, their locations, crops and farm sizes, Onyekachukwu said the technology will also combine a credit-scoring system that can help financial institutions assess farmers for lending.



The platform, he said, currently has more than 2,000 farmers, who have mapped over 10,000 hectares of farmland.



However, Onyekachukwu identified language barriers, limited smartphone access, low digital literacy and farmers’ distrust of technology as obstacles to wider adoption.



He said the government should introduce policies recognising verified digital farm profiles as acceptable evidence for accessing agricultural loans and grants.

World.title: Research-policy disconnect undermines agric interventions — Experts
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Cynthia Alo

Agricultural experts have attributed the disconnect between farmers, researchers and policymakers as a major factor undermining the effectiveness of agricultural policies and interventions.



This is even as they called for greater farmer participation in research design and policy formulation.



According to them, research priorities were often determined without adequate consideration of farmers’ immediate needs, while policy implementation was constrained by funding limitations, institutional bottlenecks and poor communication of research findings.



The experts spoke during the virtual inaugural episode of the Agricultural Policy Circle, organised by Farmosphere, with the theme, “Finding the Gap where Research, Policy, and Practice disconnect.”



Agriculture researcher, Ifunanya Orisekeh,said research questions were sometimes determined before researchers reached farming communities, leaving farmers to respond to problems that might not reflect their immediate realities.



She said research agendas were often shaped by funding calls, academic requirements and institutional timelines, while the time required to generate findings further widened the gap between research and practice.



She said: “Research agendas are shaped before a funding call comes up. For example, if there is a project that needs a student already set, by the time you reach the field, the question is already printed and the farmer is there to answer your question.



“So we can become very good in the research perspective. We are very good at answering questions that farmers have never asked.”



Orisekeh said research could take three to four years to produce findings, by which time the conditions confronting farmers might have changed.



She also questioned the practice of measuring project success by the number of farmers trained without establishing whether they continued using the recommended practices after project support ended.



Using conservation agriculture as an example, she said, “It is widely promoted and many farmers have widely dropped it as well once the project and even the report is over.”



She identified the mismatch between research schedules and farming seasons, inadequate representation of different categories of farmers and failure to return research findings to communities as other weaknesses.



Also speaking, Founder of AgricIncome Hub and Chief Executive Officer of Maxipharo Farms, Olaoluwa Farotimi, identified inadequate access to credit, unstable markets, poor extension services, logistics challenges and climate-related risks as major constraints confronting farmers.



He said agricultural financing often failed to reflect production cycles, while farmers had little control over market prices and could suffer losses from sudden policy changes.

He said: “There is no access to credit for farmers. For example, you have a production cycle of two months or a month, and you have to pay back in six months while your crop is still in the field’’.

Speaking from the policy perspective, Dr. Gideon Tups, an Economic Geography expert and Agricultural Policy and Global Bioeconomy specialist, said money and power are major constraints to translating research evidence into agricultural transformation.

Tups, a former Policy Adviser for Food Systems Transformation at GIZ, said governments needed to prioritise investments that delivered economic, environmental and social benefits, while recognising that agricultural transformation could face resistance from farmers, businesses and political interests.

World.title: COCEFAAA appoints new directors to strengthen cocoa, coffee farmers’ interests
World.content:
By Kafayat Kokumo

The Cocoa and Coffee Farmers Alliance Association of Africa (COCEFAAA) has appointed some stakeholders to its Board of Directors and country leadership positions to strengthen the representation and protection of cocoa and coffee farmers across West, East and Central Africa.



In a statement made available to Vanguard AgroBiz, Global President of the association, Comrade Adeola Adegoke, announced that the appointments include two Board Members, three Country Directors and two Deputy Country Directors, with representatives from Ethiopia, Kenya, Sierra Leone, Ghana and Cameroon.



The new appointees are Dr Liliane Kabondo Mbazumutima, a global public health leader, and Mr Raymond Katta, Executive Chairman of the Sierra Leone Produce Monitoring Board, both appointed as Board Members.



Others are Mr Abel Ayele Bunaro, Founder and Managing Director of BunAroma Specialty Coffee, appointed Country Director for Ethiopia; Mr Jack Ndirangu, Chairman of Kahiraini Coffee Factory, as Country Director for Kenya; and Mr Didan Sankoh, Director of Operations and Programmes at the Sierra Leone Produce Monitoring Board, as Country Director for Sierra Leone.



The association also appointed Mr James Kwarteng, Co-founder of Apocco Farms Limited, as Deputy Country Director for Ghana, while Prince Mahamadou Mamouda Almed, President of the Meme Cocoa Buyers Association (MECOBA), was named Deputy Country Director for Cameroon.



Commenting on the development, Adegoke said they were intended to reinforce the association’s commitment to protecting the rights and interests of cocoa and coffee producers across the continent.



He said: “This is to reinforce the commitment of the organisation to protect the rights and interests of our producers in cocoa and coffee sectors across the West, East and Central Africa in order to optimise their productivity, build sustainability in their activities, guarantee quality assurance, ensure their resilience and expand their incomes through fair pricing.”

World.title: SMEs: NADF, Sahel Capital sign MoU to reduce borrowing costs
World.content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA – IN a bid to boost agribusiness, the National Agricultural Development Fund, NADF and Sahel Capital Fund Manager Limited have signed a Memorandum of Understanding, MoU, to expand access to affordable financing for Small and Medium Enterprises, SMEs, in the agricultural sector.



The partnership which seeks to unlock more private-sector investments in agriculture, is expected to reduce the cost of borrowing for agribusinesses through innovative blended financing arrangements.



Speaking at the signing ceremony, Executive Secretary, NADF, Muhammed Ibrahim, said the agreement marked a deliberate shift from conventional agricultural financing towards building an investment ecosystem capable of attracting sustainable capital into the sector.



Ibrahim explained that NADF would bring its catalytic and development mandates, as well as its understanding of national agricultural priorities, to the partnership, while Sahel Capital would contribute investment expertise, market intelligence and experience across different agricultural value chains.



According to him, the collaboration is designed to combine public-sector and concessionary capital with private investment expertise to unlock additional financing opportunities for viable agribusinesses.



Under the MoU, both institutions will explore the feasibility of blended financing arrangements through which NADF provide funding alongside capital managed by Sahel Capital, including the Sahel Agribusiness Private Debt Fund, SAPDF.



The proposed financing framework may feature risk-sharing mechanisms, concessional financing and other innovative funding structures aimed at improving access to capital for eligible agribusinesses.



Sahel Capital is also expected to provide investment structuring, fund management and technical expertise, identify eligible agribusinesses and develop monitoring and reporting frameworks for the proposed facility.



Other areas of collaboration include information sharing, development of a pipeline of bankable agribusiness projects, technical assistance and capacity building.



Also speaking, Managing Partner, Sahel Capital, Mezuo Nwuneli, explained the partnership basically would help reduce borrowing costs for agribusiness SMEs by combining NADF funding with capital managed by the investment firm.

However, Nwuneli lamented many agribusinesses currently obtain loans at interest rates ranging between 24 and 27 per cent, a situation he said makes business expansion, investment in productive capacity and long-term growth difficult.

He said that the proposed collaboration would enable both institutions to provide financing at a lower blended cost, improving the financial viability of businesses and freeing up resources for expansion.

World.title: LASWA, Interferry complete ferry safety inspection training
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA), in partnership with global trade association Interferry, has concluded Module 6 of the Africa Ferry Safety Development and Mentoring Programme to strengthen safety standards across the waterways sector.

The training equipped maritime professionals with technical skills to audit and inspect commercial passenger ferries as part of efforts to improve passenger safety and compliance with international maritime standards.

The module, titled “Survey and Inspection”, combined self-paced theoretical lessons from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Lloyd’s Register with virtual mentorship and practical field exercises.

As part of the programme, participants attended a virtual “Ask the Expert” session on October 21 with Interferry specialists, Joep Bollerman, Francesco Ruisi and Darren Johnston, to discuss international ferry safety standards.

This was followed by live condition and safety compliance audits at operational passenger ferry terminals, supervised by Sandra (Okoli) Ubong of ABS and Engr. Frank Fayinto of Lloyd’s Register.

During the field exercises, participants applied an eight-step survey methodology covering preparation, onboard assessment and reporting.

They were trained to identify safety deficiencies relating to hull integrity, life-saving appliances, fire protection systems and machinery, while applying the 5W+1H principle to ensure evidence-based reporting.

The participants also learnt to classify identified risks into immediate, medium-term and low-priority interventions to facilitate timely corrective action.

The initiative is supported by the Lagos State Government and the Special Adviser to the Governor on Blue Economy, Mr Oluwadamilola Emmanuel, alongside Interferry Chief Executive Officer, Mike Corrigan, and Ferrysafe Executive Sponsor, Shari Corrigan.

With the successful completion of Module 6, the programme is expected to progress to Module 7, titled “Watchkeeping”, scheduled for November 2026.

The next phase will further equip participating maritime professionals with competencies in vessel operations, navigational safety and effective watchkeeping practices.

LASWA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening professional standards, improving passenger safety and developing a more efficient, resilient and sustainable water transportation system in Lagos State and across Africa through international collaboration.

World.title: Lagos urges residents to embrace routine HIV testing
World.content:
Gov Sanwo-Olu

…Extends free screening to public servants, Trade Fair visitors

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has urged residents to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare, rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening.

The government has also extended free HIV testing and counselling services to public servants and visitors to the ongoing 2026 International Trade Fair as part of efforts to promote early diagnosis and expand access to HIV prevention and treatment.

The interventions, implemented by the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency (LSACA), are aimed at bringing HIV-related services closer to residents, encouraging regular testing and ensuring that individuals who require further care are linked to appropriate treatment facilities.

At the Public Service Week health screening exercise, the Head of Service, Lagos State, Mr Bode Agoro, officially opened the free screening programme and urged public servants to prioritise their health by taking advantage of the opportunity.

Agoro said access to preventive healthcare, including HIV screening, was essential to building a healthy, productive and efficient workforce.

He encouraged workers to embrace regular health checks and utilise the confidential testing, professional counselling and information on HIV prevention, transmission and treatment provided through the exercise.

In a related intervention, LSACA commenced free HIV testing and counselling services at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), as part of activities at the 2026 International Trade Fair.

The exercise, which began on Friday, November 6, is scheduled to run for 10 days, ending on Sunday, November 15.

It provides visitors, exhibitors, traders and other participants with access to confidential HIV screening, counselling, preventive health information and guidance on accessing treatment and care where necessary.

The Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr Folakemi Animashaun, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to ensuring that HIV prevention, testing and treatment services remained accessible, confidential and free from discrimination.

Animashaun said knowing one’s HIV status was an important step towards preventing new infections and improving health outcomes, noting that early diagnosis enabled individuals who tested positive to commence treatment promptly and maintain healthy, productive lives.

She urged public servants, Trade Fair participants and residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspected an infection before seeking screening.

The LSACA chief executive also stressed the importance of collaboration with ministries, departments and agencies, development partners, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in expanding access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care services.

She urged members of the public to visit the LSACA screening centre at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square, to access the ongoing free testing and counselling services. Animashaun added that similar services were available at designated health facilities across the state.

World.title: Mining: Zamfara task force moves to reclaim gold fields
World.content:
The Zamfara State Government inaugurated a 13-man committee to curb illegal mining activities across the state.

The Secretary to the Zamfara State Government, Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee on Friday in Gusau, the state capital.

This was contained in a statement signed by Mr Sulaiman Tudu, the Senior Special Assistant on Media, Office of the Secretary to the State Government, issued in Gusau on Saturday.

The committee, headed by the State’s Commissioner for Environment, Abdulrahman Tumbido, has broad membership across security agencies, traditional institutions, and relevant federal and state government agencies.

Inaugurating the committee, Mr Nakwada said the initiative was part of the state government’s efforts to assist the Federal Government in formalising the mining sector in the state.

The SSG charged the committee to work closely with security agencies and relevant regulatory and local authorities to identify locations where illegal mining is taking place and profile the operators.

The committee will also ensure that even licensed companies comply with relevant laws and regulations, take adequate measures to prevent environmental degradation, and safeguard the safety and rights of host communities.

In his remarks, the Chairman of the Committee, Tumbido, said the committee will work with reliable information, respect for the law, fairness and regard for the rights and livelihoods of the people.

He added that the committee will ensure that its efforts contribute to lasting security, environmental protection and sustainable development in the state.

World.title: Emir Sanusi to Governor Lawal: I am impressed
World.content:
Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II

The Emir of Kano, Khalifah Muhammadu Sanusi II, has expressed satisfaction with Governor Dauda Lawal’s performance in Zamfara State.

The emir was the guest of honour at the commissioning of the rebuilt and equipped Zawiyya Mosque and Islamiyya School in Gusau on Friday.

The Zawiyya is one of the oldest Islamic institutions in Zamfara, with a long history of producing scholars across various fields.

In his Friday sermon at the rebuilt mosque, Professor Ibrahim Maqari emphasised peaceful coexistence among people and the importance of cleanliness, particularly in places of worship.

At the commissioning ceremony, the Emir of Kano, Khalifah Muhammadu Sanusi II, said that only those familiar with the Zawiyya’s former structure could fully appreciate the scale and quality of Governor Lawal’s work.

He also emphasised the importance of keeping the rebuilt mosque clean and well maintained.

He said, “The mosque should be kept clean and in good condition. We must maintain cleanliness when we come here because the mosque is a symbol of Islam.

“I am delighted with this work. May Almighty Allah reward His Excellency.

“I can see the good work you are doing in Zamfara State in education, health, security, and infrastructure.

“I am not surprised, as I have known your governor since his days in the banking industry. I know his capabilities, and I am impressed by his performance and happy to see him doing such wonderful work as governor.”

World.title: Continental Reinsurance Strengthens Proposition Ahead BSE Listing
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

Continental Reinsurance Holdings Limited, said it has strengthened its investment proposition ahead of its planned listing on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE), following the approval of its supplementary prospectus by the exchange.

The reinsurers, said the supplementary prospectus confirmed that the promoter-controlled existing shareholder vehicle, ACA Cornerstone Limited, will retain its entire 14.8 percent shareholding rather than exit the business as originally contemplated. It said this also incorporated audit reviewed interim financial results for the six months ended 30 June 2026, reflecting improved profitability and strong underwriting performance.

The Group Managing Director of Continental Reinsurance Holdings, Mutsunge Lawrence Nazare, who disclosed these said: “We have engaged closely with investors and taken on board their feedback. The revised offer reflects that engagement and reinforces our long-term investment proposition. ACA Cornerstone’s decision to remain invested, together with its five-year share retention undertaking, demonstrates continued commitment to the business and its future. We believe this strengthens alignment between existing and incoming shareholders as we prepare for our listing on the Botswana Stock Exchange.”

World.title: PenCom Mandates PFAs to Secure  Retirees’ Consent  Before Enrolment into PenCare
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

The National Pension Commission(PenCom), has mandated all licensed Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) to ensure they are in agreement with retirees before enrolling them into the PenCare initiative.

The commission stated this in a circular published in its official website.

The commission in the circular titled, “Obtaining Retirees Consent for Enrolment into the PenCare Initiative During Programmed Withdrawal Retirement Benefit Processing,” said effective from the date of the circular, (Oct 27, 2026),every PFA should obtain the informed consent of eligible retirees who elect Programmed Withdrawal at the time the retiree executed the Programmed Withdrawal Agreement.

The PenCare launch by Federal Government recently, is a social welfare initiative by PenCom and pension fund operators to provide free basic primary healthcare service to eligible retirees starting with those with low monthly pension benefit.

According to PenCom, eligible retirees must be 60 years old and above , must have chosen programme withdrawal as choice of benefit collection and must have monthly pension benefit amount between N70,000 to N150, 000 .

PenCom in the circular signed by the Director of its Surveillance Department, Mr A. M. Saleem, said the objective of the circular is to ensure that PFAs obtain the informed consent of retirees who choose Programmed Withdrawal (PW) for possible enrolment into the PenCare initiative at the point of retirement.

Highlighting the benefits, the commission stated, “This process is intended to facilitate timely identification and enrolment of eligible retirees, eliminate delays associated with obtaining consent after retirement benefits have been processed, establish a uniform industry-wide consent process and improve the quality and completeness of enrolment records.”

World.title: CMFC Headlines London Global Summit on Africa’s Opportunities
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC) is headlining discussions on Africa’s critical minerals assets at one of world’s largest mining investment forum in London, where more than 2,300 delegates and ministers from 60 countries will brainstorm on mining opportunities in Nigeria and other African countries.

Chairman, Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC), Lamon Rutten, said that Nigeria and other African countries hold significant position in the global economic future. “The world is short of the minerals it has committed to build its future on, and a material share of what is left sits in Africa. What has been missing is not geology or demand. It is the institutional layer that converts a deposit into something an international lender can underwrite.

“CMFC exists to build that layer, and London is where we intend to say so to the governments and investors who can act on it,” Rutten, founding Chief Executive Officer Saudi Arabia Mining Exchange and Indonesia Commodity and Derivatives Exchange, said.

President and Co-Chief Executive, Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC), Dr. Israel Ovirih said accompany like CMFC stands at the intersection of African minerals assets and the global investment market.

World.title: LCFE, FMDQ Partner to Strengthen Petroleum Liquids Market Infrastructure
World.content:
The Lagos Commodities and Futures Exchange (LCFE) and FMDQ Clear Limited have entered into a strategic partnership to strengthen the clearing, settlement and risk-management infrastructure for petroleum liquids transactions in Nigeria’s emerging commodities market.

The two institutions signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), establishing a framework for FMDQ Clear to provide third-party clearing infrastructure and related services for petroleum liquids transactions executed on LCFE’s electronic trading platform.

Under the proposed arrangement, FMDQ Clear will serve as the Central Counterparty (CCP) responsible for clearing and settlement of petroleum liquids transactions, subject to the terms of the MoU and subsequent definitive agreements between the parties.

The partnership is expected to strengthen the post-trade architecture of the commodities market by providing access to established clearing technology, risk-management systems, collateral management and operational infrastructure.

Speaking on the development, LCFE Managing Director, Akin Akeredolu-Ale, said the MoU aligns with the Exchange’s commitment to expanding strategic partnerships in risk management and strengthening the infrastructure required to support organised commodities trading.

He explained that the collaboration would enable LCFE to leverage FMDQ Clear’s existing clearing technology, risk-management systems and operational capabilities rather than independently developing a Central Counterparty infrastructure from the ground up.

According to him, this approach is expected to significantly reduce the time, capital investment and technical resources required to establish a robust post-trade clearing framework, while allowing the Exchange to benefit from an established institutional platform.

World.title: Capitalisation: FG Challenges Insurers on Stronger Institutions, Balance Sheet
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, has challenged operators of insurance sector to ensure that their new capital regime produces more than stronger balance sheets, stronger institutions, build public confidence as well as provide better protection for businesses and Nigerian households.

Oyedele, threw the challenge while addressing directors of insurance companies at the 8th Annual Insurance Directors’ Conference organised by the College of Insurance and Financial Management in collaboration with the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM ) recently in Lagos.

Oyedele who was represented at the directors’ forum by finance expert in the Federal Ministry of Finance, Dr Greg Ezeilo, charged insurers and their regulators not to see their transition to new capital regime as mere regulatory obligation but as opportunity to strategic transformation.

“The ultimate measure of success will not be how much capital the industry raises, but how effectively that capital protects policy holders, absorbs shocks, builds confidence and finances economic progress, I am confident that this can be achieved, “the finance minister said.

Also speaking, the Commissioner for Insurance, Mr Olusegun Ayo Omosehin, urged the insurance directors to look beyond their company’s present capital and pay particular attention to the quality of the capital, the manner in which it is deployed, the risks it supports and the returns it generates to ensure that their institutions remain resilient in the face of the new capital.

He warned the directors that the fact that their companies scaled through the recapitalisation hurdle did not mean they were resilient.

World.title: Lending, Govt Securities Gain Lifts Nine Banks Interest Income to N12.9tn
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

On the back of encouraging interest on lending to customers and yield on government securities, Access Holdings Plc and eight other deposit money banks generated N12.9 trillion interest income in nine months of 2026.

This represents about 0.9 per cent increase over N12.75 trillion reported in the same period in 2025.

The other banks are: Ecobank Transnational Incorporated, Zenith Bank Plc, First Holdco Plc, Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO), Wema Bank Plc, Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc, and Abbey Bank Plc,

During the period under review, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), reduced interest rate to 23 per cent from 26.5 per cent.

While the average global lending rate sits below 10 per cent, many African economies have interest rates far above 20 per cent where the likes of Access Holdings, GTCO, Ecobank Transnational Incorporated and First Holdco have branches. This creates a tough environment for businesses and customers who need access to credit.

In countries where inflation is high or the local currency keeps losing value, central banks often respond by raising interest rates. This makes borrowing more expensive but is seen as a way to protect the economy. However, this approach also comes with downsides: it slows down growth and limits job creation. However, the CBN at its last MPC meeting reduced MPR to 23 per cent amid ease in inflation rate and stability of Naira at the foreign exchange market.

Despite the cut in MPR, the Nigerian banking sector’s average maximum lending rate increased to 32.62 per cent in September 2026 from 29.84 per cent reported in September 2025, while the average prime lending rate moved from 11.90 per cent in in September 2025 to 19.04 per cent as of September 2026.

Meanwhile, analysis of the nine banks’ unaudited result and accounts showed that Access Holdings recoded N3.1 trillion interest income, about 6.9 per cent increase from N2.9 trillion reported in unaudited nine months of 2025.

The firms’s N1.54 trillion loans and advances to customers in nine months of 2026 from N1.38 trillion in nine months of 2025 was the major drivers of interest income in the period under review.

Also, Zenith Bank declared N2.62 trillion interest income in nine months of 2026, about 4.5 per cent drop from N2.74 trillion in 2025 while Ecobank Transnational Incorporated declared N2.28 trillion interest income, about 2.2 per cent drop from N22.33 trillion in 2025.

First HoldCo announced N2.09 trillion interest income, an 8.7 per cent drop from N2.29 trillion reported in 2025.

Similarly, GTCO announced N1.29 trillion interest income, up by 4.96 per cent from N1.23 trillion reported in 2025 while Stanbic IBTC Holdings reported N545.35 billion interest income, about 5.35 per cent drop over N576.18billion reported in 2025.

On its part, Wema Bank posted N543.56 billion interest income, representing an increase of 37.2 per cent from N396.14 billion in 2025.

In addition, Sterling Financial Holdings Company posted N353.78 billion interest income, about 34.8 per cent from N262.42 billion in 2025. Abbey Bank reported N28.8 billion interest income which is 120.3 prr cent growth from N13.09 billion in 2025.

Further analysis showed that the nine financial institutions recorded N4.97 trillion interest expenses, representing an increase of nearly 5.31 per cent from N4.72 trillion declared 2025.

These financial institutions interest expenses is made up of Deposits from banks, expenses from debt securities issued, Interest bearing borrowings and other borrowed funds, among others. Analysts have attributed the increase in interest income and expenses to the high in interest rate in most African countries over the years.

World.title: Leadway  Named Official Insurer of Lagos Trade Fair
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

Leadway Assurance, a subsidiary of Leadway Group, has for the second time been named the official insurer of the 2026 Lagos International Trade Fair (LITF) which holds from November 6 to 15th 2026.

The 40th edition of the fair, organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), is holding at Tafawa Balewa Square, Onikan Lagos, and will end on November 15th 2026.

As Official Insurer, Leadway Assurance will provide seamless insurance solutions and personalised consultations to exhibitors and visitors throughout the 10–day fair.

Speaking on the partnership, Executive Director, Retail & Partnerships at Leadway Assurance, Kikelomo Fischer, said the renewed partnership reflected the brand’s dedication to supporting and protecting enterprises and businesses in Nigeria.

“At Leadway Assurance, we have a deep belief in the power of enterprise, especially small and growing businesses, the engine of the Nigerian economy, who duly deserve partners that stand with them as they build”. She said.

Fischer, said returning as official insurer of the Lagos International Trade Fair for a second year clearly showed how interested Leadway is in the growth of SMEs.

“The fair brings thousands of entrepreneurs, buyers and investors together, and we are proud to protect that ambition while helping businesses understand how the right cover safeguards their goods, their people and their future, she stated.

She added that the fair also offered Leadway Assurance a valuable opportunity to engage business owners directly, listen to their needs, and introduce solutions tailored to the realities of running a business in Nigeria.

World.title: Ecobank Targets 35,000 Visitors, Others at December Adire Festival
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

Ecobank Nigeria has announced plans to host a special December edition of its Adire Lagos festival, targeting over 35,000 visitors and more than 150 Nigerian and African brands as it seeks to deepen support for small businesses and unlock opportunities within Nigeria’s growing creative economy.

The three-day event expected to be held in Lagos, will bring together fashion designers, textile merchants, artisans and other creative entrepreneurs, providing a platform to showcase their products, attract new customers and expand their businesses.

Speaking ahead of the festival, Head, SMEs, Partnerships & Collaborations at Ecobank Nigeria, Omoboye ODU, said the December Edition reinforces Ecobank’s commitment to the creative economy by connecting culture and creativity with real commercial opportunities for African businesses.

“Ecobank Adire Lagos has grown beyond being simply an exhibition. It is an SME and creative enterprise platform that connects culture with commerce, giving businesses visibility, access to customers and opportunities to grow. Our ambition is to ensure that the creativity we celebrate also translates into sustainable businesses, jobs, market access and economic value.”

She added: “December presents a particularly exciting opportunity. Lagos comes alive with Nigerians returning home, tourists, families and consumers looking for authentic experiences and locally made products. We want to bring that audience together with some of the most exciting African designers, artisans and creative entrepreneurs, giving our SMEs an opportunity not just to showcase, but importantly, to sell, build relationships and reach new customers.”

World.title: ‘I did not sign up’: Obren on getting cast in ‘Married at First Sight’
World.content:
On the Unscripted podcast, Obren Msuku, a former Married at First Sight Season 3 cast member, revealed that he never applied to be on the hit reality show.

Instead, one of the content producers approached him with an opportunity to join the show.

OBREN MSUKU WAS APPROACHED TO BE ON ‘MAFS’

Several participants from the show have been hopping from one podcast to another, where they have shared their side of the story, since viewers only see an edited version of who they truly are.



During a recent episode, which drew over 900 comments on YouTube, it was now Obren’s turn to lift the veil after his ex-wife, Laurinda Mabunda, made unsavoury remarks about him.

The former couple met and married on the show.

The 38-year-old entrepreneur revealed that a content producer had approached him, explaining that the show was short of prospective husbands and asked if he would be keen to take part.

The host, Peter Manjate, asked, “Why 

Obren responded: “I did not sign up. I did not write an email to Married at First Sight and say, ‘I want to get married.’ No,” he began.

“So, because I’m in the media industry, there’s a lady who’s one of the content producers. She reached out. She said, Listen, we need husbands on the show,’ he continued.



“At the time I’m single from a six-year relationship. I haven’t been dating for like a year. Yes, I was seeing people here and there, but nothing serious,” he added.

“I was like, okay. It took time though for her to convince me because I was a bit sceptical. I’ve never been one to chase clout, especially with my background. I could have been famous any day over the past 15 years,” he said.

He added, “I just gave myself a bit of grace. I was like, ‘Go for it. Why not?’ Maybe this could be an opportunity for you to meet the love of your life.”

CORRECTING MISCONCEPTIONS

Season 3 of Married at First Sight was filled with romance and drama, but for Obren, the experience leaned more towards the latter.

According to him, the infamous “list” was a turning point in his journey because he felt betrayed after Laurinda spoke negatively about him during the girls’ pajama party.

The drama started when Hlulani Ngobeni, one of the husbands on the show, jotted down the juicy gossip that his wife, Nompumelelo Sobhuza, had shared with him after returning from the party.

Hlulani then shared the list with the group, sparking the 3rd degree from fellow cast members especially Obren whose name topped the list.

The allegations against him included money laundering, car theft, and the back-room situation at his childhood home.

During the interview, Obren addressed several misconceptions and allegations that plagued him throughout the show.

World.title: Cape Town may have lost 15% of its wetlands over a nine-year period
World.content:
The report indicates 'significant wetland transformation' due to factors like urban expansion. Image: Zandvlei Trust/ Facebook

The Mother City may have lost more than 5 000 hectares of potential wetland area in nearly a decade, according to the City’s latest spatial trends report.

The 2025/26 Spatial Trends and Implementation Tracking report gives an overview of development and land use patterns in Cape Town from 2012 to 2026.

According to estimates, wetland area in the metro fell from approximately 33 106 hectares in 2016 to 28 002 hectares in 2025.



That represents a net decline of roughly 5 104 hectares, or 15%.

Where Cape Town’s wetlands are under pressure

The report identifies several areas affected by wetland loss and degradation.

These include Driftsands Nature Reserve, where associated vleis have been affected by land invasions during the Covid-19 period.

Noordhoek vlei has also been impacted by the expansion of informal settlements from Masiphumelele.

Other affected areas include the Diep River and Kleine Stink River floodplains, seasonal vleis in the Slangetjiebos section of False Bay Nature Reserve, and vleis along the lower Kuils and Eerste rivers.

“On-the-ground observations indicate significant wetland transformation and degradation associated with urban expansion, land invasion, pollution, and hydrological modification,” the report states.



Cape Town’s Rondevlei Nature Reserve. Image: Wikimedia

Drought and development

The report says rainfall patterns also influenced the estimates. The severe 2015–2018 drought, followed by wetter years, coincided with fluctuations in potential wetland extent.

It suggests reduced surface water availability and weaker hydrological connections contributed to lower estimates between 2017 and 2022.

“Although modest recoveries were observed during wetter years, the overall declining trend suggests that longer-term pressures, including urban expansion, land transformation, hydrological modification, and climate change, could be contributing to persistent wetland loss across Cape Town,” the report concluded.

Important note: The figures stated above are based on wetland probability mapping rather than a direct count of wetlands or vleis physically destroyed. The City used a machine-learning classification method to identify potential wetland areas across Cape Town.

Meanwhile, over the same period, informal structures in Cape Town have increased by 67%. Read more on that story here.

World.title: How and why is Tatjana Smith representing the Netherlands?
World.content:
How and why is Tatjana Smith representing the Netherlands? Images via Facebook/Canva

South Africa’s most decorated swimmer, Tatjana Smith, has made the difficult decision to switch to representing the Netherlands with immediate effect.

This comes after she shared her grievances about her experience with the aquatic national governing body, Swimming South Africa, in a recent interview on Carte Blanche.

The 29-year-old recently returned to competing internationally after a premature retirement in 2024. At the time, the star athlete – whose sister-in-law is Rachel Kolisi – had won one silver and one gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics.



TATJANA SMITH TO REPRESENT THE NETHERLANDS – HOW IS SHE ELIGIBLE?

In a bombshell video statement, Tatjana Smith announced that she would be switching national allegiance as a professional swimmer from South Africa to the Netherlands.

The 29-year-old explained that representing the European country could provide her with high-performance support, financial stability, and a more sustainable swimming career.

Tatjana is eligible to represent the country because her father, René, was born in the Netherlands, which grants her both South African and Dutch citizenship.



René moved from Naaldwijk, the Netherlands, to South Africa in 1989, where he met Renske, a South African woman. The couple welcomed two daughters, Tatjana and her sister Fabienne, in Johannesburg

In 2021, Tatjana’s parents and sibling relocated to the Netherlands, where they now permanently live.

The swimming icon has made it clear that she has neither renounced her South African citizenship nor does she plan to move permanently to the Netherlands. 

She has also emphasised that her decision does not diminish her pride in having represented South Africa.

WHAT HAPPENS TO HER MEDALS?

With confirmation that she will now professionally represent the Netherlands at future competitions, what happens to the medals she has earned for South Africa?



Tatjana Smith has won a large collection of medals, including her Olympic ones, such as

Tokyo 2020: Gold – 200m breaststroke.

Tokyo 2020: Silver – 100m breaststroke.

Paris 2024: Gold – 100m breaststroke.

Paris 2024: Silver – 200m breaststroke.

Although she switches allegiances, her medals are not transferable to the Netherlands and remain South African accolades. However, her future results will be credited to the Netherlands.

World.title: WMO warns of ‘off the charts’ climate extremes as El Niño strengthens
World.content:
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has warned that a very strong El Niño event could intensify global heat and extreme weather into 2027.

Raising concerns about the impact on vulnerable communities, food production and water supplies.

In its latest State of the Climate Update 2026, released on 9 November, the United Nations agency said the world was experiencing a prolonged period of exceptional temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels.



The report found that the past 12 years have each been the warmest on record.

Global average surface temperatures between January and September 2026 reached approximately 1.47°C above the pre-industrial average.

The WMO expects this figure to rise further by the end of the year as El Niño strengthens.



WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said the state of the global climate in 2026 gave new meaning to the phrase “off the charts”.

She warned that hundreds of millions of people had already experienced extreme heat this year, while heatwaves, tropical cyclones and heavy rainfall were increasing the risks facing communities.

Southern Africa faces warmer conditions

The warning is particularly relevant to southern Africa, where the WMO’s seasonal outlook points to warmer-than-normal conditions between November 2026 and January 2027.



The forecast, based on climate models from several international partners, including the South African Weather Service (SAWS), also points to shifts in rainfall patterns across different parts of the world.

For southern Africa, the warmer outlook raises concerns about the potential effects of prolonged heat on water resources, agriculture and communities already vulnerable to extreme weather.

However, the outlook does not mean that every part of the region will experience the same rainfall conditions.



El Niño can bring different impacts to different areas.

Why El Niño is raising concerns

El Niño is a natural climate pattern that develops when sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean become warmer than normal.

The WMO said the current event has been strengthening since August and is expected to reach record strength by December.



The world’s oceans absorb about 90% of the excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases, making ocean warming a major factor in the changing global climate.

The WMO also reported that global sea levels reached their highest point in the satellite record in 2026, while ocean heat continued to rise.

Extreme weather puts lives and livelihoods at risk

The agency warned that El Niño could increase the risks of heatwaves, droughts and heavy rainfall well into 2027.



These conditions could affect food production, worsen water shortages and increase health risks, particularly in communities that depend on rain-fed agriculture.

The WMO also highlighted the human cost of recent extreme weather events.

The WMO said its 2026 update uses data available up to September and does not yet capture the latest impacts of the strengthening El Niño.



Its final State of the Global Climate 2026 report is expected in March 2027

World.title: Does having a degree really give you a better chance of finding a job in South Africa?
World.content:
Does having a degree better your chances of employment in SA? Image: canva

Having a university degree does not guarantee employment in South Africa, but the latest labour market figures show that graduates have a considerably better chance of finding a job than people with lower levels of education.

Statistics South Africa’s (Stats SA) Quarterly Labour Force Survey for the third quarter of 2026 found that graduates recorded an unemployment rate of 11.9%.

This was significantly lower than the national unemployment rate of 33.7%, as well as the rate recorded among people without a matric qualification.



The figures highlight the continued importance of education and formal qualifications in a country where millions of people are struggling to find a job.

Graduates have a much better chance of finding a job

According to Stats SA, the unemployment rate among graduates stood at 11.9% between July and September 2026.

This represented a decrease of 0.6 of a percentage point compared with the previous quarter.

In comparison, people without a matric qualification recorded an unemployment rate of 39.2%, which remained unchanged from the second quarter.

The survey also found that unemployment rates among people with matric and those with less than matric were higher than the national average.

People with other tertiary qualifications, alongside university graduates, recorded unemployment rates below the national figure.



The findings suggest that further education can improve a person’s position in the labour market, although a qualification does not remove the risk of unemployment.

Unemployment increased across all education levels

Despite the advantage recorded by graduates, the latest figures also show that having a qualification does not make South Africans immune to the country’s employment challenges.

Stats SA found that unemployment increased year-on-year across all education levels.

The national unemployment rate rose from 31.9% in the third quarter of 2025 to 33.7% in the same quarter of 2026.

The number of unemployed people also increased by 571 000 over the year, reaching approximately 8.58 million.

The latest figures also show that 16.84 million people were employed in South Africa during the third quarter of 2026.

Although this represented an increase of 101 000 compared with the previous quarter, the number of unemployed people also increased by 97 000.

The broader picture remains challenging, particularly for people entering the labour market for the first time.

Stats SA also recorded a youth unemployment rate of 63.6% among people aged 15 to 24.

Furthermore, 35.7% of young people in this age group were not in employment, education or training.

World.title: Helen Zille’s one-word response to Malema’s lawsuit threat
World.content:
DA federal chairperson Helen Zille has responded with a one-word "No" to Julius Malema's legal demands following his threat to sue her over allegations involving Johannesburg. Image: Facebook/Helen Zille

Democratic Alliance (DA) federal chairperson Helen Zille has refused to back down after Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) leader Julius Malema threatened to sue her over allegations involving the City of Johannesburg.

Zille responded with a single word on a Facebook post on Tuesday, 10 November.

“No.”



She shared the response alongside a letter of demand from Malema’s lawyers, who have given her until Wednesday, 11 November, to retract her statements and apologise publicly.

WHY IS MALEMA THREATENING TO SUE ZILLE?

The dispute stems from an eNCA interview on Sunday, 8 November, during which Zille accused Malema of influencing decisions in Johannesburg while ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba was mayor.

Zille claimed Mashaba relied on the EFF’s support to remain in office and allowed Malema to dictate major decisions.

She alleged that Malema influenced decisions involving City Power and a municipal fleet tender to benefit himself and companies linked to him.

Zille also claimed Mashaba appointed former police deputy national commissioner Shadrack Sibiya to head the city’s anti-corruption unit on Malema’s instructions.

Malema has rejected the allegations as false and defamatory.



MALEMA GIVES ZILLE DEADLINE

In a letter dated 9 November, Malema’s lawyers, England Slabbert Attorneys, demanded that Zille withdraw her statements and issue a public apology.

They want her to publish the apology across her social media platforms and distribute it to media organisations.

The lawyers also demanded that Zille submit the proposed apology for their approval and provide a written undertaking not to repeat the allegations.

They warned that failure to comply by close of business on Wednesday could result in legal proceedings, including a damages claim and an interdict preventing further publication of the statements.

Zille’s one-word response signals that she does not intend to comply with the demands.

The dispute comes as political parties negotiate coalition agreements following the local government elections.

Zille is the DA’s Johannesburg mayoral candidate, while ActionSA has indicated that it is willing to negotiate with the party but will not support her appointment as mayor.

World.title: eNCA coalition builder | The numbers game in Ekurhuleni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Voters made their choice in the 2026 Local Government Election, but the question of who gets to govern the country’s major metros is now in the hands of political parties.

In Ekurhuleni, the Democratic Alliance finished first with 66 seats, but it will need support from other political parties to secure a majority in council.

eNCA election analyst Wayne Sussman provides three possible coalition scenarios that could get the 113 seats needed for a majority in Ekurhuleni.

The first option he explores is a Government of National Unity possibility that would include the DA and the African National Congress (59 seats).

A partnership between these two parties will see them securing 125 seats, which is well above the line needed to form a government.

READ | eNCA coalition builder | Three possible paths to govern Tshwane

A second scenario is a coalition between the DA and ActionSA, who have 40 seats.

But the two parties would have only 106 seats, leaving them seven seats short of a majority.

They would need a third coalition partner like the Freedom Front Plus, which has 11 seats.

However, the big question is whether ActionSA would get into bed with both the Freedom Front Plus and the DA.

The third possibility could be an ANC-led coalition that excludes the DA.

That partnership could see the ANC (59 seats), combined with ActionSA (40 seats) and the Economic Freedom Fighters with their 14 seats.

That would give those three parties exactly 113 seats, just enough for a majority.

World.title: eNCA coalition builder | Three possible paths to govern Tshwane
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The City of Tshwane is one of the major talking points as coalition talks take shape this week.

The DA finished first in the 2026 Local Government Elections, securing 74 seats, followed by ActionSA with 48 seats. Rounding off the top three was ANC with 44 seats.

In Tshwane, the overall majority needed to govern is 108 seats.

eNCA election analyst Wayne Sussman breaks down the numbers as he explores three coalition possibilities.

One option he looked at was a coalition between the DA and ANC.

READ |eNCA Coalition Builder | Battle for Joburg, who has the numbers?

Together, the two parties would have 118 seats. That is a comfortable majority that would only need those two parties to govern.

Another scenario could be the ANC and ActionSA joining up, but that amounts to only 92 seats.

That means they would need other parties to reach the number needed to govern.

If they replicated the current setup and brought in the EFF's 13 seats, that would still leave them two seats short of a majority and needing another minor party to join the coalition.

Despite the bad blood between the two parties, a third possibility would be a coalition between ActionSA and the DA, who together would have a majority of 122 seats in council.

World.title: eNCA Coalition Builder | Battle for Joburg, who has the numbers?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The City of Johannesburg is the biggest prize in the coalition negotiations, but getting the numbers to govern will require political parties to sit down and work together.

The DA emerged as the largest party in the City of Gold, securing 91 seats in the 270-seat council.

But a majority in the Johannesburg Council needs 136 seats to govern.

This leaves the parties with no other choice but to turn to other political parties for support.

eNCA election analyst Wayne Sussman breaks down the numbers as he explores three possible coalition options.

If the DA chooses to go into coalition with the ANC, which has secured 63 seats, that number combined will add up to a comfortable majority of 154 seats in council.

READ | Pressure mounts on Joburg Water amid ongoing supply disruptions

Another possibility is a partnership between the DA and ActionSA, which secured 43 seats. That number adds up to 134 seats.

But if another party like the IFP, which secured seven seats, agrees it would push the coalition to 141 seats, giving it a viable majority.

The third scenario Sussman plays around with is a coalition that excludes the DA.

He sketches the possibility of the ANC and ActionSA potentially joining with other smaller parties such as the MK Party, Rise Mzansi and the PA.

A multi-party coalition along those lines also has enough seats to get above the magic number of 136.

World.title: Number Of The Day | US$200 Billion | 10 November 2026
World.content:
The World's Most Valuable Technology Is Becoming Its Biggest Security Challenge

Artificial intelligence has turned advanced computer chips into strategic assets. The Nvidia controversy reveals how easily the boundaries between commercial ambition, political power and national security can become blurred.

For decades, the world's most strategically important resources were commonly associated with oil, minerals and industrial infrastructure. Artificial intelligence is changing that calculation. Advanced semiconductors have become essential to economic competitiveness, military capability and technological leadership, placing

the companies that manufacture them at the centre of an increasingly consequential international contest.

Nvidia's extraordinary rise illustrates the scale of this transformation. Its processors power sophisticated AI systems, making the company a critical supplier to technology businesses developing everything from automated services to advanced computing infrastructure. Yet that influence also creates vulnerability. When a company becomes central to an entire technological ecosystem, questions about its leadership, commercial relationships and security arrangements can have consequences extending far beyond its shareholders.

When Commercial Technology Becomes A Strategic Asset

The competition between the United States and China over advanced semiconductors is not simply a disagreement about international trade. Both countries recognise that access to powerful computing infrastructure can influence economic productivity, technological independence and national defence capabilities.

Washington has consequently imposed restrictions on exports of certain advanced chips to China. These measures are intended to limit access to technologies considered strategically sensitive, but they also present an enormous commercial challenge for American manufacturers. China represents a significant potential market, while export controls can restrict the ability of companies to serve customers and expand their businesses.

The disagreement exposes two competing approaches to technological leadership. One argues that allowing international customers to purchase American technology helps preserve US commercial influence and discourages competitors from developing alternatives. The other maintains that providing advanced hardware to geopolitical rivals could accelerate capabilities that eventually challenge American economic and security interests.

Neither argument eliminates the underlying tension. A company may benefit financially from broader market access while its government sees that same access as a strategic vulnerability.

The Complications Of An International Supply Chain

The challenge becomes more complicated when advanced technology moves through international networks of distributors, cloud-computing businesses and data centres. The destination of a physical chip is not necessarily the only consideration. Access to computing power can also be provided through infrastructure located outside the country where its eventual users operate.

This distinction has become relevant to scrutiny surrounding Nvidia's commercial relationships. Reporting has raised allegations about whether companies linked to Singapore-based Megaspeed International helped facilitate access to Nvidia chips by Chinese businesses. These allegations remain subject to investigation and must not be confused with established findings of wrongdoing.

The wider policy question is significant regardless of the outcome. If restrictions focus primarily on where equipment is shipped, regulators must also consider whether access to the technology can be obtained through services or infrastructure elsewhere. Effective controls require an understanding of entire technology supply chains, not merely the initial transaction.

Why Corporate Governance Is Now A Security Issue

The controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has intensified scrutiny of the relationship between corporate leadership and national security. Huang has acknowledged marital infidelity, while allegations that a businesswoman associated with him was involved in Chinese intelligence activity are being investigated.

Nvidia's board has initiated an independent inquiry and has stated that it has no reason to believe company secrets or national-security information were compromised. That distinction matters: the existence of an investigation does not establish that espionage occurred.

Nevertheless, the situation demonstrates why corporate governance cannot be separated from security considerations when a business controls strategically important technology. Effective leadership oversight, conflict-of-interest procedures and independent board scrutiny become essential safeguards for shareholders, employees and customers.

These responsibilities grow more important when the founder of a company is also its public face, principal strategist and most influential representative in government negotiations.

The Financial Cost Of Uncertainty

Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on 9 November 2026, according to Reuters, removing approximately US$190 billion from the company's market capitalisation. The episode of Number of the Day broadcast on 10 November described the loss as US$200 billion.

Such movements show how quickly financial markets can reassess perceived risks. Investors must consider not only potential legal or regulatory consequences, but also leadership continuity, reputational damage and the possibility of restrictions affecting future business opportunities.

A decline in market capitalisation does not mean an equivalent sum has disappeared from the company's bank accounts. It reflects a reduction in the market's valuation of its outstanding shares, driven by changing prices and investor expectations.

The Next Test Of Technological Power

Artificial intelligence is creating opportunities for companies and countries capable of developing sophisticated computing infrastructure. It is also introducing difficult questions about who controls that infrastructure, who can access it and how commercial interests should be balanced against national-security concerns.

Those questions will persist long after any individual investigation concludes. For businesses, policymakers and investors, the central challenge is no longer simply how quickly artificial intelligence can advance. It is whether the institutions governing that advancement can keep pace.

References

· eNCA, Number of the Day, 10 November 2026, featuring Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd.

· Reuters, 9 November 2026: Reporting on Nvidia's market-value decline and the shareholder lawsuit.

· Associated Press, 9 November 2026: Reporting on Nvidia's independent investigation and company response.

· Reuters, 10 November 2026: Reporting on allegations concerning Nvidia chip shipments to China.

World.title: Tatjana Smith dumps South Africa for Netherlands
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Tatjana Smith has made a surprise move by switching her allegiance to the Netherlands.



This means South Africa's most decorated Olympian will now compete under the Dutch flag at the Los Angeles Games in 2028.



Smith holds both Dutch and South African citizenship.



In a statement, Smith thanked South Africa and said it was an honour to represent the country at the Olympic Games, but that athletes need a chance to 'thrive, not just survive'.



This comes after Smith was involved in a legal dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money that was withheld from her.

World.title: WATCH | Matlala backtracks on R500K bribe payment claim
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged underworld kingpin Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala has tried to backtrack from a major corruption claim in his own affidavit.

During his testimony at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry on Tuesday, Matlala maintained that he did not read or realise what he was signing.

The affidavit states he paid a R500,000 bribe to former police deputy commissioner Shadrack Sibiya to secure a R228 million SAPS health tender.

World.title: Ramaphosa announces salary hikes for judges, MP's and Cabinet
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Judges and other public officials are set to receive a pay hike.

President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced salary increases of between 3.5% and 4% for the 2026/2027 financial year, effective 1 April 2026.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Presidency said the 3.5% increase applies to members of the national executive, members of the National Assembly, permanent delegates to the national council of provinces, premiers, members of provincial executive councils, and members of provincial legislatures.

The 4% salary increment applies to judges, magistrates, traditional leaders, members of the national and provincial houses of traditional and Khoi-San Leaders, and members of independent constitutional institutions.

According to the Presidency, the decision follows recommendations by the Independent Commission for the Remuneration of Public Office-Bearers, and the President’s consideration of serious economic challenges facing the country.
