The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A CBC News copy editor turned into one half of an unexpected comedy duo in a video posted to social media Tuesday.

American comedian Josh Johnson, a stand-up and occasional host of The Daily Show, was cracking jokes about CBC's coverage of a bodega cat getting evicted due to health concerns, during his show at the Vogue Theatre in Vancouver last month.

"I want so badly to meet the editor," Johnson quipped.

A voice from the audience shouted out: "He's here!"

A befuddled Johnson replied: "The cat's here?"

Nope.

"The editor's here!" shouted the crowd.

Enter Jon Azpiri.

Wearing a dark grey hoodie, coincidentally mirroring Johnson's signature light grey hoodie, Azpiri walked onstage for a 10-minute back-and-forth filled with jokes about cats, disappearing islands and journalism.

Johnson started to ask Azpiri about the bodega cat situation before Azpiri interrupted.

"We do a lot of stories about cats. So I need to know the specific cat."

WATCH | The cat in question:

Azpiri, a copy editor and reporter, answered Johnson's various questions about how a newsroom chooses what to cover.

"We're a public broadcaster," Azpiri said. "So we have a thing called Journalistic Standards and Practices."

"There's really no need to brag," Johnson replied.

As of 2 p.m. PT, Johnson's video has more than 2.4 million v iews on Instagram, and it's been seen more than 860,000 times on TikTok.

Johnson ended the exchange, and the two shook hands.

As Azpiri left, he reminded Johnson the province was set to have an election the next day.

"That's a real editor right there, too," Johnson said. "Even as he's leaving, [he's like] 'We do have an election tomorrow.'"

CBC News has reached out to J ohnson for comment.

'My eyes kind of bugged out'

Azpiri said he didn't expect Johnson's video to be posted — let alone go viral. He didn't even know the show had been recorded.

He told CBC's BC Today he had just come off his copy editing shift before heading to the show.

As he was walking to the theatre with his wife, he told her he hoped they weren't sitting too close to the stage.

"Sometimes comedians do that thing where they talk to people in the audience," Azpiri said. "And I said 'I don't want to be one of those people.'"

Their tickets were for the lower deck, his wife said.

The show started, and when Johnson said he wanted to talk to a CBC editor, Azpiri reacted.

"My eyes kind of bugged out," Azpiri said.

"My wife couldn't help herself and shouted, 'Oh, he's here.'"

LISTEN | Azpiri on his viral Josh Johnson interaction: As It Happens 6:00 When Josh Johnson invited this CBC editor on stage, he just 'rolled with it'

Azpiri said everything happened so quickly, there was no time for stage fright.

"As I walked toward the stage, I did kind of realize, 'What have I gotten myself into?'"

He estimated 1,000 or so people were in the theatre, but he didn't realize there were cameras rolling.

"That seemed crazy to me.... I thought that was a very pleasant thing I could tell my kids about. And then this happened this morning."

While he's been a hit in the comment section on social media, Azpiri has no plans to try one-upping Johnson on the comedy circuit.

"[I'm] very much second-billing to Josh."

World.title: Protesters denounce Ovechkin's support for Putin as Capitals visit Senators in Ottawa
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Russian hockey superstar Alexander Ovechkin and his Washington Capitals are in town for a matchup against the Senators. The Ukrainian Canadian Congress held a protest outside the Canadian Tire Centre ahead of Tuesday's game calling attention to Ovechkin's continued support of Russian President Vladimir Putin. David Fraser reports.

Members of the Canadian Ukrainian Canadian Congress (UCC) organized a protest outside the Canadian Tire Centre (CTC) in Ottawa on Tuesday in objection to Alex Ovechkin's first game on Canadian soil this season.

The captain of the Washington Capitals has long been criticized for his staunch support of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"It's absolutely not acceptable," Mike Ryndzak, a member of the UCC said of Ovechkin's participation in the game against the Ottawa Senators.

"It's a war. Destruction and devastation is going on as we speak and for them it's business as usual," he said.

A small group of protestors joined him outside the arena before the game started, with more planning to protest inside.

"I see [so much] support from the ordinary Canadian people. It means a lot to me," Ryndzak added, waving a Ukrainian flag. Others held up signs reading "Ban Ovechkin."

Ovechkin reacts ahead of protest

Speaking to reporters at CTC on Tuesday morning, Ovechkin seemed unbothered by the accusations or the UCC's objection to his presence in Canada.

"I just heard about [the protest] this morning and I don't know what to say," he said. "Lots of protests going on around the world."

In September, he defended his decision to appear in a campaign ad for the ruling United Russia party, saying: "I'm Russian, and I support my country."

That same day, NATO member Latvia, which borders Russia, announced Ovechkin's inclusion on a list of "personae non gratae" and prohibited his entry into that republic. The UCC has been calling on Canada to do the same.

WATCH | 'Fans want to see the best players out there,' Ovechkin argues: Alex Ovechkin suggests fans want Russian players at World Juniors | Duration closed caption 0:32 CBC's David Fraser asked Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin what he makes of Mark Carney's decision to bar Russia from competing in the upcoming World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta.

In a statement posted on its website last month, the organization pointed to Section 318 of Canada's Criminal Code which states that "every person who advocates or promotes genocide is guilty of an indictable offence and liable to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years."

The UCC argues that "by explicitly, continually and publicly endorsing Russian president Putin and his political party, Ovechkin is promoting Russia’s genocide against Ukraine."

Canada hasn't gone so far as to deny Ovechkin entry into the country, but Prime Minister Mark Carney announced last week that Russian players will not be allowed to compete at the World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta this December.

"While Russia and Belorussia [sic] are supporting this illegal, unjustified, horrific war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," Carney said when asked if Russian players would be denied visas.

Ovechkin also responded to that decision on Tuesday, suggesting that banning Russian players would be a disservice to hockey fans.

"The fans want to see the best players out there, and the fans want to see young generation players who [are] gonna be future stars, future NHLers ... but you know, it's not up to us," he said.

Ovechkin evaded a question about Russia using its success in sport to foster support for its political agenda, emphasizing that athletes just want to represent their countries.

Ahead of Tuesday's game, a CBC reporter asked Ovechkin whether he was comfortable being used as a propaganda tool by the Russian state. "Nobody's using me," he replied.

In October, Ovechkin announced this season would be his last. He has previously stated he intends to move back to Russia after he retires.

World.title: Irving Oil, Grant Enterprises plead guilty to environment charges over N.B. diesel spill next to Tim Hortons
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Irving Oil Ltd. and Grant Enterprises 1984 Ltd. have pleaded guilty in provincial court to charges under the Clean Environment Act related to a massive diesel spill in Woodstock.

The spill was discovered in December 2024 after a Tim Hortons on Beardsley Road reported its water was contaminated with fuel. The Tim Hortons is next to Murray's Irving gas station and restaurant.

In Woodstock court on Tuesday, it was revealed that the total spill was between 210,000 and 250,000 litres over four months, which is more than previous estimates.

Irving Oil and Grant Enterprises were originally charged with two counts. The charge of failing to immediately report the leak was dropped. The companies pleaded guilty to a charge of releasing a contaminant into the environment.

Crown prosecutor Patrick Wilbur read an agreed statement of facts that said the leak stemmed from a faulty elbow fitting that fed diesel into a 100,000 litre storage tank.

Grant Enterprises had the tank and fill pipe installed in 2014. One of the fittings on that pipe was made of aluminum when it should have been steel or fiberglass.

“Aluminum alloy elbows were never approved nor permitted, and aluminum … should not be part of an underground petroleum system,” Wilbur read.

A faulty aluminum elbow pipe leading to an underground diesel storage tank was found to be responsible for the leak. (Province of New Brunswick)

The cleanup began after inspectors detected the leak along the nearby Trans-Canada Highway.

Wilbur said in court that cleanup recovered about 195,000 litres of diesel. The cleanup and remediation has cost about $15 million so far and the amount will continue to grow.

He also explained how this much diesel being lost into the ground should have been noticed.

“The governance system that includes people, processes and technologies were not being followed.”

Wilbur said regulations for operating the storage tank requires the owner or operator to measure the level of the tank and compare it to how much has been sold.

He said action should be taken immediately if the comparison shows losses.

“While the measurements were taken, the process failed in that it did not detect the ongoing loss that occurred with each delivery,” said Wilbur. “It was not caught by the systems in place for the four months.”

There have now been various other systems put in place, including 42 groundwater monitoring wells and 20 drilled wells.

The Crown has requested a total fine of $400,000 with some of the money earmarked for the province’s environmental trust fund. The two companies did not disagree with the amount.

Judge Rose Campbell said she’ll review the case and come back with her sentence on Feb. 8, 2027.

World.title: Slain cartel boss 'The General' provided Ryan Wedding with fake police ID to evade capture, U.S. alleges
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

How did Ryan Wedding — the Canadian Olympic snowboarder turned international fugitive — manage to evade capture for a decade in Mexico?

U.S. federal charges announced in California on Tuesday gave part of the answer, providing new insight into two alleged accomplices accused of helping to protect Wedding by using tactics worthy of the Netflix series Narcos.

According to a grand jury indictment unsealed in Los Angeles, cartel leader Edgar Aaron Vazquez Alvarado gave Wedding and other co-conspirators a code word so cocaine loads would not be blocked by Mexican police and military personnel.

The code word changed almost daily.

What's more, Vazquez is accused of providing Wedding and co-conspirators with "authentic law enforcement credentials" that were manipulated to bear their own names, allowing Wedding and others to safely pass through security checkpoints in Mexico.

But all that help came at a cost.

$500,000 US entry fee

U.S. prosecutors said Vazquez welcomed the Thunder Bay, Ont.-born Wedding into a club of organized crime leaders who received sensitive information, including details about arrest warrants and investigations.

The indictment, released Tuesday, said Vazquez charged Wedding a one-time initiation fee of $500,000 US to be allowed into the group, and an average monthly fee of $100,000 US.

Mexico Security Minister Omar García Harfuch announced last week that 42-year-old Vazquez — known as "The General" — had been fatally shot in an operation involving Mexican security forces.

WATCH | Mexican judge arrested for allegedly taking bribes linked to Wedding lieutenant: Mexican judge accused of taking $2M bribe to free Ryan Wedding's right-hand man | Duration closed caption 2:04 U.S. prosecutors have charged a Mexican judge for allegedly accepting a $2-million U.S. bribe to free alleged Canadian drug lord Ryan Wedding's second-in-command from detention. Luis Benitez Alcantara now faces extradition to the United States.

His name was first publicly linked to Wedding a year ago when the U.S. Treasury Department announced sanctions against Vazquez and his companies for their ties to the Canadian. The department identified Vazquez as a former Mexican law enforcement officer with high-level connections.

Wedding, 45, allegedly ran a murderous drug-smuggling network that generated $1 billion US a year. The FBI said he fled to Mexico around the time he faced criminal charges in Montreal in 2015.

Also known as Public Enemy, Wedding was arrested in Mexico in January and remains in U.S. custody. He has pleaded not guilty to a list of charges related to murder and drug trafficking. He is scheduled to stand trial in Los Angeles next year.

Suspect allegedly had ties to notorious cartels

Also in Tuesday's news release , the U.S. Attorney's Office in L.A. identified "reputed street gang member" Roberto Gomez as another key facilitator in Wedding's ability to spend years on the run.

Gomez, who went by the aliases Fat Boy and Rooster, allegedly cultivated relationships with people who had access to sensitive information from Mexican and U.S. law enforcement.

The prosecutor's office said the 51-year-old former L.A. resident also kept in touch with leaders of the Sinaloa and Jalisco New Generation cartels — two of Mexico's most notorious criminal syndicates, considered terrorist organizations by the U.S. and Canada.

Ryan Wedding is escorted off a plane in Ontario, Calif., in January, hours after his arrest in Mexico. (FBI)

While Wedding was on the run, the FBI said he benefited from the protection of the Sinaloa Cartel, which was co-founded by infamous drug lord Joaquín (El Chapo) Guzmán. Further details of Wedding's purported arrangements in Mexico are only now beginning to trickle out.

"There were multiple attempts to capture Mr. Wedding, and in each of those attempts we were undermined," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli told CBC News last week.

"He either was tipped off or was given a warning, and was somehow always able to evade us, just barely … and so it was our belief that he was getting help."

U.S. authorities allege Gomez provided Wedding with sensitive information to evade capture, and also helped supply him with bulk drug shipments.

In one instance, prosecutors said Gomez attempted to broker the sale of 453.6 kilograms of methamphetamine to Wedding for $550,000 US in cryptocurrency.

Gomez, who is listed as a fugitive living in Mexico, faces six charges, including drug offences and one count of attempting to transact and deal with a "specially designated narcotics trafficker."

The charges unsealed against Vazquez and Gomez add to a flurry of law enforcement activity over the past week in the Wedding case.

Ryan Wedding's alleged second-in-command, Canadian Andrew Clark, was arrested in Mexico in October 2024 in an operation involving Interpol and the Mexican navy. (Omar García Harfuch/Facebook)

The FBI announced the arrest in Colombia last week of a Mexican judge accused of accepting $2 million US in bribes to free Wedding's alleged second-in-command, Andrew Clark.

On Wednesday, Mexican authorities are expected to auction off 61 rare and high-performance motorcycles seized last year from properties linked to Wedding. The FBI previously estimated the collection was worth $40 million US.

The U.S. treasury also announced sanctions against Iran-linked firms in the Toronto and Vancouver areas accused of helping Wedding launder billions of dollars in drug proceeds.

CBC News senior reporter Thomas Daigle has extensively covered the case of Ryan Wedding. He can be reached by email at thomas.daigle@cbc.ca.

World.title: Three months after 7.5M earthquake struck Colombia, “reconstruction hasn’t begun”
World.content:
Human rights officials warned on Tuesday that the reconstruction of west Colombia, which was partially destroyed by an August 10 earthquake, fails to show progress.

In a statement, the Ombudsman’s Office warned that “difficulties persist in providing assistance to and supporting the recovery of affected communities, particularly with regard to housing, access to essential services, the protection of rights, and funding for response measures.”

The top human rights official of Pereira, Leonardo Fabio Reales, told Caracol Radio that “the reconstruction of the city has not begun. There isn’t even a rough outline of what is planned to be done after the earthquake.”

Pereira is among the hardest hit by the 7.4M earthquake that destroyed more than 123,000 homes, and hundreds of hospitals and schools.

More than 450 people continue to live in tents in temporary camps that were set up in Pereira and cities like Buenaventura, according to the Ombudsman, which raised the alarm over “the lack of clear protocols for closing shelters and providing housing alternatives for departing residents, alongside infrastructure and security deficiencies in several facilities.”

Promised rent assistance, which would allow those who lost their homes to temporarily find residence, has also been insufficient.

“More than a month ago I received a million pesos ($304) stipend, although this was supposed to be three, I haven’t received any news,” Pereira resident Christian Castañeda told France 24.

“They’ve announced a so-called ‘Miracle Fund,’ but so far we’ve only seen billboards—no major progress,” said Castañeda, whose mother is one of more than 3,000 people who have yet to receive financial aid.

This Miracle Fund was set up a few weeks ago with an initial COP625 billion ($190 million) budget, which is only a drop in the COP59.29 trillion (18 billion) bucket that the government must get together for the reconstruction process.

“I’m not sure whether the Miracle Fund is working with the diligence and sense of urgency that are required, nor am I sure that they are doing so in the most transparent way,” said House Representative Catherine Juvinao, a member of the congressional commission that monitors the recovery process.

According to Senator Alejandro Toro, local governments from parts of the country that weren’t affected by the earthquake have also tried to receive emergency funds.

Sixteen departments were listed as affected—16, when everyone knows only 5 were actually impacted. It turns out that among these 16, certain departments reported every single public building and school as damaged. For instance: in Caqueta, according to the governor, there are more affected municipalities than families. No one knows the true number of victims in Caqueta; the press didn’t cover a single damaged house there. In Bolivar, along the Atlantic Coast, 11 families were reported affected—and do you know how many total people were listed under those 11 families? 467 people from 11 families! That averages to 43 people per family! Come on, that is completely false! That is a lie; it’s not as if every household belongs to [vallenato singer] Diomedes. They also reported about 189 damaged schools, which would mean 12 or 13 damaged schools per family… impossible. This same issue occurred across other departments—16 departments, including Sucre!

Senator Alejandro Ocampo

Ocampo said he would continue his lawsuits against the foundation of First Lady Ana Lucia Pineda, Colombia Luz y Sonrisas, which has failed to comply with court orders ordering transparency on what it has done with money collected in response to the earthquake.

World.title: De la Espriella claims ELN plans to attack Colombia’s corporate media
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella ordered State forces to protect corporate media, claiming alerts over “possible terrorist attacks by the ELN” guerrilla group.

De la Espriella said he issued “specific instructions to ensure that the full capacity of the State is directed toward protecting” private television networks RCN and Caracol, “their journalists, employees, and families” on social media platform X.

The president said he also ordered to increase the protection of Semana, a far-right magazine owned by the main sponsor of his campaign, the Gilinksi family.

Freedom of the press is sacred and must be respected! No narco-terrorist group will silence the media through threats, intimidation, or acts of violence. President Abelardo de la Espriella

According to the Bogota Mayor’s Office, the orders were issued hours after the prosecution’s Technical Investigations Unit issued a “security alert” to the media outlets and the local government.

In a response, Caracol evacuated its main office in the capital and allowed police to search the premise for bombs without result.

Press freedom foundation FLIP said that “we reject and express our profound concerns over the alerts of possible attacks against media in Bogota.”

“The fact that no explosives have been found does not mean that the risk has ended. These alerts require monitoring and effective protection,” the FLIP said on X.

The alert was issued amid increased violence between guerrilla groups and State forces, who have been ordered to carry out an offensive against insurgencies and organized crime groups by the president.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP announces steep measures after being forced to cut $53M from its budget
World.content:
The president of the JEP announced radical cuts in the war crimes tribunal’s spending, which was forced to cut $53 million (COP170 billion) from its annual budget by Colombia’s Congress.

In a press statement, JEP president Danilo Rojas said that the court would abandon its 15,000m² main office in Bogota and move to a much smaller building in March of next year.

The court president additionally announced that it would eliminate 85% of its temporary employees and force staff to absorb administrative, technical defense, and psychosocial tasks previously handled by external contractors.

Many of the remaining workers will largely be working from home to facilitate the aforementioned move.

The court will also abandon personal security details for magistrates and the court directors and ask the National Protection Unit to take on the protection of victims, witnesses and defendants.

Last but not least, the court announced partnerships with universities, the Inspector General’s Office and local governments to secure regional presence, which is necessary to investigate war crimes.

The radical austerity measures became a necessity after Congress agreed with President Abelardo de la Espriella and hi far-right National Salvation party to slash the JEP’s budget.

The war crimes tribunal seeks justice for millions of victims of the military and the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC, which agreed to demobilize and disarm in 2016.

The JEP has long been the target of criticism of the far-right, which has historically downplayed the war crimes committed by the State and regional elites that used the armed conflict to accumulate wealth.

World.title: Colombia’s labor unions and social organizations call national strike on November 19
World.content:
Colombia’s main labor unions and a collection of civil society organizations called a national strike “against the fascist government of Abelardo de la Espriella and his tax reform” bill.

In a press statement, the organizations accused De la Espriella of, among other things, dismantling the “social, environmental, trade union, and labor rights achieved during the government of Gustavo Petro,” and surrendering sovereignty and kneeling before the imperialist government of the United States.”

The government of Abelardo, like that of Duque and Carrasquilla, intends to reach into the pockets of the people and privilege the ultra-rich with its “economic rescue” bill, which imposes a 19% VAT on food and other basic goods in the family basket, higher taxes on earned income, raises health contributions up to 8%, and conversely reduces the corporate capital income tax from 35% to 31%, eliminates the wealth tax in 2031, and reduces the capital gains tax to 20% for investments in 2027 and 2028. Civil society organizations

The organizations additionally accused the government of seeking special powers to facilitate the privatization of state-controlled companies like oil firm Ecopetrol.

The organizations said they united with the main opposition party, the Historic Pact, “with the purpose of opposing this fascist government and decisively participating in the National Strike.”

The National Strike on November 19 constitutes a new stage in the organization and expression of growing popular discontent, which was also manifested in the successful national mobilization day of October 14. It is about strengthening a collective action process capable of confronting the Government’s regressive measures, demanding respect for hard-won rights, and opposing the deepening of its neoliberal and authoritarian project. Civil society organizations

The last time a national strike was organized was in 2021 when the labor unions and their allies from civil society shut down parts of the country for months.

At the time, a tax reform propose by former President Ivan Duque triggered the initiative.

World.title: Colombia’s government presents “Economic Rescue Bill”
World.content:
Colombia’s Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo on Thursday presented an Economic Rescue Bill that seeks to reduce government spending and increase its revenue.

The bill grants extraordinary powers to President Abelardo de la Espriella to slash government spending by decree and includes a tax reform that includes higher sales tax rates on gasoline, coffee, cigarettes and vegetables.

The bill also includes tax breaks for corporations in an attempt to increase investment.

Abelardo’s extraordinary powers

While on campaign, De la Espriella powers vowed a 40% reduction of the State, which the bill falls short of doing.

Article 7 of the bill does grant the president extraordinary powers to “abolish, merge, and split ministries and administrative departments, as well as to determine or modify their names, objectives, and organizational structure,” and allows De la Espriella to “abolish, merge, split, and change the legal status” of other State bodies like the superintendencies, agencies, special administrative units, and public institutions.

Article 96 allows the government to change the personnel hiring of tax agency DIAN, which “would allow for the elimination of annual competitive exams for entry into the DIAN and a return to the practice of appointing thousands of officials,” according to former DIAN director Luis Carlos Reyes.

Last but not least, the bill mandates a 20% reduction in salaries of State employees, excluding the security forces, and cut half of the costs in temporary contracts.

VAT reforms and squeezing the middle class

The bill seeks to remove popular products like cocoa, coffee, sugar and fruits from a VAT exemption list and introduce a 19% sales tac on them.

An increase in taxes on gasoline will inflate its price.

The bill additionally seeks to charge VAT on vice products like liquor and cigarettes, which would make them up to 53% more expensive.

The bulk of these tax increases wouldn’t take fore until after the November 2027 local and regional elections in an apparent compromise to Congress and Colombia’s political forces.

In an attempt to not impoverish the poor, the bill seeks a mechanism that would refund up to 100% of IVA payments to some 19 million of the country’s poorest citizens.

The increased pressure on the middle class has already resulted in opposition from within De la Espriella’s congressional coalition.

Tax benefits for the capitalists

The government seeks to gradually lower the corporate income tax from 35% to 31% and offer a reduced tax rate for large companies that decide to invest in new enterprises.

According to the Inter-American Development Bank, a similar scheme introduced by former President Alvaro Uribe “was ineffective in promoting investment.”

World.title: Accusations over De la Espriella’s narco ties “lack conclusive or solid evidence,” says Colombia’s justice minister
World.content:
Colombia’s Justice Minister, Ivan Cancino, downplayed the evidence of ties between President Abelardo de la Espriella and drug traffickers that was displayed in Congress by opposition Senator Ivan Cepeda.

In a video, Cancino said that “political oversight is a fundamental tool of our democracy. However, it cannot become an arena for launching accusations without proving and substantiating them.”

The justice minister admitted that the pieces of evidence provided to Congress “may seem serious,” but “lack conclusive or solid evidence, as well as any support that could jeopardize the innocence and the presumption of innocence of our president.”

It is not just about displaying organizational charts, deeds from over a decade ago, and business transactions to construct a narrative that supports neither judicial decisions nor the documentary, testimonial, circumstantial, or expert backing required for these types of accusations. Ivan Cancino

Cancino accused the opposition of remaining “silent regarding the grave scandals involving corruption, drug trafficking, and even alleged sexual abuse, as well as fiscal irresponsibility and possible links to criminal organizations that surrounded the previous government. ”

The justice minister was forced to come out after Cepeda showed Congress evidence of De la Espriella’s business ties with multiple convicted drug traffickers and announced criminal complaints against the president.

De la Espriella’s law firm rose to prominence during the demobilization of paramilitary organization AUC with whom he created a foundation that sought to justify the paramilitary violence that terrorized much of Colombia in the 1990’s and 2000s.

Once the ties between the AUC and elected politicians became known, the president ended up defending many of the “parapoliticians” in court.

According to Cepeda, De la Espriella plays a key role in a “revolving door” system that could end up benefiting the very drug traffickers and corrupt politicians that have paid the president for his legal defense in the past.

World.title: Colombia’s opposition announces criminal charges against De la Espriella over ties to drug traffickers
World.content:
Colombia’s opposition leader, senator Ian Cepeda, accused President Abelardo de la Espriella of leading an agrarian counter-reform designed to benefit land-owning clans and convicted drug traffickers.

During a congressional debate, Cepeda claimed that De la Espriella put allies of drug traffickers and paramilitaries in charge of key state institutions responsible for land distribution and asset forfeiture.

The president and his appointees are part of a revolving door system of people who, before being appointed to government positions, defended the interests of drug traffickers and paramilitaries associated with De la Espriella and his businesses, according to the opposition leader.

For example, the president put Diana Patrica Bravo, a former prosecutor and partner at his law firm De la Espriella Lawyers, in charge of The Society of Special Assets (SAE), which controls assets that were seized from drug traffickers.

The leader of the leftist Historic Pact party showed financial statements of one of De la Espriella’s companies, Dominio De la Espriella, that would prove that in between 38% and 40% of its capital deposits came from the family and corporate network of Hugues Rodríguez, a.k.a. Comandante Barbie, a former paramilitary financier who was charged with drug trafficking in the US.

The SAE would control more than 130 properties of Comandante Barbie.

De la Espriella family construction firm, Cosenza S.A.S., made property purchases in the city of Monteria directly with individuals under investigation for money laundering and illicit enrichment, according to Cepeda.

The president’s ex-wife, Yoly Beatriz Illidge, was appointed Superintendent of Notaries, making her “directly responsible for inspecting and monitoring all land entries and records issued by restitution judges throughout the country,” according to Cepeda.

De la Espriella is an associate of drug traffickers, owns assets purchased from drug traffickers, and defends drug traffickers from within the national government. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Last but not least, Agriculture Minister Indalecio Dangond “arrived at this post to execute an agrarian counter-reform at the service of paramilitary land-grabbers, foreign capital, and agro-industrial partners” while blocking investments for small farmers and displacement victims, the opposition leader stated.

Cepeda vowed that he would give the dossier to the United States Department of Justcie and to “Congressmen of the Democratic Party, given that mister De la Espriella is a US citizen.”

The opposition leader additionally promised to file criminal charges against the president and his agriculture minister in Colombia.

World.title: Colombia’s government claims Petro exploited 48 women as president
World.content:
The administration chief of Colombia’s President Abelardo De la Espriella told Congress that former President Gustavo Petro hired at least 48 women who were “trapped and exploited” for presidential parties.

During a hearing, DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios claimed that Petro had 48 women “working in the Presidency, who were unfortunately exploited through temporary work contracts.”

We’re going to prove this to the Colombian people: how, unfortunately, the Casa de Nariño was set up, organized, and designed not for governing, but for partying there every day, bringing women there and engaging in behavior we should not be engaging in—behavior that sets a bad example. DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios

“Forty-eight women are already speaking with us about how, through a contract and an OPS, they were trapped and exploited in order to be with President Petro,” said Rios.

Former DAPRE director Angie Rodriguez, who was sacked by Petro in July, doubled down on her successor’s allegations and asked the former president to prove that the president managed a network of women, including child transvestites.

Were there transvestite children there? Answer me, Mr. President. Were there transvestite children there? I am asking you a question, and I have every right to ask it. Were there? And if there weren’t, uh… prove that what I am saying is a lie. Angie Rodriguez

Last but not least, far-right magazine Semana published an interview with a woman identified as Deicy Jimenez, who claimed she as hired by Petro after meeting him on an adult website.

Jimenez even told Semana’s former presidential candidate Vicky Davila she trafficked drugs for the former president when he was senator.

VD: What happened on the day you say you transported drugs for Petro? DJ: Yes, I was traveling, and he asked me as a favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Were you outside of Bogotá? DJ: Yes. VD: How do you recall that favor Petro asked of you? DJ: He asked me as the favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Did you buy them? DJ: Yes, I bought them somewhere. He gave me money. VD: Did he give it to you in cash or deposit it for you? DJ: In cash. VD: How much money? DJ: Three million pesos. VD: What kind of drugs did you buy? DJ: Cocaine. VD: Where did you buy it? DJ: I bought it from some people. I can’t say (publicly) their names or the location. VD: Is it a gang? DJ: Yes. VD: Did he know you were going to buy the drugs from that gang? DJ: Yes. VD: At that time, was he a senator or the president? DJ: A senator. VD: How did you bring that drug in? DJ: I brought it through the airport. VD: You mean, on a plane? DJ: Yeah. VD: Did you get on a plane with Petro’s drugs? DJ: Yes. VD: How were the drugs packaged? DJ: In bags. VD: Like individual doses? DJ: Yes. VD: And where did you hide the drugs? DJ: In my suitcase.

In a response, Petro denied having hired women for sex and claimed that the far-right attack were the result of authorities’ failure to sustain corruption allegations.

World.title: Sunrise Movement Co-Founder Elected to Congress on Anti-Data Center Platform
World.content:
By Democracy Now

HAVANA TIMES – Progressive candidate Will Lawrence of Michigan has defeated Republican incumbent Tom Barrett, flipping the state’s 7th Congressional District, a closely watched swing district that includes Lansing. Lawrence, the co-founder of the youth-led climate organization Sunrise Movement, refused corporate PAC money, instead building a people-powered grassroots mobilization campaign. He focused on lowering the costs of housing and healthcare, opposing the war on Iran, and challenging the power of Big Tech.

“I’m fighting for a federal moratorium on new data center development, along with a pause on advanced AI development,” says Lawrence. “These developers come into small towns, and they say, ’We’re going to suck up a bunch of water. We’re going to use more energy than the current capacity of the grid. We don’t know what’s going to happen to your property values, but if everything goes well, we’re going to put 10 or 20 million people out of work, and if it goes poorly, we may kill everybody by accident.’”

Lawrence also says he will back Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker, but that he will demand Democratic leadership listen to progressive concerns.

Transcript

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman, with Juan Gonzalez.

In Michigan, progressive candidate Will Lawrence has defeated Republican incumbent Tom Barrett, flipping a closely watched swing district that includes Lansing. Lawrence is the co-founder of the youth-led climate group the Sunrise Movement. He ran a grassroots campaign focused on lowering the cost of housing and healthcare, opposing the war in Iran, and challenging the power of Big Tech.

One of the central issues of Lawrence’s campaign was opposition to artificial intelligence, AI, data centers. He called for a pause on the construction of new centers, joining residents’ concerns about their impact on Michigan’s water, electricity bills, quality of life, including noise pollution. Three hyperscale data centers have been proposed in different parts of the district. Lawrence also campaigned against Flock surveillance cameras and called for tighter restrictions on AI overall.

The race was one of the most expensive House contests in the country, $66 million spent on political advertising.

But Will Lawrence is now in Washington, D.C. The congressmember-elect is there for orientation.

Congressmember-elect Will Lawrence, welcome to Democracy Now! If you can start off by —

REP.-ELECT WILL LAWRENCE: Thank you.

AMY GOODMAN: — talking about what you’re planning to bring to Congress, and then respond to what’s happening? The House leader race is underway. There’s going to be an internal vote, I think, next week, with Congressmember Hakeem Jeffries as the House speaker. But there are those who are questioning that leadership. I’m wondering if you can talk about that, as well.

REP.-ELECT WILL LAWRENCE: Thank you, Amy. It’s a real honor to be here. Longtime fan of the show.

You know, I’m just thrilled to be here to offer independent-minded representation for my district. People voted to get Big Money out of politics, to hold Big Tech accountable, to stop these endless wars around the world and to bring our money home to invest in first things first, good jobs and education, housing and healthcare, so that we can all look forward to the future again. And I just couldn’t be more honored to represent the people of my district.

And, you know, I’ve been getting the correspondence from my constituents over the last number of days, you know, expressing concern about who the next speaker is going to be. And I do want to make clear that I’ve said since July that I will support Hakeem for speaker. I’m a man of my word, and I intend to keep that word. But the correspondence is very important, not just in my district, but I’m hearing from all my other incoming freshmen here that they’re also hearing the same thing. And it reflects the anxiety that people feel that this election, which was clearly about change and a repudiation of the status quo, could result in more of the same. And they’re hungry to know that it’s going to be different and the Democratic Party is truly going to fight for real reform in our economy and our democracy. And people doubt that that will happen because of leadership’s well-documented ties to Big Money, including weapons manufacturers and health insurance CEOs and AIPAC and many others.

And so, I’m going to push Leader Jeffries publicly, and I will push him privately, to hear those concerns and commit to giving voice to the American people by putting votes on the floor that reflect the issues that I and people across the country campaigned on. We need to have a vote to block the bombs to Israel. We need to have a vote to guarantee healthcare to every person in my district. And we need to have a vote to get Big Money out of politics and ban super PACs, because people deserve to know that their representatives actually represent them rather than the wealthy elite. And as long as we have this Big Money in politics, they will never be able to be confident in that knowledge. So, regardless of the speaker’s own positions on those issues, he can give voice to the American people by putting those votes on the floor and letting us have those votes, regardless of where he personally comes down on the issue. And I’m going to be pushing hard to ensure that that happens.

JUAN GONZALEZ: Well, Will Lawrence, one of the big planks of your campaign was your opposition to these data centers and AI regulation, Flock cameras. Now that you are — will be in Congress, and I expect, if history is any lesson at all, the tech industry will start shifting more money to Democrats, hoping to peel people off and be able to neutralize any major legislation, what are your red lines, and what are you expecting to be able to accomplish when it comes to AI regulation, these data centers and Flock cameras?

REP.-ELECT WILL LAWRENCE: Well, what I hear from residents across my district is that this is out of control, it’s moving too fast, and we need to slow it down. And they’re fighting on a playing field that is fundamentally rigged to the benefit of these billion-, soon to be trillion-dollar corporations in Silicon Valley and leaves local communities behind.

So, I’m fighting for a federal moratorium on new data center development, along with a pause on advanced AI development. I mean, these developers come into small towns, and they say, you know, “We’re going to suck up a bunch of water. We’re going to use more energy than the current capacity of the grid. We don’t know what’s going to happen to your property values, but if everything goes well, we’re going to put 10 or 20 million people out of work, and if it goes poorly, we may kill everybody by accident.” I mean, what are we talking about? What are we talking about? Why have we allowed these clearly reckless individuals, who do not share the values and aspirations of my constituents in Michigan, to determine the future of our entire economy?

You know, I believe that AI could be used for the benefit of humanity, but right now it’s on track to make the already rich and powerful even richer and more powerful. And that’s why there is such a bottom-up grassroots rebellion happening, not just in my district, but around the country. And it’s uniting Democrats and Republicans from the bottom up who do not trust Big Tech to write the future of our communities and our entire economy.

JUAN GONZALEZ: And could you comment about what made it possible, despite all this money poured into the — into your district to defeat you, that you were able to emerge victorious?

REP.-ELECT WILL LAWRENCE: Well, we had an unprecedented ground game. You know, I’m an organizer by trade. I was a co-founder of the Sunrise Movement. I’ve been an organizer fighting alongside renters and tenants to assert our rights and prevent homelessness in my area. And we built a ground game that knocked on 350,000 doors between the primary and the general election. And when there were so many negative ads on TV, so many lies and so many smears, it was those face-to-face conversations, eye contact, a handshake, a real human being coming to you and talking about the values that we share and the future we can build together, that cut through all the noise. And that’s what allowed us to win this election. And I’m just tremendously proud of all the volunteers, the whole team, everybody who poured into the movement. It was a true team effort, and I couldn’t be more honored to be representing that movement here in Congress.

AMY GOODMAN: Congressmember-elect Will Lawrence of Michigan, thank you so much for being with us as you stand there in Washington at orientation for new congressmembers. He defeated incumbent Republican Congressmember Tom Barrett in one of the most competitive swing House races these midterms, co-founder of the Sunrise Movement.

Read more interviews here on Havana Times.

World.title: International News Briefs for Tuesday, November 10, 2026
World.content:
HAVANA TIMES – We bring you some of the top international news stories compiled by Democracy Now on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

GOP Rep. Thomas Massie Introduces Articles of Impeachment Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth

Nov 10, 2026

Republican Congressmember Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday for “high crimes and misdemeanors.” The eight impeachment articles accuse Hegseth of violating the 1973 War Powers Resolution by continuing to attack Iran even after both chambers of Congress ordered the Trump administration to stop. He’s also accused of illegally waging war against Yemen, ignoring laws designed to reduce civilian casualties, overseeing “extrajudicial killings” in attacks on boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific, abducting Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro without congressional authorization, and suppressing the free speech rights of Democratic Senator Mark Kelly in retaliation for reminding troops not to obey illegal orders. Congressmember Massie outlined the charges during a speech from the House floor.

Rep. Thomas Massie: “Wherefore, Secretary of Defense Peter Hegseth, by such conduct, has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law, Peter Brian Hegseth thus warrants impeachment and trial, removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust or profit under the United States.”

It’s expected the House will vote on Hegseth’s impeachment on Wednesday. Only a few Republican defectors would be needed for a simple majority, setting up a Senate trial on whether to remove Hegseth. On Monday, President Trump said he would stand by Hegseth if he’s impeached.

Pentagon Retreats from Second U.K. Base Due to Alleged Threat from Iran

Nov 10, 2026

The Wall Street Journal reports the Pentagon has evacuated aircraft from a second base in the United Kingdom due to another alleged threat from Iran. U.S. refueling tankers were reportedly moved from a base in Mildenhall on Monday. Last month, the Pentagon pulled B-1 bombers out of another British base.

Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says two more ships, including a supertanker, are on fire near the Strait of Hormuz after using what Iranian officials have called an “unauthorized route.” Iran has claimed 11 strikes on ships over a 10-day span. The continued attacks on shipping came as Iran’s Foreign Ministry said it could reopen the strait within 48 hours if the U.S. agrees to Tehran’s list of demands.

Esmail Baghaei: “If the U.S. meets the demands put forward by Iran, the situation in the region could see a positive shift in as little as two days, and security in the Strait of Hormuz could also be restored.”

On Monday, President Trump spoke with Qatar’s prime minister, who’s acted as a mediator in efforts to end the war. After the talks, Trump claimed there was “positive momentum” in negotiations for a deal with Iran.

President Donald Trump: “The military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes. Israel and the entire Middle East are protected from Iranian danger and threats, and we’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.”

Since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, Trump has claimed more than 40 times that the war was close to an end, that a deal was near, or that the war was already over.

Trump Raises New Election Conspiracy Theory After Democrats Sweep Midterms

Nov 10, 2026

Image Credit: Lauren Boebert for Congress

Democrats are continuing to build on their historic wins in last week’s midterm elections as votes continue to be counted. In Mississippi, Scott Colom’s lead over Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith has topped 2,500 votes, with just two batches of ballots left to be counted before a Friday deadline to certify the results.

In Colorado, Republican Congressmember Lauren Boebert is trailing in her bid to hold on to her seat. On Monday, CNN projected Boebert will lose the race to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired U.S. Navy admiral who served on the National Security Council under President Joe Biden.

On Monday, President Trump reversed his previous comment that he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results of the midterm elections. Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???”

Schumer Faces Pressure to Step Aside as Chris Van Hollen Hints at Run for Senate Majority Leader

Nov 10, 2026

Senate Democrats could be headed for a leadership shakeup, after Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen indicated Monday he’s open to running for Senate majority leader when the new Congress convenes in January. A source close to Van Hollen told Politico the Maryland Democrat is thinking about a run after he “received an outpouring of calls and is now in active listening mode. The door is not shut.”

This comes as a growing number of Senate Democrats have called for new leadership or refused to commit to supporting New York Senator Chuck Schumer for majority leader. Joining the call is a major labor union, the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, which wrote in a letter to Schumer on Monday, “We believe this is the right moment for a new generation to lead Senate Democrats.”

Meanwhile, Connecticut Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal said he’s open to new leadership if a challenger to Schumer emerges.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal: “But we need to have a conversation about leadership going forward, because we need new energy and ideas.”

Senate Advances Bill to Speed Construction of Fossil Fuel Projects and Data Centers

Nov 10, 2026

Image Credit: USA TODAY Network

In more news from Capitol Hill, the Senate voted 73 to 25 Monday to take up a sweeping permitting reform bill. It was advanced by nearly every Republican and 22 Democrats. Environmental groups have called the legislation an “aggressive attack on federal environmental protections in order to facilitate rapid, unregulated development of fracked gas power plants, dirty fossil fuel pipelines, and expensive hyperscale data centers.” Meanwhile, Indigenous leaders, including New Mexico Governor-elect Deb Haaland, argue the bill would undermine tribal sovereignty.

More than 160 health, consumer, religious and environmental groups are calling on Congress to instead pass the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act. It’s sponsored by Michigan democratic socialist Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, who said, “[The] elections send a clear message that Americans want their representatives to protect their health and environment, not sell them out to Big Tech and Big Oil.”

5 Arrested at Anthropic’s NYC Offices as Protesters Demand Halt to IPO Plans

Nov 10, 2026

Here in New York, activists with Climate Defenders, New York Communities for Change and Planet Over Profit protested at Anthropic’s Manhattan offices for over an hour on Monday. Five of them were arrested for blocking the employee security entrance. The protesters blasted Anthropic’s moves toward an initial public offering that could see it valued at $1.4 trillion — far less than previous estimates it could be worth as much as $2 trillion. This comes after major global tech stocks fell sharply last week following the U.S. midterm elections, which sparked concerns among investors that the Democratic takeover of both chambers of Congress will mean tougher regulation of AI. This is activist Jonathan Westin speaking to Democracy Now! as he was being arrested.

Jonathan Westin: “I’m getting arrested because we’re trying to stop Anthropic from crashing the global economy, along with AI. They are not worth the paper they’re printed on. Millions and millions of lives will be affected by it.”

African National Congress Suffers Its Worst Election Result Since South Africa Ended Apartheid

Nov 10, 2026

In South Africa, the African National Congress, the party of Nelson Mandela, suffered its worst results in local elections on Sunday. The ANC won just 31% of the vote, though it remains South Africa’s largest party. Its main rival, the Democratic Alliance, said it won the votes of more than 1 million Black South ⁠Africans for the first time.

Dozens Drown in Capsized Boats While Attempting to Reach European Soil

Nov 10, 2026

At least 39 migrants have died after a small wooden boat capsized off the Atlantic coast of Senegal as it tried to reach Spain’s Canary Islands. This year alone, the Spanish immigrant rights group Walking Borders has recorded over 600 migrants’ deaths in the Atlantic, as more people desperately flee war, famine and climate disasters and attempt to reach Europe. This comes as at least 22 people have died while attempting to reach Greece from Libya over the course of three days.

U.S. Cancels Deportation Flight of Iranians at Last Minute

Nov 10, 2026

Back in the United States, a deportation flight carrying Iranian nationals to Iran via Pakistan was abruptly canceled Sunday morning, after at least eight Iranians had been loaded onto a plane in Mesa, Arizona, bound first for the Republic of Georgia. The flight would reportedly have been the first deportation of Iranians since the U.S. launched attacks on Iran in February. Back in October, U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes ordered the U.S. government to give the court 24-hour notice of any plans to deport Iranians to Iran or to any other country, and five days’ written notice before deportation is carried out.

ICE Detains 8-Year-Old Haitian Boy in San Diego After Routine Immigration Check-In

Nov 10, 2026

Image Credit: NBC San Diego

In San Diego, an 8-year-old Haitian boy is in federal custody after ICE detained him at a scheduled immigration appointment. He had been living with his uncle since his father was deported last year. DHS says the uncle could not establish legal guardianship. Guerline Jozef, executive director of Haitian Bridge Alliance, said, “This is not child protection. This is state-inflicted trauma disguised as immigration enforcement. An eight-year-old child should be sitting in a classroom, learning, playing, and dreaming about his future, not being taken away and retraumatized by armed federal agents. His father has already been taken from him and deported, now this administration has stripped him of the stability, family, and community every child deserves.”

SCOTUS Allows Trump Admin to Resume Border Wall Construction in Big Bend National Park

Nov 10, 2026

Image Credit: X/@LaikenJordahl

The U.S. Supreme Court is allowing the Trump administration to resume the construction of a new border wall in Big Bend National Park and along more than 500 miles of the Rio Grande in Texas. Monday’s ruling lifted a lower court’s temporary injunction that blocked construction back in October while a lawsuit filed by the Center for Biological Diversity and others is resolved. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only Supreme Court member to dissent. Click here to see our coverage of this story.

Proposed USDA Policy Would Cut Food Aid for Millions of People

Nov 10, 2026

An estimated 6.3 million people in the U.S. could lose their food assistance by 2029 over a new proposed policy set forth by the Department of Agriculture. The Republican-backed measure would toughen restrictions on people’s eligibility for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. The policy change could also leave millions of children without access to free school meals.

New York Focus Uncovers 2023 Sexual Assault Lawsuit by Two Former Cornell Students

Nov 10, 2026

The news outlet New York Focus has uncovered a 2023 lawsuit in which two former Cornell students say the university’s Title IX office ignored their complaints that the same male student sexually assaulted them in 2018 and 2021. A complaint filed by one of the students and their lawyer says, “At least five to ten others are known to have been sexually abused and it is believed that many more were abused but have yet to come forward.” Cornell University and the male student tried to have the case dismissed, but a trial is scheduled for next year. The lawsuit follows another high-profile lawsuit filed by Jane Doe in September over an alleged fraternity gang rape at Cornell in 2024, prompting a massive public outcry and leading to New York Attorney General Letitia James ordering a new investigation.

Russell Brand Sentenced to 10.5 Years in Prison

Nov 10, 2026

In the United Kingdom, the comedian, actor and podcaster Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for raping a fan and sexually assaulting three other women. The abuses occurred between 2004 and 2009 at the peak of Brand’s career. This is Judge Joel Bennathan.

Judge Joel Bennathan: “About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous. You were clever and, in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator.”

Proposition 40 Billionaire Tax Fails to Pass in California

Nov 10, 2026

In California, Proposition 40, a one-time 5% wealth tax on individuals and trusts with over $1 billion in assets, has failed to pass. Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom was an opponent of the wealth tax, while Democratic Congressmember Ro Khanna of California was in favor of the tax.

Online Magazine Salon Closes After 31 Years of Publication

Nov 10, 2026

The progressive online magazine Salon has abruptly shut down after 31 years of publication. Salon was widely celebrated as a trailblazer for digital journalism after it was founded in 1995.

Palestinian American Ahmed Moor Launches 2028 Democratic Primary Challenge Against Sen. Fetterman

Nov 10, 2026

Image Credit: Moor for Senate

In Pennsylvania, the Gaza-born Palestinian American writer and businessman Ahmed Moor launched a 2028 Democratic primary challenge Monday against Senator John Fetterman, who is an ardent defender of Israel. Moor is a regular columnist at publications including The Guardian and The Nation. He’s running as a democratic socialist, connecting U.S. military aid to Israel and the Trump administration’s war on Iran to the rising cost of living. This is Ahmed Moor speaking with Democracy Now! in 2024 about his family in Gaza.

Ahmed Moor: “My family has experienced direct loss through the genocide. Most recently, my cousin’s 19-year-old son was killed by an Israeli sniper in Rafah. And so, the urgency surrounding this lawsuit goes to the fact that the conditions are getting worse. The danger that people are exposed to continues even as we speak.”

Read more news here on Havana Times.

World.title: El Salvador’s Costly Military Adventure in Haiti
World.content:
Amid unmet needs at home

Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, alongside his Peruvian counterpart Keiko Fujimori, during her visit to El Salvador on October 29, 2026. That day, the president declined to specify the cost of the military operation in Haiti—an operation his government claims to be 90% funding. Image: Presidency of El Salvador

By Edgardo Ayala (IPS)

HAVANA TIMES – As if El Salvador were a global economic powerhouse with resources to spare, President Nayib Bukele is pressing ahead with his risky military gamble in Haiti, where some 2,000 Salvadoran troops have been searching since late October for four of their missing comrades following an ambush by gangs.

That a poor country like El Salvador, with serious social needs, would embark on such an operation continues to surprise analysts both locally and across the region, considering the economic cost of maintaining a military contingent in the Caribbean nation.

Although overall poverty affected 22.5% of Salvadoran households in 2025, slightly below the 22.8% recorded in 2019, the year Bukele took office in El Salvador, extreme poverty rose from 4.5% to 7.67% during that period, according to household surveys from those years.

According to Bukele, El Salvador is covering 90% of the financial cost of the deployment in Haiti. However, the president did not disclose the estimated total, despite being asked directly by a journalist at a press conference in San Salvador on October 29.

“Obviously, I don’t think the cost is low. I suspect that when he says 90% is covered by El Salvador’s budget, he means that those troops are not receiving any additional salary beyond what they already earn as members of the Salvadoran Armed Forces,” economist Carlos Acevedo told IPS.

The new deployment followed the disappearance of four Salvadoran aviation technicians on October 18, 2026, after an ambush in Croix-des-Bouquets, on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince, the country’s capital.

They were part of the contingent supporting the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF).

Bukele, a leader who has drifted toward authoritarianism and aligned himself with the far right, announced the rescue operation on October 21. By October 28, the press was reporting that approximately 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers were in Haiti.

UN spokespersons have been careful to clarify that Bukele’s forces are not part of the GSF and that only 200 Salvadoran personnel had been operating under its mandate before the four aviation technicians were abducted.

Emboldened by his success in subduing El Salvador’s violent gangs through a hardline crackdown launched in March 2022, the Salvadoran president has claimed that he can also eliminate Haiti’s criminal groups.

To carry out his plan in El Salvador, he resorted to a state of emergency that continues to suspend several constitutional guarantees. To date, more than 90,000 people have been arrested, most of them gang members who had previously been identified and located.

Haiti’s longstanding crisis worsened, descending into collapse and a breakdown of governance following the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in July 2021. Gangs took advantage of the power vacuum to expand their control over Port-au-Prince and other areas through killings, kidnappings, and control of transportation routes and services.

Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé will visit El Salvador on November 16 and 17 to participate in an international conference on democracy and discuss the future of Salvadoran troops in Haiti, according to an announcement made by Vice President Félix Ulloa on November 6.

However, in a country where secrecy surrounding the president’s activities is common, it remains unclear whether Fils-Aimé will meet with Bukele.

Salvadoran soldiers in formation in San Salvador. The deployment of approximately 2,000 military personnel to Haiti—an operation of uncertain nature—raises questions regarding El Salvador’s public spending priorities, at a time when deep-seated social deficiencies persist. Image: Office of the President of El Salvador

Poor Country, Grandiose Ambitions

To cover the transportation of troops and military equipment to Haiti, probably the most expensive component of the operation, El Salvador has received support primarily from the United States, whose president, Donald Trump, has backed the operation in Haiti.

The United States contributed at least one C-130 military transport aircraft to move personnel and military equipment, according to confirmation provided to the Miami Herald by a spokesperson for US Southern Command. It is unknown whether Washington has provided other forms of military assistance.

“I don’t know how much the day-to-day logistics cost over there. I imagine it depends on the activity, whether ammunition is being used, how intensive the patrols are, and now with diesel prices through the roof, those kinds of expenses,” said Acevedo, a former president of El Salvador’s Central Reserve Bank.

He added: “But I suspect that the United States must be providing substantial support for those kinds of costs.”

As the Salvadoran operation continues, the financial resources being invested in the military campaign in Haiti, whatever the amount, could instead be used to strengthen social services in El Salvador, such as healthcare and education.

That was the view expressed by a 55-year-old Salvadoran barber as he rested in a plaza in downtown San Salvador, the country’s capital.

“We approve of what the president has done here, putting an end to the gangs. We all support him, and it’s good to go rescue our fellow countrymen, but I think it’s very risky,” said the barber, who asked that his name not be disclosed “to avoid problems.”

Moreover, he continued, that money “could be used to keep building better hospitals,” referring to the Rosales National Hospital in San Salvador, which was renovated by the government. The project included construction of a modern tower for specialized consultations and outpatient treatment, inaugurated in June.

Economist Acevedo acknowledged that those resources could be used to address social needs, although he noted that the impact of the operation in Haiti on public finances could be relatively small compared with the country’s fiscal obligations and longstanding social deficiencies accumulated over decades.

The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) project that El Salvador’s economy will grow by 4.5% in 2026, compared with 3.9% in 2025. The World Bank attributes this momentum to consumption and investment, particularly in construction, amid increased business confidence resulting from reduced crime.

However, the IMF recommends protecting priority social spending to continue reducing poverty.

In this regard, Acevedo called on the Salvadoran government to adopt a more active policy against extreme poverty, with targeted programs that complement economic growth and job creation.

The government should adopt a policy of “zero tolerance for extreme poverty,” he argued.

Acevedo viewed favorably the earlier participation of Salvadoran aviation technicians in the United Nations-backed mission and initially supported the recent troop deployment. However, he fears that the intervention could drag on and lead to more deaths.

“I’m very skeptical of military adventures,” he said. In Haiti’s case, he acknowledged, “I’m really afraid this could turn into a quagmire, that we’ll end up bringing home four, five, twenty, or fifty bodies, and that the situation will escalate.”

A police officer keeps watch over inmates packed into a cell in El Salvador. President Nayib Bukele maintains that he can subdue Haitian gangs just as he did in his own country, while analysts question the risks and the economic cost of this military-led approach. Edgardo Ayala / IPS

A Different Kind of Combat

The Salvadoran military deployment in Haiti requires “a ton of money,” former guerrilla commander Pablo Parada told IPS. Known as Goyo during El Salvador’s civil war, Parada fought in the conflict between the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front (FMLN) and the army under right-wing governments from 1980 to 1992.

Following the Peace Accords signed in 1992, the FMLN became a political party and went on to win two consecutive presidential terms, from 2009 to 2019.

According to Parada, if the objective is to recover the missing soldiers, whether alive or dead, the government should first have relied on intelligence operations and explored the possibility of negotiating with their captors.

That would mean coordinating with more experienced agencies if El Salvador’s own capabilities proved insufficient, and establishing possible channels for negotiation, he explained.

The former commander, now a lawyer, warned that an armed confrontation could result in the deaths of people who possess information about the missing soldiers’ whereabouts, making it harder to locate them.

In his view, an impulsive reaction accompanied by threats of retaliation, such as those made by the Salvadoran president, could jeopardize both the safety of the deployed troops and the objective of recovering their comrades.

“When you react that way, it’s very dangerous because you put many things at risk, including the lives of the newly arrived troops,” he said.

Parada also questioned the Salvadoran army’s readiness to confront Haiti’s armed groups, despite Bukele’s assertion that his hardline methods could also crush them.

It is known that, under the state of emergency, Salvadoran gangs simply fled en masse without putting up resistance against the army. There were no major battles as such.

“I can state categorically that our army is not prepared for the urban combat it would face in Haiti,” Parada emphasized.

So far, the Haitian press has reported clashes in Santo and Croix-des-Missions, with several gang members reportedly killed.

Knowledge of the terrain, the experience of commanding officers, and soldiers’ ability to advance, protect themselves, and assist their comrades are all factors that, according to Parada, determine the chances of success in an urban combat operation.

Other important factors include available weapons and support, as well as an understanding of the historical and cultural conditions of the place where the intervention takes place, he added.

“Whoever knows the terrain will always have the advantage,” he said.

Parada recalled that before the November 1989 guerrilla offensive in the urban areas of San Salvador, in which he participated, the rebel forces, composed mainly of peasants, spent three months scouting the locations where they would operate.

They also had local guides and had identified routes for moving around and evacuating in an emergency, he said.

The former commander believes the deployment in Haiti has a strong propaganda component, “in the style of what we’ve had in this country for about seven years,” referring to Bukele’s rise to power in June 2019.

Similarly, economist Acevedo argued that the Salvadoran president is also seeking to demonstrate to the world that his hardline model can bring Haiti’s gangs under control.

“I think he wants to teach the world a lesson, showing that even Haiti’s powerful gangs can indeed be subdued by the power of the state,” he stressed.

Acevedo described Bukele as a president “obsessed with his image” and argued that his taste for media spectacles entails expenditures that could otherwise be directed toward social needs.

“I think the president is quite narcissistic,” the economist concluded.

First published in Spanish by IPS and translated and posted in English by Havana Times.

Read more feature articles here on Havana Times.

World.content:
View From Inside the Taxi, Havana, Cuba. By: Andrew Cannon (Canada). Camera: iPhone13
