World.title: Saudi environmental security forces arrest citizen for illegal hunting at wildlife reserve
World.content:
RIYADH: The Special Forces for Environmental Security arrested a Saudi citizen for violating the Environment Law by hunting without a license in Imam Turki bin Abdullah Royal Reserve.

The individual was found in possession of an air rifle and four, hunted, wild animals.

Legal procedures were taken against him.

The SFES stressed the importance of complying with the Environment Law and its implementing regulations, which prohibit illegal wildlife hunting.

It noted that hunting without a license carries a fine of SR10,000, hunting in prohibited areas carries a fine of SR5,000, and hunting a warbler without a license carries a fine of SR5,000.

The SFES urged the public to report any environmental or wildlife violations by calling 911 in Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Region, or 999 and 996 in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s other regions.

All reports will be treated with complete confidentiality, and informants will bear no liability.

World.title: Chelsea frustrated by Hacken in women’s Champions League, Man City win
World.content:
PARIS, France: Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women’s Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned a first win of the competition.

The London club hit the woodwork twice in Sweden as an inspired showing by Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk also helped keep the visitors at bay.

Chelsea are third in the league phase table after four matches, one point behind defending champions and pacesetters Barcelona, although the perfect Catalans hold a game in hand.

However, several teams, including Lyon and Arsenal — both of whom are just a point behind Sonia Bompastor’s side — could leapfrog them this matchday.

“It’s a frustrating result,” Blues boss Bompastor told UEFA.

“We came here with the ambition of winning the game... But tonight it didn’t go that way. We need to learn from this.”

Women’s Super League champions Man City enjoyed a 4-1 success at Inter Milan to earn a first win in the league phase after drawing their first three outings.

A first-half Aoba Fujino brace canceled out Elisa Bartoli’s opener for the hosts by half-time.

Kerstin Casparij and Grace Clinton were on target after the break to send City up to seventh in the table.

Paris Saint-Germain fell to a first defeat as Bayern Munich held on to win 2-1 at the Parc des Princes and climb to second in the table, ahead of Chelsea on goal difference.

Klara Buehl’s strike five minutes from half-time proved the winner as she added to PSG goalkeeper Katarzyna Kiedrzynek’s early own goal to put the Bavarians in a comfortable position.

Paulina Dudek halved the deficit from the spot midway through the second period but Bayern held on.

PSG lie in ninth place on five points.

In the Spanish capital, Real Madrid downed visitors Paris FC 3-0 thanks to three second-half strikes.

A first win of the league phase sent Pau Quesada’s side eighth in the table on six points, while Paris FC lounge 16th on two points.

Arianna Caruso broke the deadlock in the 55th minute and Lineth Beerensteyn thumped home soon after.

Linda Caicedo made the points safe with nine minutes remaining as she finished smartly from Felicia Schroeder’s reverse pass.

“It was really important to pick up the three points today because we hadn’t won any of our first three games,” Caruso said. “We have to try to finish among the top teams.”

Roma held on to beat Swiss side Servette 2-1.

On Wednesday, eight-time winners Lyon are in action away to Juventus.

World.title: US Republicans derail bid to impeach Pentagon chief
World.content:
Washington, United States: Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party’s crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote Wednesday on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.

The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to US media.

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Trump’s troubles after Democrats swept last week’s midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.

Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.

Trump hailed the procedural defeat as an “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot,” in a post on Truth Social, while Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, called the vote as a “TOTAL VICTORY!”

“We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest,” Parnell added.

Hegseth earlier Tuesday dismissed the impeachment effort as a “farce” and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Trump.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations “slander” and “sabotage.”

Moments after Hegseth’s televised appearance, Trump signaled his support.

“Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Vice President JD Vance also backed the defense secretary, saying he had “obviously not” committed impeachable offenses.

‘Would do it again’

Massie’s eight articles of impeachment accused Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

Several related to the eight-month Iran war, accusing him of violating the War Powers Resolution, which places limits on US military interventions without congressional authorization.

Other allegations involved the 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which Massie branded “extrajudicial killings.”

He also accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video urging military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.

Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers, while seeking to equate the impeachment effort with an attack on US troops.

“I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said.

The decision to send the resolution to committee halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January.

Massie, who lost his Republican primary to a Trump-backed challenger, will leave Congress at the end of his term.

World.title: US calls for new Europe security at Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
World.content:
ABU DHABI: Washington called for a “new” security framework on the first day of US-led talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was “happy” with the changes in approach by US mediators.

US leader Donald Trump’s envoys — his son-in-law Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff — brought together the warring sides for several hours of negotiations that are set to continue Wednesday.

Kushner told delegates the United States had “narrowed the gaps” between the sides — without providing details — and hoped to move toward a “solution” to Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.

In Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hailed the talks as “very productive” and called for Europeans to be eventually included at the negotiating table “because they are part of solving this problem.”

Ukraine’s Zelensky later said the talks were “constructive and quite substantive,” saying his team reported to him that humanitarian issues and security guarantees were among the topics discussed.

Speaking in Copenhagen, the Ukrainian president also said it was “time” for Europe to choose a representative for the talks.

Zelensky said negotiators in Abu Dhabi were working on a “large-scale exchange of prisoners,” adding that US officials would travel to Russia to discuss it further.

‘I see changes’

Asked about changes in the approach to peace talks by Kushner and Witkoff, Zelensky said: “I see changes. I’m very happy with what I hear.”

Europe has been rattled as Trump has floated a deal with Russia on rewriting Europe’s post-war security, also worrying that Washington will force Kyiv to accept a de facto defeat.

Kushner said the United States hoped to “create a new framework” of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that will secure “decades, if not centuries, of peace.”

Moscow, which several weeks before invading Ukraine issued an ultimatum to Western countries to roll back troops from eastern Europe, had also said this was a priority.

Ukraine has warned against a “Yalta 2.0,” referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union after World War II, and the EU has said security arrangements can only be discussed after a ceasefire.

“Putin wants the USSR back,” Zelensky told Danish media.

Russia, which occupies swathes of its smaller neighbor, pummelled Ukraine with more attacks overnight, cutting power to thousands as temperatures plummet.

Putin has repeatedly turned down broader ceasefire offers and vowed his troops will press on in Ukraine.

Moscow pushes security review

In a sign it is serious about reviving its demand to review Europe’s decades-old security arrangement, Russia included a diplomat — Sergei Ryabkov — who logged Moscow’s pre-invasion demand for NATO to pull back from eastern Europe.

A Russian delegation source had said that settling the war was “merely one item on the agenda,” and that Moscow’s main objective was reviewing security “for the entire continent.”

Kyiv’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov met the US envoys and European, EU and NATO officials before the negotiations.

The top US and NATO general in Europe, Alexus Grynkewich, is also taking part.

In a joint statement, the Europeans, Ukraine, United States and NATO reaffirmed their “shared commitment to a strong post-war European security architecture.”

Ukraine pushes for truces

Umerov said Kyiv’s priorities remained securing a ceasefire and security guarantees. “Our people are waiting to end this war,” he said.

As talks continued, Ukrainian and French foreign ministers in Paris commended US efforts to push for “partial truces,” which could serve as a “first step toward a complete and unconditional ceasefire.”

Last month, a local truce in Ukraine’s Kherson region brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump became the longest pause in fighting during the war.

Kyiv is also pushing post-war support for its army.

A senior Ukrainian source told AFP Ukraine wanted at least 10 years of financial support to sustain an 800,000-strong army able to defend any future Russian attack.

Land issue

There is huge distrust in Ukraine toward Trump’s aims.

The US leader hinted before the talks that Kyiv might have to give up land, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape.”

Russia’s troops have ground westwards but have not been able to seize the whole of the coveted Donetsk region, and Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the embattled area it controls.

“Allowing Russia to decide the borders of Europe will be a huge mistake,” Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen said, as she hosted Zelensky Tuesday.

Russia continues to pound Ukraine and its energy network, raising fears of another winter without heating, running water or electricity for millions of Ukrainians.

On Tuesday, Russian strikes killed four people in Ukraine, according to local authorities.

World.title: House Democrats to investigate Trump’s handling of US spy agencies
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Democrats in the US ​House of Representatives, who will control key committees next year, are preparing investigations into what they say was President Donald Trump’s politicization and gutting of US spy agencies, including whether analysts have censored themselves to avoid retaliation.

“There’s absolutely evidence that analysts are hesitant to write on topics that they think might be controversial. There’s absolutely evidence of a decline in morale in the analytic community because of the pressures that they are under,” US Representative Jim Himes, a Connecticut Democrat who will become chairman of the House intelligence committee in January, told Reuters on Tuesday.

There has been little scrutiny of the state ‌of the US intelligence ‌community by the Republican-run Congress during the first two years of ​Trump’s ‌second ⁠term, ​during which ⁠the administration fired or forced out hundreds of officers and disrupted the production of analyzes on key issues, including Iran.

Himes said that would change after he takes over the committee in January, when Democrats assume control of the House of Representatives and the Senate following their sweep of the November 3 midterm elections.

He did not disclose how the investigations would proceed, but said that one focus would be what he called retaliatory firings.

“We’re going to tell the story of the patriots who were fired because they said something that ⁠was inconsistent with what the president wanted to be true,” Himes said.

Former ‌Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard last year cut her ‌agency’s staff by about 40 percent.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe publicly pledged ​to reduce his workforce by more than 1,000 ‌positions over several years. Both offered deferred-resignation programs that provided pay and benefits for employees who ‌chose to leave.

The cuts included the firings of longtime intelligence analysts and officers from top posts, including at the National Intelligence Council, the analytical group overseen by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

At least two of those fired were analysts involved in an assessment that contradicted the White House’s official policy on Venezuela.

The reductions have ‌been viewed inside the intelligence agencies as a continuation of Trump’s campaign against what he called the “deep state,” a move critics say has drained ⁠the community of experience ⁠and expertise.

Reuters previously reported that some of Gabbard’s projects affiliated with her Director’s Initiative Group, a task force that revisited the 2020 election and the origins of COVID-19, created tensions inside the intelligence community.

Breakdown in intelligence sharing

That was particularly the case after Gabbard’s office revoked the security clearances of current and former intelligence officials a year ago.

Gabbard’s actions caused a breakdown in intelligence sharing and cooperation inside the intelligence community and with Congress, as Reuters previously reported.

“The moment the intelligence community stops telling the truth to national leaders, you get into an Iraq war because of weapons of mass destruction that don’t exist,” Himes said.

Himes said he had reviewed a statutorily mandated intelligence community survey showing that, in 2025, the workforce had begun to “feel very real political pressure.”

He added he was working to ​declassify other internal intelligence community reporting that could ​potentially underscore the effects of the firings and politicization.

The committee, Himes said, will also probe the administration’s relationships with defense and intelligence contractors and US covert efforts overseas.

World.title: Pegula keeps WTA Finals hopes alive, Kostyuk eliminated
World.content:
INDIAN WELLS, California: ‌Jessica Pegula kept her hopes alive of reaching the semifinals of the WTA Finals with ​a 6-2 7-5 victory over Marta Kostyuk on Tuesday, as Group 1 action continued at the season-ending tournament.

The American, who lost her opening match to compatriot Coco Gauff in three sets, responded with a composed performance to eliminate ‌Kostyuk, who ‌was a late addition ​to ‌the ⁠draw ​after replacing ⁠world number one Elena Rybakina following the Kazakh’s withdrawal through illness.

Pegula made an immediate statement, breaking Kostyuk in the opening game before securing another break to take the first set comfortably. She ⁠carried that momentum into the second, ‌breaking again in ‌the opening game, but ​the Ukrainian fought ‌back as the pair exchanged breaks twice ‌to remain level.

Kostyuk’s resistance ultimately faltered, with Pegula finding another break late in the set before serving out the match.

The victory marked ‌a turnaround for Pegula, following her opening defeat, and a particularly ⁠disappointing ⁠result for Kostyuk, who was eliminated from semifinal contention.

The world number 10 faced Pegula on a five-match losing streak and had been struggling with a right wrist injury that had troubled her since the hard-court swing.

Kostyuk had also beaten Pegula in both of their previous meetings this year, in Brisbane and ​Madrid, but ​was unable to reproduce that form.

World.title: Controversial French writer Houellebecq probed over comments on Muslims
World.content:
PARIS: Controversial French writer Michel Houellebecq was placed under formal investigation on Tuesday on suspicion of complicity in incitement to discrimination, hatred or violence, a source close to the case told AFP.

Houellebecq, 70, is arguably France’s most famous writer internationally, but has grown increasingly controversial as his pessimistic views on the decline of Western civilization are seen as aligning with the ascendant far-right.

The investigation concerns comments about Muslims published in 2022 in Front Populaire magazine.

In the interview with philosopher Michel Onfray, the author of “Submission” described Muslims as a threat to the security of French people.

“What the native French population, as they say, wants is not for Muslims to assimilate but for them to stop stealing from and attacking them,” Houellebecq said. “Or, alternatively, that they leave.”

He also warned of future “Bataclans in reverse” targeting Muslims, a reference to the jihadist attacks in Paris on November 13, 2015.

In 2023, the Union of Mosques of France (UMF) filed a complaint against Houellebecq, Onfray and Front Populaire director Stephane Simon.

In a statement to AFP, the writer’s lawyers said Houellebecq’s statements contained no element of incitement.

“A prophet of doom does not wish for misfortune to occur, quite the contrary. His place is not in a courtroom,” Thibault de Montbrial and Louis Cailliez said.

“Michel Houellebecq can only regret the growing tendency to litigate intellectual debate.”

In his memoir “A Few Months in My Life: October 2022-March 2023,” Houellebecq described his remarks as clumsy, saying he had been the victim of his own stupidity or naivety, as well as of the greed of those who sought to exploit his notoriety.

“Freedom of expression is fundamental, but it cannot justify everything,” Najwa El Haite, a lawyer for the Union of Mosques of France, told AFP.

“When it is established, incitement to hatred does not fall within the realm of intellectual debate. It is now for the courts to assess the matter, while respecting the presumption of innocence.”

The Grand Mosque of Paris had also considered legal action against Houellebecq, but later decided not to pursue it after meeting him.

Houellebecq made his name dissecting touchy subjects — including sex, race and religion — with dark irony and clinical detachment.

World.title: Restored Lebanon-Syria border crossing could handle 10,000 travelers a day, officials say
World.content:
LONDON: A key border crossing between northern Lebanon and Syria reopened on Monday after two years closed, restoring a vital trade and travel route that officials said could eventually handle up to 10,000 travelers a day.

The Abboudieh-Dabbousieh crossing, linking the Akkar region of Lebanon with Homs province in Syria, had been closed since it was damaged by an Israeli airstrike in November 2024 during the war between Israel and Hezbollah.

Passenger and commercial traffic has now resumed following extensive repairs, including reconstruction of the bridge connecting the two countries, said Mazen Alloush, director of relations and international cooperation at Syria’s General Authority of Borders and Customs.

Speaking on Tuesday, Alloush said the crossing will be able to accommodate between 8,000 and 10,000 travelers and 150 to 250 freight trucks each day when fully operational, the state-run Syrian Arab News Agency reported.

The reopening was expected to ease pressure on the Masnaa Border Crossing in Lebanon’s eastern Bekaa Valley, known as Jdeidet Yabous on the Syrian side. It has handled most of the land traffic between the countries while the two crossings to the north, Abboudieh-Dabbousieh and Arida, have been closed. Arida, which connects Lebanon’s Akkar with Syria’s coastal Tartous province, is expected to reopen in December after rehabilitation work.

The reopened Abboudieh-Dabbousieh crossing offers businesses in northern Lebanon, an area long dogged by underinvestment, the prospect of renewed trade as it restores a direct link between the region, including the Port of Tripoli, and Syrian industrial facilities in Hassia and the Port of Tartous.

It comes as the countries seek to reset a relationship shaped by decades of Syrian intervention in Lebanon. Syrian troops entered the country in 1976 and remained there until 2005, a period during which the Assad regime in Syria was accused of involvement in political assassinations.

When Israeli attacks damaged the crossing in November 2024, Bashar Assad, a key Hezbollah ally, was still the president of Syria, and border routes served as conduits for weapons bound for the group in Lebanon. Assad fled to Russia the following month as a rebel offensive swept through Damascus, and the new authorities in Syria have sought closer ties with Lebanon.

World.title: Iraq, BP discusses increasing oil industry investments
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and officials from British Petroleum (BP) met on Tuesday in London to discuss prospects for a strategic partnership between Iraq and the British firm.

The two sides discussed strategies to increase investments in the energy sector, serve mutual interests, and support the Iraqi economy, according to a statement released by al-Mandalawi’s media office.

The meeting addressed plans to broaden the scope of oil and gas exploration across Iraq, employ modern technologies for development, and create a promising investment climate.

BP is developing four oilfields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, a move that aligns with larger attempts to broaden the base of foreign partners.

The development plan intends to achieve a significant increase in oil and gas output in the next few years.

According to Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, the plan aims to reach an oil production level of 450,000 barrels per day, in addition to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.

The four oilfields—Kirkuk, Bai Hassan, Jambur, and Khabbaz—are key oil assets in northern Iraq and represent an important part of the government’s plans to increase production.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company to develop the oil fields, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

Khudair affirmed that BP is a strategic partner in the oil and gas sectors. He noted that working together as a team will support the project’s implementation and help address any obstacles that may arise during the development phases.

World.title: Police search Ritz, glitzy French Al-Fayed properties in trafficking probe
World.content:
Paris – French police have advanced an investigation into a vast alleged international network trafficking women for Mohamed Al-Fayed, prosecutors told AFP Tuesday, searching luxury properties linked to the late billionaire, including the Ritz hotel.

The Paris prosecutor’s office said authorities had searched the famed five-star Paris hotel, the former royal residence Villa Windsor and the Castel Sainte-Therese in Saint-Tropez, one of the most exclusive villas on the French Riviera.

Prosecutors said individuals had been held for questioning and authorities were analysing computers, phones and other digital media in operations that represent a development in a probe launched in 2025 to track down accomplices of Fayed and his late brother, Salah Al-Fayed.

Mohamed Al-Fayed, who died aged 94 in 2023, is at the heart of a vast sexual abuse scandal in the United Kingdom, but died with no charges brought against him despite multiple complaints.

The Ritz was just one of the Egyptian-born tycoon’s high-end ventures where victims have said they faced abuse. Others include London department store Harrods, Fulham Football Club and a fleet of private jets.

Victims have also alleged abuse at the Villa Windsor in western Paris, the one-time residence of the Duke and Duchess of Windsor — the former British King Edward VIII and his American wife Wallis Simpson.

The property was reportedly planned as the residence of Mohamed Al-Fayed’s son Dodi and his girlfriend Princess Diana, before their deaths in a Paris car crash in 1997.

– ‘Courage to speak out’ –

In 2025 Paris prosecutors opened an investigation into claims of aggravated human trafficking, procuring prostitutes and rape in a bid to track down accomplices in an alleged international network supplying victims to Mohamed Al-Fayed and his brother.

French investigators have already heard from at least five complainants — the latest in October, sources close to the case told AFP, with some hesitating to come forward due to trauma or fear.

“Every month, new victims from around the world overcome their fears and find the courage to speak out about what they endured,” lawyers Eva Joly, Caroline Joly and Agathe Barril, who represent several complainants, told AFP in a joint statement.

“We are, however, only halfway through the investigations,” they added.

“But the testimony already points to an organisation in which their immense personal wealth and business empire were allegedly mobilised in the service of their sexual predation: a mechanism devised with cold calculation and meticulous care.”

– ‘Highly organised’ –

Complainants have told investigators of a system aimed at recruiting young women hoping for a career at Harrods, or as assistants, coupled with invasive gynaecological examinations, leading to made-up jobs that put them at the disposal of the Al-Fayed brothers.

Some told AFP they believe they were drugged.

“Trafficking cannot be carried out without a highly organised group of individuals,” said one complainant, a former Ritz employee who was transported between France and Britain, speaking on condition of anonymity.

She praised the French investigation, but said London’s Metropolitan Police were still “beating around the bush”, 30 years after the first complaints.

In a letter to survivors on Tuesday, the Met said the investigation was one of the force’s “largest and most complex”, saying 169 victims have now come forward, and its officers are working closely with French authorities.

The London force has questioned seven people suspected of enabling Mohamed Al-Fayed, but none has been charged.

French and British investigators are now sharing information on the case and the prosecutor’s office said UK authorities were present during the recent operations in France.

The management of the Ritz told AFP it “does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour”, adding it was ready “to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities”.

World.title: Rubio sees ‘no need’ for major combat operations against Iran
World.content:
Paris – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because economic sanctions and other restrictions were working so effectively.

“The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations,” Rubio said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. “That’s what I told our allies here today.”

President Donald Trump “has concluded that for the time being there is no need for major combat operations because we are achieving the same objective by economic means,” Rubio said.

But if Iran were to cross “red lines” then the “US military stands ready”, said Rubio, warning of a “terrible price” for Tehran.

European members of the G7 had pressed Rubio at the meeting of foreign ministers of the group in Paris to avoid any new escalation against Iran.

In a surprise move, Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani joined talks on the G7 sidelines with four European top diplomats and the Saudi foreign minister hours after meeting Trump to discuss ending Washington’s war with Iran, Paris said.

Trump had said after meeting Al Thani — a key mediator who is also Qatar’s foreign minister — that there was momentum toward ending the war, which erupted on February 28 with the killing of supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

“The economic pain that is being inflicted on Iran right now and on that regime is extraordinary and it is growing every day,” said Rubio, saying Iranian oil supplies were drying up due to US blockades.

“This radical regime of lunatics is imposing this on their own people,” he said, referring to the Islamic republic’s clerical leadership.

– Downbeat on diplomacy –

But Rubio also appeared downbeat about the prospects of a deal with Tehran, saying Iran currently did not appear realistic about negotiations.

“Iran would love a deal. The problem is, the conditions they continue to place are absurd. They’re not even serious. But that could change,” he said.

But he added: “Eventually, you have to eat, you have pay your own fighters, your own security forces. I think as time goes on that will have an impact… Eventually economic realities penetrate the skull of the most radical lunatic”.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, who chaired the meeting in Paris, warned that the risk of a new escalation between the United States and Iran “has not been completely ruled out”.

“Otherwise, we would not have devoted so much time and energy over the past two days to addressing these issues” with Rubio and the Qatari premier, Barrot said.

British foreign minister Ed Miliband urged an “all-out diplomatic effort” to end the conflict, warning a stalemate of “no war, no peace” was causing economic damage.

“The status quo is bad economically for us and it’s not a stable equilibrium,” said Miliband, urging a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz energy transit hub.

World.title: G7 agrees on need to avoid ‘security void’ in Lebanon after UN force mandate ends
World.content:
Paris – G7 foreign ministers agreed on “the need to avoid a security void” in Lebanon after UN peacekeepers pull out, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday after a meeting of the group in Paris.

They also backed “the need to move quickly toward a new security architecture” after the mandate of United Nations peacekeeping forces in Israel’s neighbour expires at the end of the year, he said.

But Barrot acknowledged there had been no breakthrough on what should replace the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), which has been in place since 1978 and now counts some 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries.

Under US pressure, the UN Security Council voted last year to end UNIFIL’s mandate on December 31, 2026.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP in October that the bloc favoured a UN peacekeeping mandate in south Lebanon.

Lebanese militant group Hezbollah drew the country into the broader Middle East war by attacking Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.

“I am hopeful that we will reach a consensus,” said Barrot. “The objective is widely shared: the withdrawal of Israel (from southern Lebanon), the disarmament of Hezbollah (which is pro-Iranian), and the restoration of a strong state that holds a monopoly on the use of arms — a state capable of ensuring the security and prosperity of all the populations and all the communities in Lebanon.”

Israel now maintains troops in a self-declared “security zone” running around 10 kilometres (six miles) inside Lebanon along the border.

“We underscored the need for a robust, credible, and long-lasting security architecture in Lebanon in support of the Lebanese Armed Forces,” the ministers said in their final communique.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that he had discussed the issue with President Emmanuel Macron and suggested that what replaces UNIFIL “doesn’t have to be a military mission, it could be a civilian mission.”

“We need a verification system trusted by everyone and trusted by both sides that both sides are complying with their obligations under the agreements that are in place,” Rubio said.

A transitional mechanism utilising UNIFIL forces is among the options on the table, a European diplomat said, asking not to be named.

But this could require a UN Security Council resolution and thus run into an American veto, the diplomat warned.

The Europeans are also pushing a proposal for an international military coalition tasked with supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces in their mission to disarm Hezbollah.

However, the formation of such a coalition faces hesitation from Italy, which “remains strongly committed to its presence in Lebanon but appears reluctant to join an ad hoc coalition”, partly due to cost concerns, as such missions are not funded by the UN, diplomats said.

World.title: Iraqi FM participates in Paris Peace Forum
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein has arrived in the French capital to participate in the 9th annual Paris Peace Forum, where he will engage in discussions on key regional and international challenges.

Hussein said in a statement on Tuesday that he will exchange perspectives and explore approaches to de-escalate tensions and advance peace and stability.

The Iraqi foreign minister will present Iraq’s perspective on regional developments, emphasizing the importance of dialogue, diplomacy, and political solutions in addressing crises.

Hussein is expected to meet with international officials and partners to discuss strategies to strengthen cooperation, enhance coordination, and advance shared interests.

According to Hussein, Iraq will remain committed to constructive international efforts to promote regional stability, peace, and sustainable partnerships.

Participating as a featured speaker, Hussein addressed Iraq’s central role in mediating regional conflicts. He confirmed that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi recently conducted an unannounced visit to Tehran.

Al-Zaidi’s secret trip to Iran is part of Baghdad’s active diplomatic bridge to narrow differences, reduce escalating tensions, and work toward ending the ongoing conflict between Iran and the United States.

Hussein stressed that Iraq uses its good connections with the US and strong relationships with Iran to promote peace.

To reduce tension, Hussein had earlier suggested that a regional group of foreign ministers travel to both Washington and Tehran.

During his discussions at the forum, Hussein cautioned world leaders about the dire security and economic consequences of the conflict. He noted that the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz and regional unrest directly harm Iraq’s financial status and threaten worldwide energy, oil, and raw material markets.

World.title: Plane carrying Iran’s football team barred from landing in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq barred on Tuesday a plane carrying Iran’s national football team from landing at Basra International Airport, turning the aircraft back due to strict compliance with US sanctions on Iranian airlines.

The Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority (ICAA) denied landing rights to the flight carrying the Iranian team.

The aircraft successfully altered its course and landed at Abadan Airport in Iran. An official from the Iranian consulate confirmed that the team would continue their journey to Basra by road.

Along with Iraq, Lebanon, and Palestine, the Iranian national team was headed to Basra to participate in a four-nation competition.

Iraq could not risk violating the harsh secondary penalties imposed by Washington, according to an Iraqi civil aviation official.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned earlier that any foreign airports or service providers that assist sanctioned Iranian carriers will be excluded from the US currency system, a step aimed at grounding Iran’s civil fleet worldwide.

After Iraq previously secured a limited humanitarian exemption allowing specific civilian flights from Iran to Najaf, other major Iraqi airports in Basra, Erbil, and Baghdad remain restricted to avoid US financial penalties.

World.title: Excelerate Energy to launch Iraq’s first LNG import terminal in Q2 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is seeing rapid on-site progress, as efforts continue to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq.

Excelerate Energy, the US-based firm implementing the project, anticipates an increase in the pace of work in the upcoming weeks, with construction activities on terminal facilities set to ramp up.

The company aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the military conflict in the region have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026.

The delays forced Excelerate Energy to redirect its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), the Excelerate Acadia, to Jordan for a period of nine months.

To avoid disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed in the region, eliminating the need for such a vessel to transit the strait.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express, according to Attaqa news.

Excelerate Energy indicated that it is attempting to set up the import of LNG from Gulf countries, a remark that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: Iraq, Qatar to lay optical fiber cable linking Singapore to Italy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ooredoo Group’s international connectivity arm, OFN, has partnered with Iraq’s iQ Networks and the Iraqi Telecommunications and Post Company (ITPC) to build a massive terrestrial and subsea digital corridor connecting Asia, the Gulf, and Europe.

Ooredoo is developing a project that includes a 2,000-kilometer subsea system. This system will feature up to 24 fiber pairs and can support a capacity of up to 720 terabits per second.

The project will link seven Gulf and regional markets, which are Qatar, Iraq, Oman, the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait.

This dual-arrangement bridges the subsea Gulf network with an overland path heading north through Iraq toward Turkey and Europe, bypassing traditional maritime chokepoints like the Red Sea.

The fiber-optic connection that will bridge Singapore in East Asia to Italy in southern Europe is expected to be completed by 2027.

The Iraqi Ministry of Communications announced that it signed a deal with Qatar to establish the terrestrial and submarine fiber-optic connection.

World.title: 80% of Delhi's pollution Monday due to crackers
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Firecracker emissions accounted for more than 80% of Delhi's pollution load on Monday, a day after

, according to the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology's models, highlighting the sharp impact of fireworks on the capital's air quality.

The contribution came even as the city was already battling high pollution levels from multiple sources.

The situation, however, showed some improvement on Tuesday, with the AQI at 299 at 4pm, bringing it into the 'poor' category from 'very poor' a day earlier. However, it deteriorated to very poor by 6pm with an AQI of 302.

Toxins from Diwali firecrackers lingered on Tuesday as well, with IITM showing 29.9% of pollution contribution due to firecrackers between 1am and 9am, while secondary organic compounds - formed due to chemical reactions of emitted particles in air - were the secondary source at 17.5% of net pollution on Tuesday.

attributed cleaner air to favourable wind, which helped disperse pollutants accumulated over the city and barred intrusion of stubble smoke from neighbouring states.



Vehicular emissions third biggest source of pollution day after Diwali

The easing came despite a significant number of farm fires being reported in neighbouring Punjab. An assessment of the decision support system for air quality management indicated that stubble burning was not a major contributor to Delhiâs pollution load on Monday. This suggests that the immediate post-Diwali pollution spike was driven primarily by local fireworks rather than a major influx of crop-residue smoke.

The high contribution from firecrackers followed a sharp deterioration in air quality during the festival. Delhiâs average AQI was 376 on Diwali, Nov 8, the highest recorded for the festival in five years. It remained in the âvery poorâ category on Monday, with the city waking up to a thick layer of smog and several monitoring stations reporting severe air quality.

IITMâs model estimates the contribution of different sources to the cityâs particulate pollution a day after Diwali on Nov 9, including secondary organic compounds, at 5.8%, the second dominant source, and vehicular pollution at 4.4%, the third biggest source. World.title: For the first time, Sonia confirms battle with cancer in memoirs
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

's memoirs, released on Tuesday, officially acknowledge what was long whispered within political circles but never publicly confirmed - her battle with cancer, which occurred during the second term of UPA govt.

They also set the record straight on where her two surgeries took place - first at European Institute of Oncology, near Milan in Italy, and later at Erasmus University Medical Centre in Rotterdam - and not at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, as was widely speculated.

According to

, while she had suffered from occasional bouts of asthma and allergies, she had no serious health troubles until 2010, when she was advised to undergo surgery for suspected breast cancer.



She chose not to get operated on in India as she wanted to avoid a media frenzy.

âI saw

Rajiv

reaching out to me, smiling at meâ

After much discussion with her doctors, Sonia Gandhi opted to get operated on by Dr Veronesi, a celebrated surgeon who was the founder and head of the European Institute.

In her book, âBelonging: A Journey of Loveâ, Sonia writes, âOn the day of the surgery, as I was wheeled into the operation theatre,

and Priyanka held my hand and kissed me on the forehead, assuring me that all would be well.





Afterwards, still groggy from the anaesthesia, I saw Dr Veronesi with them by my bedside. How relieved I felt to hear him announce, âNon câÃ¨ niente da preoccuparsi, tutto Ã¨ andato bene e non ci sono residui. (No need to worry, everything has gone well and there are no residues).â He had removed two tumours, including a non-suspicious one to be on the safe side, and conducted an intra-operative radiation to spare me five weeks of radiotherapy.

â

However, a year later, routine follow-up tests detected a growth in the pancreas. This time Sonia was sent to Erasmus, to be treated by a well-known pancreatic surgeon, Dr Casper van Eijck. Again, Rahul and Priyanka were by her side before the surgery. When she woke up, dazed and parched, she heard them calling out, âMa, Mama, all is well â nothing bad!â The doctor later explained that fortunately, the tumour was found in a preliminary precancerous stage, having been detected early.

World.title: MEA slams US court summons to Doval, RAW ex-chief Goel
World.content:
New Delhi: Govt on Tuesday dismissed a US court civil summons naming national security adviser Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel as a "frivolous lawsuit" driven by "fabricated and malicious" claims, asserting that designated Khalistani terrorist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's legal maneuvering did not hold any merit, reports Rajshekhar Jha.

"...Requests for the service of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India's designated central authority, that is, the ministry of law and justice," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.

MEA's reaction came on reports of the US state department notifying India via a diplomatic note about a civil suit filed by SFJ member Pannun regarding an alleged plot to assassinate him.

Summons served by US court said to be âroutine, procedural stepâ

The summons naming Doval and Goel among the defendants seeks damages for an attempt on Pannunâs life and was delivered to the Indian embassy in Washington on Oct 9.



Sources described the move as a âroutine, procedural stepâ. They said this was not the first time such a summons had been served by US courts.

Former PM Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in 2013 in connection with a suit filed by the same outfit, SFJ, alleging human rights violations related to 1984. In 2013, a federal court in Washington DC had issued summons to Singh during his visit to Washington. Former Chinese President Jiang Zemin was also served a similar summons in 2002.

NEW DELHI: As many as 411 MBBS seats remained unallotted even after the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) conducted a special stray vacancy round, with the high fee structure in private medical colleges potentially being one of the factors behind the seats remaining unfilled. Of the 948 vacant MBBS seats included in the special round's seat matrix, only 537 were allotted, leaving 411 unfilled. World.title: Being underweight with high BP can be a problem too: Study
World.content:
Being underweight with high BP can be a problem too: Study

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

While obesity with hypertension is the most widely recognised high-risk category, a recent study has shown that being underweight with elevated blood pressure or hypertension may also be a high-risk sub-group in Asian populations.The study done in Japan and published in Hypertension Research, an open-source journal in the Nature group of journals, showed the combination of being underweight and having elevated blood pressure or hypertension was associated with increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events like heart attacks and strokes, particularly among women and among adults aged 40 and above. This is significant for India, where one in five men and women in the 15-49 age group is underweight (body mass index below 18.5)."Conventional prevention strategies for obesity with hypertension appropriately emphasise weight control and cardiometabolic risk reduction; however, the same approach may not be sufficient for underweight individuals with elevated BP or hypertension," stated the study, suggesting the need for additional assessment for unintentional weight loss, malnutrition, low muscle mass, frailty, and underlying chronic disease for those who are underweight with hypertension.Potential management strategies may, therefore, include nutritional assessment and support, resistance exercise or muscle-strengthening interventions where appropriate, and individualised BP control that considers frailty, and symptoms like dizziness or fainting when rising from sitting or lying down.The association between being underweight and cardiovascular events and mortality has been observed in previous studies but significance of high blood pressure was not as well studied or understood. This is of particular significance in Asia where being underweight is relatively common and the distribution of BMI is different from Western populations. In India, the latest National Family Health Survey of 2023-24 showed about 20% of men and women above 15 years had elevated blood pressure or were taking medicine to control it.Understanding cardiovascular risk across the full range of BMI, rather than focusing exclusively on obesity, is expected to enhance understanding of risk stratification in hypertension. The study used the nationwise claims and health-check database of Japan for the period Jan 2005 to Oct 2023 and analysed 62.6 lakh adults without prior cardiovascular disease, chronic renal failure, dialysis, or antihypertensive medication use.

World.title: Unesco: Women ahead in higher edu, but rural-urban gap hits schoolgirls
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has made substantial progress in closing the gender gap in education, with women now outpacing men in higher education. But a rural-urban divide continues to disadvantage girls at the school-completion stage.

A

report found that for every 100 boys completing upper secondary education in rural India, only 59 girls do so, compared with gender parity in urban areas. India has closed at least 65% of its initial disparity in upper secondary completion since 2000.

The 2026 Global Education Monitoring report, Gender Equity in Access to Education, puts India's overall gender parity index for upper secondary completion at 0.89, or 89 girls for every 100 boys.



In rural areas, it falls to 0.59.

Unesco categorises India as having made "fast progress" among countries with large disadvantages for girls at the start of the century. This applies to students completing school within the expected age window and those finishing late.

Recent govt data point to improvements in participation and retention. UDISE+ 2025-26 shows girls account for 48.4% of school enrolment. The secondary-stage dropout rate fell from 8.2% in 2024-25 to 7%, while retention rose from 47.2% to 51.9%.





These indicators cannot be directly compared with Unesco's household-survey-based completion ratios.

At college level, women lead men. AISHE 2023-24 puts the female gross enrolment ratio at 31.2%, against 28.9% for males. Women's enrolment rose from 1.57 crore in 2014-15 to 2.24 crore, a 42.2% increase. The higher education gender parity index stood at 1.08, with women's participation exceeding men's for seven consecutive years.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Unesco's review of Indian studies found free school lunches had nearly twice the impact on primary enrolment for girls as for boys in disadvantaged rural communities. Separate toilets helped raise enrolment among adolescent girls, while girls' clubs offering life skills and social support modestly improved secondary completion in

.

Globally, Unesco found parity in enrolment from pre-primary through upper secondary school. Women increasingly outnumber men in higher education, with 88 male students for every 100 women enrolled and 82 male graduates. Yet 273 million children and young people were out of education in 2024.

World.title: Person has no claim in grandpa's property held by dad, says SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Can a grandson claim a share in property inherited by his father from his grandfather?

has ruled that a person becomes the absolute owner of his share in his father's ancestral or self-acquired property and can deal with it exclusively, including excluding his sons.

Ending a 29-year legal battle, a bench of Justices Augustine George Masih and Sunita Agarwal rejected a son's plea for partition of his father's property. The son had filed the suit in 1997, claiming the property was ancestral or joint family property. The court said a son's son is not listed as a Class I heir under the Hindu Succession Act and cannot claim a share in his grandfather's property.

Referring to Section 8, which lays down succession rules when a Hindu male dies intestate, the bench said a son becomes the absolute owner of property inherited from his father, while his own son has no right by birth over it.



SC said Class I heirs inherit simultaneously, to the exclusion of all others. "A son's son is not mentioned as an heir under Class I of the Schedule, and, therefore, he could not get any right in the property of his grandfather," it said.

It added that 1956 law did not preserve right under personal Hindu law of a grandson to claim a share in his grandfather's property during his father's lifetime. Sec 8 must be read as a self-contained provision governing devolution of property of a Hindu male dying intestate, it said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Citing SC judgements, the bench rejected the argument that a son inheriting property under Section 8 holds it as karta of his undivided family. Such an interpretation would create two classes among Class I heirs, treating property as joint family property for male heirs but not female heirs, it said. The express wording of Sec 8 must prevail.

Upholding HC's order, the bench said a grandson cannot seek partition of property held by his father. The high court had ruled that when a son or daughter receives property through partition, whether ancestral or self-acquired, they become absolute owners of their shares and can deal with them exclusively, including excluding their sons.

World.title: U.S. Republicans derail bid to impeach Hegseth
World.content:
Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) blocked an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party's crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.

The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to U.S. media.

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Mr. Trump's troubles after Democrats swept last week's midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.

Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, hailed the vote as a "TOTAL VICTORY!"

"We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest."

Mr. Hegseth earlier on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the impeachment effort as a "farce" and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Mr. Trump.

"It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it," he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations "slander" and "sabotage."

Moments after Mr. Hegseth's televised appearance, Mr. Trump signalled his support.

"Pete Hegseth gets an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS," the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Vice-President J.D. Vance also backed the Defence Secretary, saying he had "obviously not" committed impeachable offenses.

'Would do it again'

Mr. Massie's eight articles of impeachment accused Mr. Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

Several related to the eight-month Iran war, accusing him of violating the War Powers Resolution, which places limits on U.S. military interventions without congressional authorisation.

Other allegations involved the 2025 conflict with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which Mr. Massie branded "extrajudicial killings."

He also accused Mr. Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video urging military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.

Mr. Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers, while seeking to equate the impeachment effort with an attack on U.S. troops.

"I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow," he said.

The decision to send the resolution to committee halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January.

Mr. Massie, who lost his Republican primary to a Trump-backed challenger, will leave Congress at the end of his term.

World.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy says he is pleased with messages from U.S. envoys on diplomatic efforts to end war
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said ​on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) he was very happy with messages he was getting from ‌the U.S. in terms of moving towards a resolution ​of the more than four-and-a-half-year-old war with Russia.

Mr. Zelenskyy ⁠was addressing journalists after a day of talks with Nordic leaders in Denmark, as a first day of U.S.-led trilateral discussions between Ukraine, Russia ‌and the U.S. wrapped up in Abu Dhabi.

“I see changes. I am very happy about what I hear,” Mr. Zelenskyy said when asked about the recent messages by U.S. presidential ‌envoys ⁠Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

Mr. Zelenskyy has been careful ⁠to smooth over what has often been a volatile relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump, particularly after a February 2025 Oval Office meeting during which Mr. Trump accused him ​of being ungrateful.

The talks ‌in Abu Dhabi are the first three-sided discussions to be held since February. Mr. Zelenskyy described the first day as constructive and substantive.

Later, in his latest comments to journalists, Mr. Zelenskyy said the ‌agenda of the talks in Abu Dhabi had included formulating ​a new security architecture for Europe, an idea raised earlier on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) by Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov.

Mr. Zelenskyy ⁠said the notion was “very difficult”.

“We are all very cautious with this topic because nobody really understands 100% what they want. I think ‌we understand, but nobody saw the documents, what the Americans discussed with the Russians,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.

He said the idea was first raised by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2021 and the administration of President Joe Biden at the time was cautious about it as the sequence of what had to be done first was ‌important.

“Everybody is ready for dialogue. First, stop the war in Ukraine. Second, ​security guarantees for Ukraine. Third, maybe some dialogue about the topic of security in Europe, in the world,” Mr. Zelenskyy ⁠said.

“This sequence is very, very important in this case.”

Earlier, Mr. Lavrov had said Moscow would not agree to an immediate ceasefire without knowing what would happen next.

He ‌said it would be wiser to discuss the outlines of the future security architecture in Europe first, and then a ceasefire ​in Ukraine.

World.title: U.S. Army member arrested in U.K. for alleged Russian links
World.content:
British authorities arrested a member of the U.S. Army on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) on allegations of spying for Russia. The 41 year old man, who has not been named, was arrested in Gloucestershire.

“The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing,” said Vicki Evans, a senior officer with U.K. Counterterrorism Policing.

The U.K. authorities said the investigation was not linked to other ongoing counterterrorism investigations.

“This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.

“While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message — this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners,” he added.

The soldier was based at Imjin Barracks, the headquarters of NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, as per a report in the BBC..

World.title: U.S. charges three ‘Iranian operatives’ over U.K. airbase plot
World.content:
The U.S. Justice Department on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) announced charges against three men it described as "Iranian operatives," including one already in jail, over their role in an alleged terrorist plot at Britain's RAF Fairford airbase.

Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at the base, which has been used by the U.S. military in its operations against Iran.

Police were called to the Fairford site in southwest England after a local farmer reported seeing a group of men with several white vans engaged in "suspicious" activity.

A U.S. charging document states that Al-Hassani, a 35-year-old Iraqi national, directed unnamed individuals to drive to the base in the vans, some of which contained barrels of fuel.

It claims that he earlier paid the group to buy metallic objects that could be used as shrapnel, and to disguise the vehicles as being engaged in fuel delivery services.

Al-Saadi, 32, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national already jailed in New York on terrorism charges, allegedly passed coded messages to Al-Hassani and Mohajeri, 48, an Iranian national, to coordinate ahead of the plot.

Days after the incident, the United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the base.

"Anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American servicemembers will be prosecuted by the United States government," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

The trio were charged in an eight-count indictment that alleges their involvement in several other plots in support of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and pro-Iranian group Kataeb Hezbollah.

Terrorist attacks

U.S. authorities first detailed charges in May against Al-Saadi, accusing him of directing and urging others to attack U.S. and Israeli interests, and to kill Americans and Jews, in retaliation for the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

He and associates were said to have planned, coordinated and claimed responsibility for at least 18 terrorist attacks in Europe, and two in Canada.

Examples included the non-fatal stabbing of two Jewish men in London in April, as well as several arson attacks on synagogues, Israeli businesses and Jewish schools in Amsterdam, Munich and elsewhere.

Al-Saadi has been in U.S. custody since May.

The latest indictment adds his apparent role in the RAF Fairford incident, as well as the alleged involvement of Al-Hassani and Mohajeri. Prosecutors did not disclose their whereabouts.

The three men are charged with conspiracy to provide material support to terrorist groups Kataeb Hezbollah and the IRGC, conspiring and providing material support for acts of terrorism, and conspiring to bomb a place of public use.

Al-Saadi is additionally charged with attempted acts of terrorism transcending national boundaries, and attempted destruction of property by means of fire or explosive.

U.K. police last month charged two British men with national security offences related to the RAF Fairford incident.

One was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be in Iran, and another with entering a prohibited place for a purpose "prejudicial" to the U.K.

Flight-tracking data showed on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that the U.S. military had removed at least a dozen aircraft from a second British airbase, RAF Mildenhall, following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran.

World.title: Bihar CM suspends 15 officers for negligence of duty
World.content:
Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) suspended 15 officers with immediate effect for negligence and failure to ensure the quality resolution of applications under the ‘Sahyog’ (Assistance) Programme.

The action has been taken and departmental proceedings have also been initiated against them for failing to process applications in a timely manner,

Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD), four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.

The officers include Block Development Officers (BDOs) and Circle Officers (COs), assistance engineers and junior engineers.

“All officers and personnel must extend their full cooperation in the processing of applications. It is our duty to address everyone’s problems with sensitivity and promptness, and to ensure they receive justice,” Mr. Choudhary said while holding the ‘State-Level Sahyog Programme at Chief Minister’s Secretariat where 76 applications were received.

He further said that the government’s objective is to ensure a transparent, fair, and time-bound resolution to every citizen’s grievance. The ‘Sahyog’ camps are intended to address public concerns and ensure citizen satisfaction.

Mr. Choudhary has directed all District Magistrates, departmental secretaries, and officials within the Chief Minister’s Secretariat to go beyond merely reviewing the timeliness of the resolution of applications received through the ‘Sahyog’ portal; they must also conduct a thorough review of the quality of these resolutions.

The initiative, which was launched for the first time by Mr. Choudhary, is part of the state government’s ‘Ease of Living’ under the ambitious ‘Saat Nischay-3’ programme aimed at delivering services at citizens’ doorsteps.

At the time of launching the initiative in May 19, 2026, it was already mentioned that if a case is not resolved within 30 days of receiving the application, suspension and disciplinary action will be taken against the responsible officers. These camps are organised on the first and third Tuesdays of every month to address complaints related to block offices, police stations, and revenue offices.

Mr. Choudhary instructed officials to ensure that the grievances of the general public are addressed with complete clarity and transparency.

“All officers and staff should extend their full cooperation in the processing and disposal of applications. It is our duty to address everyone’s concerns with sensitivity and promptness, and to ensure they receive justice,” Mr. Choudhary said.

Earlier in the day, Bihar CM also transferred ₹1,205.91 crore to the bank accounts of over 1.09 crore beneficiaries under social security pension scheme ahead of the Chhath festival.

The Chief Minister directed all concerned officials to launch a campaign to identify eligible individuals who are not yet covered by the social security pension scheme and to ensure they are enrolled and receive its benefits. He also mentioned that 136,854 new beneficiaries have been added to the scheme last month.

World.title: Bombay High Court refuses stage permission for Chhath Puja at Girgaon Chowpatty
World.content:
The Bombay High Court on Monday (November 9, 2026) refused Mithila Chhath Puja Sangh permission to construct a stage at Girgaon Chowpatty for Chhath Puja.

A Bench of Justices Advait Sethna and Ranjitsinha Bhonsale held that Article 25 places freedom of conscience and freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion within order, morality and health. The Bench said checks and balances under the Constitution must be followed.

The court heard the plea during vacation. The Sangh sought permission for two days to construct a stage at the beach for the festival. The police in September denied permission. The police cited an order of the High Court from 1998. The order, a document from proceedings in 1998, said Girgaon Chowpatty would host Ganeshotsav, Navratri Utsav, Ramlila, Krishnalila and Christmas, and no programme beyond those. The order set up a Monitoring Committee. The order made the Committee a party in any plea seeking permission for celebrations at Chowpatty areas in Mumbai.

The Bench noted that the plea did not make the Monitoring Committee a party and said that the plea did not justify the omission. The court said the petitioner did not place material to justify the omission. The court examined the mandate of Article 25. The court said freedom of religion carries limits under the Constitution. The court said the Constitution provides checks and balances and these must be followed.

The court said it would not pass orders at this stage. It listed the matter on reopening. It declined to direct a site for the event. It said the petitioner may pursue remedies in law. The court said it expresses no opinion on a site for the event. The court refused the plea to construct a stage at Chowpatty for Chhath Puja. The court said the petitioner may move the court on reopening.

Advocate Jogendra Thakur appeared for the petitioner. Advocates Bibhishan Sutar and Komal Punjabi represented the BMC. Assistant Government Pleader Gauri Sawant represented the State.

World.title: No proposal to allot Central Secretariat club premises to anyone: Centre tells Delhi High Court
World.content:
The Centre has informed the Delhi High Court that there is no proposal to allot the Central Secretariat Club premises to anyone at this stage.

The submission was made while the court was hearing an interim application filed by the club seeking a stay on the Centre’s decision to withdraw its recognition and the subsequent eviction order.

Taking note of the government’s submission, Justice Amit Mahajan said no interim directions were necessary at this stage. The court, however, permitted the club to remove its belongings from the premises within a week.

“Considering the above, no order is required to be passed. The petitioners are permitted to take away their belongings in next one week. List on the date already fixed, that is, December 21, 2026,” the court said.

The club, earlier known as Talkatora Club, has challenged the government’s decision to withdraw its recognition as well as an eviction order issued by the estate officer directing it to immediately vacate its premises in the President’s Estate.

The interim relief was sought against the July 14, 2026 de-recognition order and the July 17, 2026 eviction order. During the November 5 hearing, the Centre’s counsel informed the court that there was no proposal to allot the premises to any party at present.

According to the club, the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) arbitrarily, illegally and unconstitutionally withdrew its recognition on July 14.

The petitioner said that instead of taking corrective action on its complaints regarding irregularities during the term of the ad hoc committee managing its affairs, the authorities first withdrew the recognition in February without issuing any show cause notice.

It further contended, “the respondents are attempting to weaponise their own administrative failures and the misdeeds of their ad hoc committee to forcefully dispossess and extinguish a historic institution, in flagrant violation of Article 14 of the Constitution of India and the fundamental principles of natural justice”.

The plea alleged that the eviction order arbitrarily treated a historic 107-year-old institution, which was given permanent occupancy, as an “unauthorised occupant”, solely on the basis of the illegal cancellation of allotment.

World.title: Producers welcome proposal for minimum sustainable price for tea
World.content:
Observing that a committee of Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to implement minimum sustainable price for tea, several stakeholders of the tea industry on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) welcomed the proposal and said that such an initiative will help in increasing wages of tea garden workers and is essential for long term sustainability of the industry.

Representatives of different associations associated with the industry expressed apprehensions that with implementation of the Code on Wages, there will be a further increase in wage costs, and the financial viability of tea producers is likely to face additional challenges

“The tea industry is confronted with mounting cost pressures, while tea price realisations have remained relatively stagnant. A Minimum Sustainable Price framework is therefore essential to bridge the widening gap between production costs and market realisations and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the industry,” said C. K Dhanuka, Chairman, Dhunseri Tea and Industries. Mr. Dhanuka added that a minimum sustainable price will help bring realisations in line with costs, so that the industry can accommodate wage revisions, protect employment and the competitiveness of Indian tea.

The proposal of implementing minimum sustainable price for tea have been made to Ministry of Commerce, which is yet to take a decision on the proposal, the stakeholders of tea industry said.

Suneel Singh Sikand, chairman of Indian Tea Association (ITA) called the recommendation for a minimum sustainable price is an important policy intervention towards addressing the structural challenges confronting the Indian tea industry.

“Ensuring remunerative returns to producers is critical to sustaining operations, facilitating investment in re-plantation and productivity enhancement and securing the industry’s long-term sustainability,” Mr. Sikand said.

Hemanta Bangur, former president of ITA said that the industry has failed to uplift the workforce and something is fundamentally wrong with the industry as the balance sheet of most of the tea growers is in the red.

“The market is dysfunctional and there is no level playing field. If market forces are left to determine the fate of industry, it will bring about the demise of tea gardens,” he said.

The Tea Industry employs millions of workers in about 270 large tea gardens and hundreds of small tea gardens across the State. The daily wage for a tea garden worker in West Bengal is ₹250 per day.

Representatives of Indian Tea Association (ITA), Tea Association of India (TAI), United Planters’ Association of Southern India (UPASI), Confederation of Indian Small Tea Growers Associations (CISTA) and Federation of Indian Tea Manufacturers Association (FITMA) issued a press statement on the stagnation in the prices over the past several years

“Over the years, tea prices have registered a marginal compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 2–3%, as compared to an estimated CAGR of 10–14% in input costs. This growing disparity has affected producers’ ability to sustain operations, invest in re-plantation, improve productivity and maintain quality standards,” the press statement said.

Without divulging any details of the minimum sustainable price, the tea growers said that the proposed price band will cover only the cost of production.

“The proposed MSP framework also needs to account for the diverse economic realities of India’s tea-growing regions. Differences in agro-climatic conditions, production practices, productivity levels and operating costs influence the economics of tea cultivation across regions,” the press statement said.

The producers, however, did not specify what will be the impact of the minimum sustainable price on the price of tea in the retail market and on the consumers.

World.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs8 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs7 in another reduction
World.content:
The government on Tuesday slashed the price of petrol by Rs8 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs338 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs371 on Nov 11 (Wednesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

The government and Jamaat-i-Islami held another round of negotiations today to formulate a way forward on relief in petroleum prices.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.
